title: fix mode crashes on any coverage-incomplete report (scoreOf throws)
description:
fixer/fix.mjs calls scoreOf(baseline) unconditionally when it seeds the
hill-climb history:

  const history = [{ iteration: 0, outstanding: startIssues, score: scoreOf(baseline) }];

scoreOf -> reportSummary -> scoreReport, and aggregate/scorecard.mjs:117
throws on any report whose coverage.complete is not exactly true:

  "Refusing to score an atomic-coverage-incomplete report"

So fix mode dies with an unhandled throw on every partial report, and on
every report written before the atomic coverage contract existed (no
coverage field at all). The headless fix path is unusable against exactly
the reports that most need fixing.

Fix: make score optional in the history rows. Wrap scoreOf in a try, record
null on throw, and print "score N/A" as the surrounding code already
anticipates with `score ?? 'N/A'`.

Verify: run `node fixer/fix.mjs --findings <a report.json with no coverage
field> --target x --audit-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --dry-run` and confirm
it no longer throws.
close_reason: Landed to master at ead9c9e after independent review PASS by uplift-ds-flash

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW. Implemented by uplift-opus (opus), branch uplift/opus-aoo-audit, commit f7f44b4.

Root cause: fix.mjs seeded its hill-climb history with an unguarded scoreOf(baseline). scoreReport correctly refuses to score a coverage-incomplete report, so that refusal surfaced as an unhandled throw and killed the run. Two shapes hit it: a partial run (coverage.complete false) and any pre-contract report (no coverage field). Both reproduced before the fix, both at fix.mjs:178.

Change: reportSummary -> reportSummarySafe returning { scoreable, reason, summary }. Severity counts still come off findings (no coverage guarantee needed). Climb proceeds on outstanding findings and prints why the score is unavailable.

Non-obvious part worth reviewing: goal evaluation needed an explicit failed check rather than passing a null summary to evaluateGates. evaluateGates treats a null outcome as not-applicable and PASSES it. Verified an all-null summary against 'discoverable>=90, fast>=90, critical<=0' returns passed: true, so falling through would have let a partial run stop on a target it never measured.

Scope: deliberately narrow. Does NOT fix countOutstanding ignoring blocked/not-run, so a partial run can still print PASS on findings alone. That is web-uplift-cuv, which blocks on this.

Test: testFixSurvivesUnscoreableReports drives fix.mjs end to end with --max-iterations 0 (no agent, no browser). Asserts both shapes degrade, an unscoreable report cannot meet a score goal, a complete report still scores 88 and exits 0. No test previously exercised fixer/fix.mjs at all. Verified by reverting fix.mjs and confirming the test fails.

Gate: node tests/regression.mjs -> tests OK, exit 0. Needs review by a different model family before landing.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
REVIEW: PASS (reviewer: uplift-ds-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, independent of author uplift-opus)

Candidate reviewed: origin/uplift/opus-aoo-audit @ f7f44b4 in an isolated worktree
(/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/uplift-acl-review). Candidate left untouched; no diff vs f7f44b4.

WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not by reading the test, by running fix.mjs)

1. Bug is real. On the pre-fix file (extracted from cc91b07) both shapes die with an unhandled
   throw, exit 1:
     partial (coverage.complete=false): Error: Refusing to score an atomic-coverage-incomplete
       report (expected=58, recorded=58, ...) at scoreReport aggregate/scorecard.mjs:119
     legacy  (no coverage field):       same, (expected=unknown, ...)
2. Both shapes degrade cleanly post-fix. No stack trace, exit 1 on outstanding findings (correct),
   and all of: "Score unavailable: <reason>", "Climbing on outstanding findings; scores read N/A",
   "iteration 0: 9 outstanding, score N/A", "STOPPED with 9 outstanding issue(s)".
3. An unscoreable report cannot meet a score goal. Verified across every goal shape, on both
   partial and legacy: --goal-min discoverable=90 --goal-min fast=90 --goal-max-critical 0,
   --goal-overall 1, --goal-max-critical 0. All refused, all named "atomic coverage complete".
4. The new guard is LOAD-BEARING, proven adversarially. I called evaluateGates directly with an
   all-null summary against {min:{discoverable:90,fast:90}, maxCritical:0} and it returns
   passed:true, with every check reading N/A. I then neutered the guard to simulate the naive
   catch-and-continue fix and a partial report printed "PASS: score goal met." with exit 0.
   So the author's non-obvious finding is correct and the explicit failed check is necessary,
   not decoration.
5. The regression test genuinely covers the bug. I swapped the pre-fix fix.mjs into fixer/ and the
   suite failed with "fix: partial report crashed the hill-climb instead of degrading" (exit 1);
   restored, suite is green. Post-fix file restored byte-identical.
6. No regression on scoreable reports. examples/playground-report.json still scores 88, reports
   "goal ALREADY met", "PASS: score goal met.", exit 0, and no "Score unavailable".
7. node tests/regression.mjs -> tests OK, exit 0 (run four times, including after the swap/restore).
8. Scope is exactly the two claimed files. --dry-run and --help still exit 0.

Author claims spot-checked and all accurate: root cause at fix.mjs:178, the evaluateGates null
=> not-applicable => PASS behaviour at aggregate/scorecard.mjs:609, and "no test previously
exercised fixer/fix.mjs" (baseline regression.mjs has 0 references).

RISK THE MERGER MUST HANDLE (not a defect in this diff)

acl alone converts a loud failure into a SILENT FALSE PASS for one input class. A coverage-
incomplete report with zero non-excused findings now exits 0 and prints "PASS: no outstanding
issues remain.". Verified: coverage {expected:58, notRun:40}, findings [], zero scoreable
work => exit 0, PASS. Before this fix that same input crashed loudly. That is exactly SKILL.md's
"a partial run must not make a completion claim", and it is web-uplift-cuv's scope, which blocks
on this bead. The author documented the boundary honestly.
Recommendation: land acl and cuv as a PAIR, or land acl only with the PASS line additionally
guarded on coverage.complete. Landing acl alone opens a window where a partial run reports success.

NON-BLOCKING NOTES (no change required)

- Test strength: the goal assertion pairs --goal-min with --goal-overall 1. Because evaluateGates
  correctly null-checks overall (scorecard.mjs:604), the overall gate alone would also block a
  false PASS, so the test does not exercise the min-only shape that actually false-passes. The
  test still catches guard removal (it asserts the coverage reason appears). Worth adding a
  min-only/max-only goal case to pin the shape that motivated the guard.
- The catch in reportSummarySafe is broad, so an unintended TypeError inside scoreReport would be
  relabelled "unscoreable/coverage". Low impact: scoreReport has exactly one explicit throw (the
  coverage refusal at :119), and the message is still printed. Consider matching the refusal
  explicitly if you want the distinction preserved.
- reportSummarySafe recomputes scoreReport 2-3x per report (baselineScore, scoreOf(baseline),
  goalOf(baseline)). Cosmetic.

FILED FROM THIS REVIEW
web-uplift-rj2 (P2): fix mode still crashes on a structurally malformed report. countOutstanding
(fixer/fix.mjs:373) does report.principleOutcomes.filter unguarded, so a non-array
principleOutcomes throws "TypeError: outcomes.filter is not a function" at line 182, BEFORE the
new score safety net is reached. Different input class from acl's scope (structurally invalid,
not coverage-incomplete), so not a blocker: reported for a follow-up.

VERDICT: PASS. Recommend landing with cuv.

title: waitForPipeReady hangs indefinitely on pipe.send if Chrome does not answer on fd 4 (evidence/cdp.mjs:888)
description:
Reviewed web-uplift-j3re delta 02bdec3..bb63be1 (bb63be1).
Repro: node tests/regression.mjs --only testChromeSandboxPolicy
Observed: Command hangs until event loop empties, printing 'Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await at tests/regression.mjs:239' and exiting with code 13.
Expected: waitForPipeReady enforces deadlineMs and fails fast if browser does not answer on pipe or exits, without hanging unsettled promises.
Evidence: evidence/cdp.mjs:888; pipe.send('Browser.getVersion') is awaited without a timeout/race wrapper, leaving a pending promise unsettled indefinitely if fd 4 is silent or process exits.
Fix owner: web-uplift-mwg-drift
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
FIXED on fleet/pipe-default-fixes @ 5da2310 (commit a8a4f7d), pushed. in_review, not queued - cdp-pipe is held until coord's own verdict.

The P1: waitForPipeReady awaited pipe.send('Browser.getVersion') with nothing bounding it. The deadline was only consulted in the catch, so a promise that never settled never reached it, and the process-exit check at the top of the loop was unreachable for the same reason. A browser alive but silent on fd 4 suspended the audit forever. It now RACES the answer, the remaining budget and process exit; the losing promise is caught so it cannot surface as an unhandled rejection, and the timer and exit listener are removed before returning.

I also found and fixed a second defect in the same path, beyond the reported one: the failure branch read alive/exitCode/signal AFTER `await close()` and hardcoded stderrText to ''. close() signals the browser and waits for it to exit, so EVERY pipe failure reported alive=false and signal=SIGTERM with no stderr - erasing the alive-but-silent versus exited-early distinction that describeLaunchFailure exists to make and that the port path takes care to preserve. The snapshot is now taken before teardown and Chrome's stderr is captured, which also drains a stream nothing was reading.

Regression test: testSilentPipeReadinessIsBounded, registered in ALL_TESTS, using a fake Chrome that starts, stays alive and never writes a frame - the exact shape that hung. It requires the launch to fail inside its 400ms budget. Mutation-proven: removing the race makes it wait the fake child's full 30s lifetime instead of failing in 400ms.

Census updated with reasons: the bounded race is a new bounded:own-deadline site (3 -> 4), and the probe it replaced left an awaited line, so bounded:transitive-caller-wraps now matches 0. That rule is KEPT rather than deleted, because a bare await of that probe reappearing is still correctly a transitive-caller-wraps site.

title: [4rv P1] cdpEndpointExposure can certify an exposed endpoint as safe on an incomplete kernel read
description:
Static review finding on web-uplift-4rv (fleet/cdp-endpoint-guard @490fbe6), by reviewer subagent openai-codex/gpt-6-sol.

Evidence: evidence/cdp.mjs:490 readBoundListeners silently skips an unreadable /proc/net/tcp6 but still returns IPv4 listeners found. cdpEndpointExposure (:590) then returns verifiedBy 'the kernel binding' and never tries reachability when it sees only the IPv4 loopback listener, even though the same browser also owns a non-loopback IPv6 listener on that port.

Expected: an unreadable address-family table is an INCOMPLETE result, never a verified-safe binding. Treat it as unknown and fall through to reachability (or fail loud).
Fix owner: web-uplift-mwg-drift on branch fleet/cdp-endpoint-guard.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
FIXED on fleet/cdp-endpoint-guard @ 18751fb (commit 4 of the branch; the branch is queued for the merger through web-uplift-4rv, which stays the one merge-queue entry for this branch). Your finding was correct and I reproduced it without a browser before touching the code.

REPRODUCED (old code): readBoundListeners skipped a table it could not read - the `continue` even carried a comment calling it "no IPv6 table on a v4-only kernel, or unreadable in some sandboxes" - and returned the IPv4 listeners, so classifyBoundListeners saw 127.0.0.1 and cdpEndpointExposure returned {exposed:false, verifiedBy:'the kernel binding'} without probing. With the IPv4 half readable, /proc/net/tcp6 unreadable, and a non-loopback IPv6 address answering DevTools, that is a false all-clear for exactly the failure this check exists to catch. Measured on the real reader here: readBoundListeners(process.pid, {tcpFiles:['/proc/net/tcp','/proc/net/tcp6-not-on-this-host']}) silently returned only the IPv4 rows, with nothing in the return value to say a family was missing.

FIX: readBoundListeners now returns { listeners, unreadable } and names every table it could not read (a real missing path is listed, not swallowed). An unreadable address family is an INCOMPLETE result, never a verified binding: cdpEndpointExposure records the incompleteness, says in the note which family is unchecked, and falls through to reachability, which is what finds the invisible IPv6 listener. A null read, a thrown read, and a reader returning an unusable shape are all incomplete for the same reason. A COMPLETE loopback-only read is unchanged: verified by the kernel with no probe, no note, no unknown.

AFTER: with a complete read and a loopback-only bind, the verdict is still {exposed:false, verifiedBy:'the kernel binding'} with unknown undefined. With /proc/net/tcp6 unreadable and a non-loopback IPv6 host answering, the verdict is now {exposed:true, verifiedBy:'reachability', reason:'... on [IPv6]:9222'}. With an unreadable table and every reachable address refusing, it is {verifiedBy:'reachability'} plus a note naming the table, because reachability did decide every address.

TEST: tests/cdp-endpoint-exposure.mjs gained the finding's scenario (readable IPv4 loopback + unreadable tcp6 + an IPv6 host answering DevTools = exposure), the incomplete-read fall-through with its note, the complete-read control, and a real read with a missing /proc path. Mutation: restoring the pre-fix rule (a clean readable family verifies regardless of the unreadable one) fails the test with the original "verifiedBy: the kernel binding" verdict; restored byte-identically by md5.

SCOPE, stated plainly: on this VM there is no non-loopback IPv6 address to bind, so the browser half of the scenario is simulated through the injectable reader and connect this module already takes; the read half (a missing /proc table) is real. The predicate the fix changes - incomplete read must not verify - is exercised for real either way. The reviewer lane coord is arranging can drive the dynamic half in a scratch worktree.

Verified: tests/cdp-endpoint-exposure.mjs tests OK, tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs all 23 vendored copies identical, tests/flow.mjs tests OK, tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs tests OK. IN_REVIEW on the branch tip; coord is getting a reviewer lane for the dynamic verification.

P2 it raised: when classifyBoundListeners reports unknown because no listening socket for the ANNounced port was found, the code already could not claim kernel verification, but it did not set bindingIncomplete, so the reachability-only verdict lost the "the kernel binding was incomplete" clause. That is an incomplete binding answer - the endpoint was announced, so not seeing it means the read did not cover it. Fixed, and the test now pins the end-to-end verdict for that shape (both the per-port note and the incompleteness clause).
P3 it raised: with the whole binding read unreadable the note said "an address family is unchecked", understating it; it now says the socket bindings are unchecked.

It also independently confirmed the parts I claimed: the unreadable-table fall-through catches an IPv6 listener the binding read cannot see; verifiedBy is absent exactly when a probe was undecided; the twin remains byte-identical; no caller still expects the old array return; and a healthy launch is never refused by any of this (refusal needs exposed === true).

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW on fleet/mwg-catalog-parse @ 8e1cfa7 (merge-base origin/master = 7517ce2; 6 commits). Merge-queue label added.

REPRODUCED FIRST, and the bead's one-liner needed sharpening: the recipe's regex is `/var USE_CASES = (\[[\s\S]*?\n\];)/`, so it only matches a table whose closing bracket is on its own line - the bead's single-line printf produces a null match and the eval line throws before it writes anything. With a MULTI-LINE table containing a marker-writing element, the recipe's own extraction line writes the marker:
  BEFORE marker: RAN
The same class, faithfully reproduced. The fix is still exactly the right one.

FIX: the doc's inline recipe is gone. Extraction now lives in a committed generator, tests/mwg-catalog.mjs, whose USE_CASES reader is a strict DATA-ONLY literal parser: strings (single, double, template without interpolation), numbers (signs, fractions, exponents, separators, hex/octal/binary), booleans, null, arrays, objects, with comments and trailing commas tolerated because they cannot execute. A call, an operator, a bare identifier, `${...}`, or a prototype key is REFUSED by name. There is no eval, no Function and no module evaluator in the file, and the test suite asserts that. The same table that the recipe executed now fails closed:
  AFTER: "FAIL: refused to build the catalog: the USE_CASES table is not pure data: expected a literal, found "(" ..." / exit 1 / marker absent / no catalog written.

EQUIVALENCE, because a parser that is safe by dropping guides is a different bug: regenerating modern-web-guidance@0.0.193 from the REAL published tarball with the new parser produces a catalog identical to the committed one in EVERY field (all 178 guides, guideIds, guideIdsSha256, guideCount, retrievedAt). The real table turned out to use template literals (16 backticks, zero interpolations), which the parser accepts as data and refuses the moment one interpolates.

REVIEW: independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol; implementer deepseek-flash). Pass 1 on 3325ca7: REQUEST CHANGES, BLOCK - three findings plus a vacuous test, and one of them was a bug I had introduced in the refactor (the boolean/null arm referenced `table`, which is not in scope, so any table containing true/false/null died with a ReferenceError; the published table has none, so no fixture or real-package run could have found it). Also: `\x41` was silently flattened to "x41" (an altered description is worse than a refusal), field shapes were substituted or filtered instead of validated, and one of my assertions threw its own refusal so it passed either way. All four fixed. Escapes now decode exactly as JavaScript does (verified against eval of 13 authored literals in a throwaway script: \xNN, \uXXXX, \u{...} code points, undefined escapes, LF and CRLF line continuations, escaped backticks, multi-line templates - every value matches). Field shapes now REFUSE rather than default. Pass 2 on 8e1cfa7: VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues found. Its stated limitations: it reviewed the frozen artifacts I supplied rather than an independent checkout, and did not run the suite. Two further commits came from my own mutation sweep: refusing a 0-guide catalog, and making the twin-insertion order observable in the fixture (the twin had been the last table entry, so "inserted next to its twin" and "appended" were indistinguishable).

MUTATION-CHECKED (each guard broken in the committed worktree, suite expected to fail, then restored): interpolation refusal, prototype-key refusal, hex/unicode/code-point escape decoding, line continuation, description shape, featuresUsed member shape, tokenCount shape, sha construction, twin insertion, retrievedAt preservation, zero-guide refusal, trailing content, category slug, non-slug id, duplicate id, missing id, non-object entry - all caught. One honest exception, recorded in the test file rather than dressed up: the literal/identifier word-boundary check is defence in depth and not load-bearing (without it `trueish` is still refused, just with a different message).

ALSO: tests/regression.mjs's testMwgCatalogRegenerateAgreement used to compare the catalog's regenerate text against the markdown script by eval-ing a string out of the markdown; it now compares against the generator's exported REGENERATE constant (imported, not evaluated) and asserts the markdown carries no extraction script, so the old shape cannot come back. knowledge/mwg-state.json's catalogSha256 moved because the catalog's regenerate text changed; node tests/mwg-artefact.mjs update was run and verify passes (178 guides, unchanged guideIdsSha256/guideCount).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: the documented catalog-regeneration path no longer evaluates the downloaded modern-web-guidance package. tests/mwg-catalog.mjs (new) extracts the catalog with a strict data-only reader that decodes literals and refuses anything that is not one; knowledge/mwg-catalog.md's inline eval recipe is deleted, knowledge/mwg-catalog.json's regenerate field and docs/mwg-drift-check.md's reanalysis step point at the generator, and tests/mwg-catalog-extract.mjs (new, with fixtures) covers the refusals, the union/ordering output, byte-identical regeneration and a tripwire proving a table containing an expression is refused without being run.
WHY: knowledge/mwg-catalog.md evaluated its own unpacked package's USE_CASES array with eval() in the operator's Node process, on the path the drift runbook sends the reanalysis lane down - so a malicious or compromised release ran code in the operator's account.
EFFECT: regenerating the catalog is now safe to run against an untrusted release: a changed or hostile table fails with a named reason and a non-zero exit, the catalog it writes is byte-identical for the real 0.0.193 package, and the documented recipe can no longer drift from the code that implements it.

title: flow redaction: OAuth/API credential query keys 'code' and 'key' are never redacted (runner/flow-record.mjs:183; 5b8321c removed the matcher)
description:
Reviewed web-uplift-3if sweep, POST-LANDING (follow-up, not a block). Branch under review: origin/master @ f83372c.
Repro:
  node -e 'import("./runner/flow-record.mjs").then(m => console.log(m.sanitizeNavUrl("https://example.com/oauth/callback?code=AUTH_SECRET_CODE_12345")))'
  node -e 'import("./runner/flow-record.mjs").then(m => console.log(m.sanitizeNavUrl("https://api.example.com/x?key=AIza_REDACTED&q=1")))'
Observed: both URLs printed verbatim (https://example.com/oauth/callback?code=AUTH_SECRET_CODE_12345 and ...?key=AIza_REDACTED&q=1).
Expected: '?code=[redacted]' and '?key=[redacted]' - README.md:358-360 claims credential/PII-shaped fields and TOKENS are redacted from flow.json by default.
Cause: sanitizeNavUrl() redacts a query param only when hasSensitiveWord(k) || isSensitiveNavValue(v,k). 5b8321c REMOVED isSensitiveNavParam(), which matched lower==='code'/'auth_code'/'authcode'/'one_time_code'/'passcode'/'pin'/'otp' and lower==='key'/'api_key'/'apikey'/'*_key'/'secret_key'/'private_key' (see git show 5b8321c -- runner/flow-record.mjs). SENSITIVE_WORDS (runner/flow-record.mjs:34-47) deliberately omits bare 'code'/'key', and isSensitiveNavValue() only classifies emails/SSN/cards/phones. A 5b8321c round-2 review then edited flow-record.mjs without restoring it.
Impact: an OAuth authorization code or an API key in the query string is persisted unredacted into the recorded flow.json and replayed. Common (OAuth callbacks, ?key= maps/API flows).
Evidence: runner/flow-record.mjs:183 (searchParams loop), :34-47, :151-171; README.md:358-360; git show 5b8321c.
Fix owner: coord -> a flow lane (restore a bounded key list: exact 'code'/'key'/'auth_code'/'api_key', not substring, so postalCode/sortKey stay safe).

title: Recurring MWG reanalysis: detect upstream version delta and publish one versioned hash-pinned artefact for mwg-train
description:
PAUL'S ORDER (2026-10-08 13:43Z): modern web guidance is updating very frequently, so the MWG reanalysis must be a REGULAR (recurring) analysis, and its output must be consumable by mwg-train.

Deliverable 1 - the recurring job:
- A scheduled cheap check that reads the CURRENT upstream guide set and compares it to the last ANALYSED version. Full reanalysis runs only on a VERSION DELTA, not on a clock; the clock exists only so a silent upstream change is caught within a bounded time.
- A guard so a STALLED check is itself detectable - total absence of output must alert, not look like a quiet period.
- Delta classification with REVERSALS as their own class, first and loudest: NEW = gap, CHANGED = defect, REVERSED = an implemented rule is now wrong and is producing bad repairs elsewhere. Never list a reversal beside cosmetic changes. Severity by class, not by count.
- Sabotage-proven self-test: a known-reversed guide must report a REVERSAL, and unparseable or empty upstream must FAIL rather than report no-change. A diff job that cannot parse upstream and exits 0 is the same defect class as gendn's eight false greens.

Deliverable 2 - the consumable artefact (this constrains deliverable 1):
- ONE versioned artefact carrying the catalog, its FULL 64-char sha256, the canonicalisation rule, the upstream version analysed against, and the version of the APPLIED RULES. Do not collapse the last two: "behind upstream" and "our rules are wrong" are different states.
- NO live cross-VM coupling. No cross-VM call, no shared filesystem, no push through the hub. The artefact and its hash ARE the interface to mwg-train.
- mwg-train PINS the hash and FAILS CLOSED when it moves - pipeline stops, not a warning. The artefact must therefore change whenever the applied rules would change.

Depends on: cy8 (the 0.0.193 rule and test update) landing first, since the job must analyse against a correct ruleset. Related: 968 (the hash pin on the uplift side).

Note: the pin makes the floor VERIFIABLE, not CORRECT. mwg-train must not recompute the uplift floor until cy8 lands.

comments.text:
REVIEW ADDENDUM (mwg-drift, k3; full delta 0a58dc3..15bc2cb; new EVIDENCE.md sections 4-6). Verdict on the addendum: **2 defects + 1 misquote; the critical published-vs-proxy question resolves in OUR favour.**

A. SECTION 5 TABLE — baseline column VERIFIED against mwg-train src/corpus/rules.mjs (line 65: 'no aria-errormessage/aria-describedby linking the field to its error text'; line 114: 'after a failed interaction the error text is still not visible'; liveRegions/announced checks for the announcement rule; autofill/username and street-address/postal-code probes as tabled). Canonical column matches the branch's own artifacts (EVIDENCE.md item 6 native-validation rationale). ONE MISQUOTE: the accessible-error-announcement row claims the 0.0.193 guide 'requires an in-DOM live region (aria-live=polite)'. The guide makes live regions OPTIONAL ('consider adding role=alert or aria-live=polite ... but test thoroughly'); the MANDATORY parts are the aria-invalid JS bridge and the aria-errormessage-linked in-DOM error element. The row's conclusion stands; its cited requirement is wrong and should be corrected before the cut.

B. SECTION 4 SUPERSEDED SET — MIS-IDENTIFIED: 6 of the 20 enumerated 'Guide / Rule IDs' DO NOT EXIST in the 0.0.193 catalog (checked against knowledge/mwg-catalog.json guideIds): security/csp-direct-enforcement, security/csp-object-src-none, security/csp-frame-ancestors, visual-design/light-dark, privacy/storage-access-api, resilience/document-render-blocking (prevent-text-wrapping is legitimately absent, being the removal). The underlying guidance is real but lives under real catalog ids, verified in the 0.0.193 package: the CSP trio in the 'security' guide, light-dark() in visual-design/dark-mode.md + ui-atoms/component-specific-light-dark-theme.md, storage partitioning in privacy/privacy.md, render-blocking in performance/performance.md. For a document whose entire purpose is precise rule attribution the table must cite real catalog ids (or explicitly say 'rule within guide X'). Framing nit: 'from cy8' conflates upstream 2026-09-04-to-0.0.193 drift with cy8's own reanalysis; the hub asked for the set derived from cy8's diff, and only a subset of the 20 are in that diff (the rest are upstream version drift, which is still valid expected drift vs mwg-train's snapshot, but should be labelled as such).

C. CRITICAL DISTINCTION — the discrepancy is a PROXY-HARNESS-ONLY calibration bug, NOT a published-ruleset bug, and I can show why from primary sources:
  - Guide text (0.0.193, verified in the npm package): forms/required-field-feedback REQUIRES an author-provided in-DOM error container ('MANDATORY: Provide multiple indicators (border shift + helper text/icon) to avoid color-only state communication', linked via aria-errormessage); accessibility/accessible-error-announcement states native validation 'doesn't automatically synchronize with accessibility attributes' and requires the aria-invalid JS bridge plus the linked in-DOM error element.

A model-led audit applying our published ruleset + guides would flag the missing containers/bridge exactly as mwg-train's baseline did.
  - The PASS came solely from the proxy harness's hard-coded threshold in scripts/evaluate-targets.mjs ('native HTML5 constraint validation without novalidate bypass and without eager :invalid CSS rules passes cleanly') — precisely the deterministic decision the repo docs forbid.
  Conclusion: NO bug to file against the published instrument (principles.json + SKILL.md); the addendum's own attribution ('finding against web-uplift proxy benchmark harness calibration') is correct and folds into round-1 finding F1 (harness under hub ruling). Caveat on section 6: 'Impact on Floor' ('adjust downwards by 2 findings per target, aligning exactly with mwg-train') is speculative arithmetic, not a recomputation — label it as an estimate.

Round-1 findings F1 (harness/hub ruling), F2 (unrecorded review claim), F3 (scope) stand unchanged. Prior verdict holds: do not merge as-is; the addendum improves mpz compliance but needs the section-4 id corrections and the section-5 misquote fix.

Using the canonical catalog (C1) and the CURRENT knowledge/principles.json + tests, produce TWO SEPARATE reports: (a) GUIDES NOT COVERED - guides present in the current catalog with no corresponding principle/check/guide pointer (the missing-feature class); (b) GUIDES CHANGED OR SUPERSEDED - guides whose recommendation has changed since the pinned 0.0.172 baseline, or that are now discouraged/retired (the ACTIVE-DEFECT class: a rule that was correct and is now discouraged produces repairs that make sites worse while looking like the tool working). For (b), retrieve the current full guide text and compare against what the repo's principles/guides/tests actually assert; list each with the old vs new recommendation and the repo location that encodes the stale rule. Explicitly check the test suite for tests asserting outdated behaviour. ACCEPTANCE: two lists on the bead, each item naming the guide id, category, and the repo file/line that must change; changed-guide items name the specific behavioural delta, not just 'doc changed'.

comments.text:
# DIFF STEP RESULT — 0.0.172 (pinned) vs 0.0.193 (current catalog)

Method / evidence base (no invented ids; every id below verified against package files):
- Current catalog: `git show origin/fleet/mwg-catalog:knowledge/mwg-catalog.json` (177 guides, generated by `npx -y --ignore-scripts modern-web-guidance@0.0.193 list --json`).
- Guide text: cached real packages — 0.0.172 at `~/.npm/_npx/52ab4efd411c4b37/node_modules/modern-web-guidance` (137 guide files), 0.0.193 at `~/.npm/_npx/fe252ab63c16588c/node_modules/modern-web-guidance` (178 guide files). Deltas below are unified diffs of `skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/<category>/<id>.md` between those two packages.
- Semantic resolution of the 58 free-text query pointers: `npx -y --ignore-scripts modern-web-guidance@0.0.193 search "<query>"` run for all 58 (top-5 hits recorded; similarity scores cited where marginal).
- Pointers: knowledge/principles.json @ origin/master pins `guidanceCatalogVersion: modern-web-guidance@0.0.172`, 58 checks, 232 guide pointers = 195 unique = 136 exact current ids + 1 removed old id + 58 free-text queries.
- Note: `prompt-api` (built-in-ai) exists as a guide file in the 0.0.193 package but is absent from the `list --json` catalog (178 files vs 177 listed). Treated as not-in-catalog; flag upstream.

---

## (a) GUIDES NOT COVERED — present in 0.0.193, no rule implements them

Mapping result: 136 exact-id pointers all resolve in 0.0.193. Of the 58 free-text queries, 37 resolve semantically to current guides (adding coverage for motion, color, contrast-color, typography, responsive-design, respect-os-text-scale, dark-mode-toggle, scrollspy, state-aware-sticky-headers, accessible-web-components, trusted-types, validate-origins, lazy-load-video-and-audio, custom-elements and others). The remaining 21 queries no longer resolve (listed at the end of this section).

### a.1 — Current guides nobody references (27). All are "new" (no check exists); suggested parent check in parentheses is advisory only.

1. `accessible-generated-content` [accessibility] — new. (Topic is summarised inside the `accessibility` guide §6, which IS referenced at principles.json:191/553/591, but the dedicated guide has no pointer; candidate check: be-inclusive/names-roles-labels.)
2. `atrule-support-conditionals` [css] — new.
3. `browser-ui-theming` [visual-design] — new. (Content moved OUT of the `css` guide; see b.1. Candidate: respect-user-preferences/respects-color-scheme, principles.json:181.)
4. `cpp-on-the-web` [wasm] — new.
5. `drag` [ui-behaviors] — new.
6. `equal-width-text-lines` [visual-design] — new. (Candidate: be-inclusive/legible-text, principles.json:583.)
7. `form-associated-custom-elements` [html] — new. (Candidate: be-trustworthy/trustworthy-input-assistance, principles.json:895.)
8. `ime-safe-enter-submit` [forms] — new. (Now cross-referenced BY the `forms` guide; candidate: be-trustworthy/humane-error-handling, principles.json:882.)
9. `interaction-paint-timing` [performance] — new. (Candidate: be-fast-and-stable/good-core-web-vitals, principles.json:484.)
10. `local-network-access` [security] — new. (Candidate: be-private-and-secure/defensive-browser-policies, principles.json:739.)
11. `migrate-web-app-origin` [pwa] — new. Only guide in the pwa category; note it is about origin migration, NOT offline/installability (see a.2 L786).
12. `out-of-order-html-streaming` [performance] — new. (Candidate: be-fast-and-stable/efficient-resource-delivery, principles.json:518.)
13. `prerendering-custom-elements` [html] — new.
14. `progress-ring` [ui-components] — new. (Candidate: support-core-task-success/clear-system-state-and-recovery, principles.json:457.)
15. `responsive-table` [ui-atoms] — new. (Candidate: adapt-to-the-form-factor/responsive-no-horizontal-scroll, principles.json:389.)
16. `restrict-outbound-connections` [security] — new. (Candidate: be-private-and-secure/defensive-browser-policies, principles.json:739.)
17. `sanitize-untrusted-html` [security] — new. (Now cross-referenced BY the `security` guide §1.2; candidate: be-private-and-secure/secure-transport-and-headers, principles.json:703.)
18. `selector-atrule-combinations` [css] — new.
19. `shadow-dom` [html] — new.
20. `sms-otp-form` [forms] — new. (Now cross-referenced BY the `forms` guide; candidate: be-trustworthy/trustworthy-input-assistance, principles.json:895.)
21. `spatial-navigation` [ui-behaviors] — new. (Candidate: be-inclusive/structure-and-focus, principles.json:572.)
22. `spinner` [ui-components] — new. (Candidate: support-core-task-success/clear-system-state-and-recovery, principles.json:457.)
23. `styling-web-components` [html] — new.
24. `usage-aware-component-variations` [css] — new.
25. `verify-email-ownership` [security] — new. (Candidate: be-private-and-secure/in-context-permissions-and-modern-auth, principles.json:729.)
26. `visual-effects` [visual-design] — new. (Content moved OUT of the `css` guide; see b.1. Candidate: maximize-content-reduce-noise/reduced-chrome, principles.json:365.)
27. `web-components` [html] — new. (Candidate: be-resilient/resilient-runtime-behaviour, principles.json:778.)

### a.2 — Free-text-query pointers that no longer resolve against the 0.0.193 catalog (21)

Each was run through `modern-web-guidance@0.0.193 search`; top hit and score cited. None of these had a corresponding concrete guide in 0.0.172 either (id/description scan of the 137-guide old set), so these are pre-existing coverage holes made visible by the mapping, not regressions from the bump. File is knowledge/principles.json throughout.

1. L333 (maximize-content-reduce-noise/no-intrusive-interruptions) "avoid intrusive interstitial popup content first" — top hit declarative-dialog-popover-control @0.435 (wrong topic: it is about building popovers, not avoiding interstitials). No guide covers interstitial avoidance.
2. L365 (maximize-content-reduce-noise/reduced-chrome) "reduce visual clutter maximize content" — top hit defer-rendering-heavy-content @0.526 (rendering perf, not clutter). No guide covers chrome/clutter reduction. (Same check also holds the removed `prevent-text-wrapping` pointer — see b.7.)
3. L432 (support-core-task-success/clear-purpose-and-primary-action) "direct user attention primary action visual hierarchy task success" — top hit interest-triggered-action-previews @0.405 (not semantic). No guide covers visual hierarchy/primary-action heuristics.
4. L445 (support-core-task-success/primary-flow-completion) "primary user journey task completion" — search returned ZERO results. No guide covers task-completion flow analysis.
5. L457 (support-core-task-success/clear-system-state-and-recovery) "loading empty error success retry undo cancel state" — top hit agentic-javascript-tools @0.425 (not semantic). No guide covers UI state-machine/empty-error-retry patterns (progress-ring/spinner cover only spinner visuals).
6. L615 (follow-best-practices/no-console-errors) "avoid console errors uncaught exceptions" — top hit agentic-javascript-tools @0.456 (not semantic). No guide covers console-error hygiene.
7. L626 (follow-best-practices/sound-document-and-assets) "valid doctype charset image aspect ratio deprecated api best practices" — top hit deliver-optimized-decorative-images @0.369 (not semantic). No guide covers doctype/charset/deprecated-API hygiene.
8. L636 (follow-best-practices/browser-platform-hygiene) "baseline deprecated api bfcache source maps inspector issues paste prevention geolocation notification on load" — top hit capture-location-agnostic-data @0.338 (not semantic). No guide covers bfcache/source-maps/inspector-issues hygiene.
9. L657 (be-discoverable/title-and-description) "page title meta description seo" — top hit accessibility @0.460 (partial at best). No SEO guide exists in 0.0.193.
10. L665 (be-discoverable/crawlable-and-mobile-friendly) "crawlable links viewport meta robots descriptive link text" — top hit accessibility @0.456. No crawlability guide exists.
11. L673 (be-discoverable/canonical-and-indexing-signals) "canonical hreflang http status robots sitemap noindex seo indexing" — top hit validate-origins @0.308 (not semantic). No indexing/canonical guide exists.
12. L681 (be-discoverable/structured-and-shareable-metadata) "structured data schema.org json-ld open graph social preview metadata" — top hit language-model @0.368 (not semantic). No structured-data/OG guide exists.
13. L764 (be-resilient/progressive-enhancement) "progressive enhancement graceful degradation no javascript baseline fallback" — top hit calculate-with-intrinsic-sizes @0.531 (not semantic). No dedicated progressive-enhancement guide exists.
14. L778 (be-resilient/resilient-runtime-behaviour) "robust overlay state async resilience" — top hit stabilize-reactive-state @0.437 (scheduling, not overlay/async resilience). No matching guide.
15. L786 (be-resilient/offline-and-installable) "offline fallback service worker web app manifest installable pwa" — top hit migrate-web-app-origin @0.584 (origin migration, NOT offline). No offline/service-worker/manifest guide exists; the pwa category contains only migrate-web-app-origin.
16. L797 (be-resilient/network-and-http-failure-states) "http error network failure timeout retry stale data resilient state" — top hit local-network-access @0.408 (not semantic). No network-failure-states guide exists.
17. L821 (be-internationalised/lang-dir-and-logical-properties) "lang dir logical properties translation ready bidi" — top hit translator @0.374 (on-device translation API, not markup i18n). No lang/dir/logical-properties guide exists.
18. L868 (be-trustworthy/no-dark-patterns) "honest defaults no dark patterns confirmshaming forced continuity consent" — top hit dark-mode-toggle @0.429 (not semantic). No dark-patterns guide exists.
19. L907 (be-trustworthy/safe-commercial-and-account-flows) "clear pricing consent cancellation subscription checkout account flow" — top hit privacy @0.322 (not semantic). No commercial-flows guide exists.
20. L1010 (be-memory-efficient/no-leak-under-repeated-interaction) "memory leak retained heap growth under repeated interaction long single-page-app session" — top hit language-model @0.473 (not semantic). No memory/heap guide exists in 0.0.193.
21. L1029 (be-memory-efficient/bounded-footprint) "bounded memory footprint javascript heap size page weight proportionate allocations" — top hit html @0.432 (not semantic). No memory-footprint guide exists.
22. (Partial, borderline) L1049 (be-memory-efficient/no-detached-dom-or-unbounded-listeners) "detached DOM nodes event listener leak uncleared timers observers caches" — top hit custom-elements @0.452; its `disconnectedCallback` teardown guidance DOES cover listener/timer/observer cleanup for custom elements only. Counted as weakly resolved; no general detached-DOM guide exists.

---

## (b) GUIDES CHANGED OR SUPERSEDED — the ACTIVE-DEFECT class

### b.0 — Set-level diff (0.0.172 -> 0.0.193), from package file enumeration

- Removed ids (2): `declarative-button-actions` (user-experience) — renamed to `custom-button-actions` (ui-behaviors), see b.6; `prevent-text-wrapping` (user-experience) — removed with no successor, see b.7.
- Category restructure: 85 guides changed category. `user-experience` (79 guides) split into ui-behaviors (27), visual-design (15), css (12), ui-atoms (9), js (8), ui-components (4), performance (2); `passkeys` (6) folded into security; `css-layout` (1) folded into css; `highlight-text-ranges` moved css->ui-behaviors. New categories vs 0.0.172: js, pwa, wasm, ui-atoms, ui-behaviors, ui-components, visual-design.
- New guide files (43): listed in a.1 (27 unreferenced) plus 16 reachable only via the free-text queries (motion, color, contrast-color, typography, responsive-design, respect-os-text-scale, dark-mode-toggle, scrollspy, state-aware-sticky-headers, accessible-web-components, trusted-types, validate-origins, lazy-load-video-and-audio, custom-elements, shadow-dom, custom-button-actions — of these, shadow-dom and custom-button-actions: shadow-dom is unreferenced (in a.1), custom-button-actions is referenced but absent from the pinned 0.0.172, see b.6).

### b.1 — `css` [css] — referenced at knowledge/principles.json:623 (follow-best-practices/sound-document-and-assets)

SPLIT. Old (27593 chars): monolithic — dark mode, forced colors, tint generation, browser-UI theming, responsive design + responsive typography, typography/text-wrap, visual effects (depth/shapes/gradients/patterns), transitions & animations incl. the prefers-reduced-motion guidance, generated content alt text. New (12538 chars): those sections replaced by one-line pointers to NEW guides `dark-mode`, `component-specific-light-dark-theme`, `color`, `browser-ui-theming`, `responsive-design`, `typography`, `visual-effects`, `motion`, `accessible-generated-content`, `accessibility`, `performance`. Behavioural delta: any check relying on `retrieve "css"` for dark-mode/forced-colors/typography/motion/generated-content guidance now gets a stub; the receiving check (sound-document-and-assets) loses the actual recommendations. Also added: `revert-layer` note for override fallbacks. principles.json must add pointers to the split destinations (see a.1 items 3, 26 and query-resolved color/typography/motion/responsive-design).

### b.2 — `security` [security] — referenced at principles.json:635 (browser-platform-hygiene), :702 (secure-transport-and-headers), :737 (defensive-browser-policies)

Multiple recommendation reversals/strengthenings:
- OLD §3.2: `object-src 'none'` called a "legacy directive" that "can be omitted"; `frame-ancestors` and `require-trusted-types-for` absent from the enforced CSP example; enforcement gated on "report-only violations near zero". NEW: `object-src 'none'` is MANDATORY, `frame-ancestors 'self'` and `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` are MANDATORY in both report-only and enforced examples; the report-only-first gate is removed for direct codebase edits ("apply Phase 1 + reporting + Phase 3 enforcement in the same pass").
- OLD §1.3 cookies: no HttpOnly requirement. NEW: "Set HttpOnly on session and authentication cookies unless the cookie must be read by client-side script".
- OLD §3.3 Trusted Types: incremental report-only rollout with an escape-`<>`-only policy example. NEW: enforce directly; DO NOT create pass-through policies; prefer `element.setHTML()`; defers to the new `trusted-types` guide (unreferenced — a.1).
- NEW additions: `Vary: Sec-Fetch-Dest, Sec-Fetch-Mode, Sec-Fetch-Site` on Fetch Metadata middleware; `focus-without-user-activation=()` in Permissions-Policy; per-request nonce middleware pattern; postMessage origin validation now points to the new `validate-origins` guide (unreferenced — a.1).

### b.3 — `agentic-javascript-tools` [webmcp] — referenced at principles.json:977 (be-agent-ready/structured-agent-capabilities)

- OLD: `document.modelContext.registerTool({...})` synchronous; `execute(input)` single-arg; errors thrown. NEW: `await registerTool(...)` (now async); new `exposedTo` option for cross-origin frame tool exposure (with SecurityError on untrustworthy origins); `execute(input, { signal })` two-arg signature; MANDATORY: long-running tools MUST honor the abort signal; errors must be RETURNED as structured values ("DO NOT throw new Error(...)") because thrown error messages never reach the agent; getTools/executeTool repositioned as for in-page agents/test harnesses only.
- Same API change class in `agentic-forms` [webmacp→webmcp] referenced at principles.json:976: `toolactivated`/`toolcancel` events moved from `window` to `document.modelContext` in Chrome 156; code must feature-detect the target.

### b.4 — `language-model` [built-in-ai] — referenced at principles.json:986 (be-agent-ready/on-device-inference)

Added a large "Dos and Don'ts" section (7235->16698 chars): pre-warm the session before the user clicks; set initialPrompts only at `create()`; `clone()` a base session for repetitive tasks instead of repeated `create()`; explicitly `destroy()` unused sessions; treat all streamed LLM output as untrusted — sanitize the FULL combined output (Sanitizer API), never set innerHTML per chunk; minimize input size; use `responseConstraint` JSON Schema instead of "output only JSON" instructions. None of this existed in 0.0.172.

### b.5 — `dark-mode` [user-experience->visual-design] — referenced at principles.json:181 (respect-user-preferences/respects-color-scheme)

- OLD: full in-guide toggle implementation — two-state control UX rationale, FOUC-prevention inline script, `<meta name="color-scheme">` updating, localStorage persistence. NEW: all of that MOVED to the new `dark-mode-toggle` guide (unreferenced — reachable via query [0]); dark-mode now just says "most sites do not need a persistent toggle".
- NEW additions: `light-dark()` image values (`image(<color>)` wrapping rule — both values must be the same type); any JS reading `matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` MUST also handle its `change` event.

### b.6 — `declarative-button-actions` -> `custom-button-actions` [user-experience->ui-behaviors] — RENAMED

principles.json references `custom-button-actions` at L443 (support-core-task-success/primary-flow-completion) and L865 (be-trustworthy/no-dark-patterns) — an id that DOES NOT EXIST in the pinned 0.0.172 (verified against the cached 0.0.172 package), so the current pin and pointers are already inconsistent; under 0.0.193 the pointer resolves to the renamed guide. Text delta: OLD step 3 "attach the `command` event listener to the document (or a common parent)… even if dispatched by a polyfill"; NEW step 3 "attach the command event listener directly on the target element", plus NEW mandatory step 4 "Handle aria states: custom commands do not have inherent semantics, you must handle `aria-pressed`/`aria-expanded`".

### b.7 — `prevent-text-wrapping` [user-experience] — REMOVED, referenced at principles.json:362 (maximize-content-reduce-noise/reduced-chrome)

No successor guide in 0.0.193: grep of all 178 guide files finds NO remaining `text-wrap: nowrap` recommendation (the new `typography` guide covers only balance/pretty; `respect-os-text-scale` now actively warns against nowrap on sentence blocks). The pointer is dead and the recommendation it encoded (modern replacement for `white-space: nowrap`) no longer exists in the feed. Pointer must be deleted or the check re-scoped.

### b.8 — `custom-select-picker-layouts` [forms] — referenced at principles.json:345 (maximize-content-reduce-noise/semantic-dismissible-primitives)

Rewritten (5161->7558 chars). OLD: general `appearance: base-select` adoption advice incl. "DO NOT assume the styles apply to all browsers equally yet; verify support and provide a fallback", `<selectedcontent>` for trigger content, standard `value` attributes, `name`+`<label>` requirement. NEW: narrowed to 2D grid/custom picker layouts; those general DOs removed; new guidance to compute next/previous option via `getBoundingClientRect()` geometry instead of parsing `grid-template-columns` CSS strings; new warning that styling `select::picker(select)` without `:open` makes the picker visible when closed.

### b.9 — `animate-to-from-top-layer` [user-experience->ui-behaviors] — referenced at principles.json:249 (implement-natural-interactions/physical-gestures)

Feature-detection reversal: OLD recommended `CSS.supports('transition-behavior', 'allow-discrete') && CSS.supports('overlay', 'auto')`. NEW states Firefox 129+ parses `allow-discrete` without actually transitioning `display` (Firefox bug 1882408), so CSS.supports is explicitly insufficient; a runtime probe element is required instead. Code also migrated from the `transition: ... allow-discrete` shorthand to longhand properties. Same change in `animate-element-entry-exit` (referenced at principles.json:248), which additionally gains a `[data-closing]` vs `[hidden]` exit-fallback pattern.

### b.10 — `declarative-dialog-popover-control` [user-experience->ui-behaviors] — referenced at principles.json:341 (maximize-content-reduce-noise/semantic-dismissible-primitives)

- OLD feature detect: `'commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype`. NEW: `globalThis.CommandEvent` check with a bundled CommandEvent polyfill class.
- OLD polyfill URL `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/invokers-polyfill@latest/dist/index.min.js`; NEW `https://esm.run/invokers-polyfill` wrapped in an async IIFE.
- NEW: polyfill does not manage ARIA states — manual `aria-pressed`/`aria-expanded` sync required (matches b.6).
- Fallback click-handler now uses `event.composedPath()` instead of `event.target.closest(...)`.

### b.11 — `passkey-management` [passkeys->security] — referenced at principles.json:728 (in-context-permissions-and-modern-auth), :906 (safe-commercial-and-account-flows)

NEW requirement: always feature-detect Signal API methods before invoking (`if (PublicKeyCredential.signalAllAcceptedCredentials)` etc.) — 0.0.172 called them unconditionally. Backend scope widened to user profile detail updates; `signalCurrentUserDetails()` now keyed to account rename (`name`/`displayName`).

### b.12 — `consistent-cross-document-transitions` [user-experience->ui-behaviors] — referenced at principles.json:762 (be-resilient/progressive-enhancement)

- Clarified correction: `<link rel="expect">` waits only for the target element to be PARSED, not for image download/decode — NEW requirement to preload/pre-decode transition images and provide explicit sizing to avoid blank snapshots.
- OLD: render-blocking timeout skips the transition with a `TimeoutError`. NEW: rejects `viewTransition.ready` with an `InvalidStateError`.
- NEW: DO NOT mark analytics/ad/tag-manager loaders with `blocking="render"`.

### b.13 — Popover-polyfill guidance change across 4 referenced guides

OLD variants of "use the @oddbird/popover-polyfill" (unconditional). NEW (all four): MANDATORY feature-detect `'popover' in HTMLElement.prototype` and load the polyfill ONLY when native support is missing, never unconditionally.
- `persistent-toast-notifications` [user-experience->ui-components] — principles.json:309, :444, :456, :794. (Also dropped the old "fall back to a fixed-position div" sentence.)
- `interest-triggered-tooltips` [user-experience->ui-behaviors] — principles.json:294. NEW caveat: `popover="hint"` behavior is NOT polyfilled in browsers with popover-but-no-hint; a focus-opened tooltip may stay open.
- `position-aware-tooltips` [user-experience->ui-atoms] — principles.json:293.
- `persistent-app-tours` [user-experience->ui-components] — principles.json:308.
(Same reformat also in `resilient-context-menus-and-nested-dropdowns` [user-experience->ui-atoms] — principles.json:772.)

### b.14 — `performance` [performance] — referenced at principles.json:483 (be-fast-and-stable/good-core-web-vitals)

LCP image guidance reworked. OLD: fetchpriority="high" on the LCP `<img>`; declare LCP in raw HTML; preload CSS background-image LCPs; fetchpriority="low" to demote above-the-fold competitors. NEW: fetchpriority="high" on BOTH the `<img>` AND any `<link rel="preload" as="image">`; fetchpriority="low" only for competitors NOT in the initial viewport; NEW DO: `loading="lazy"` for images/iframes/media well outside the viewport. Same pairing change in `optimize-image-priority` [performance] — principles.json:514, :930 (now pairs `loading="lazy"` with fetchpriority="low" for galleries/carousels).

### b.15 — `forms` [forms] — referenced at principles.json:442 (primary-flow-completion), :876 (humane-error-handling)

NEW: `autocorrect="off"` + `autocapitalize="off"` + `spellcheck="false"` on identifier fields (usernames, emails, URLs, codes); NEW: single `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code">` + WebOTP for SMS OTPs (points to new `sms-otp-form`, unreferenced — a.1); NEW: check `KeyboardEvent.isComposing` before Enter-as-submit (points to new `ime-safe-enter-submit`, unreferenced — a.1); the `type="number"` DON'T now explicitly covers one-time passcodes. Same identifier-field addition appears in `autofill-sign-in-form` (principles.json:892, :904) and `autofill-sign-up-form` (principles.json:893).

### b.16 — `translator` [built-in-ai] — referenced at principles.json:819 (be-internationalised/lang-dir-and-logical-properties)

NEW: "DO NOT use or check the deprecated `window.ai.translator` namespace." (0.0.172 had no deprecation warning.)

### b.17 — Canvas/WebGL element-texture API change in 4 referenced guides

OLD: `gl.texElementImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D, 0, gl.RGBA, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, uiElement)` (7-arg form). NEW: `try { gl.texElementImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D, gl.RGBA8, uiElement) } catch ...` (3-arg RGBA8 form with error handling). Applies to `interactive-content-in-3d-scenes` [visual-design] (principles.json:360), `expose-canvas-content-to-browser-features` [visual-design] (:554), `export-html-media-from-canvas` [visual-design] (:364), `apply-webgl-shaders` [visual-design] (:359).

### b.18 — `accessibility` [accessibility] — referenced at principles.json:191, :553, :591

Restructured (TOC added, sections reorganized); NEW guidelines added: manage toggle states with `aria-expanded`/`aria-pressed`; do not put `aria-hidden`/`role="presentation"` on focusable elements; skip-link code example; CSS-generated-content section (mirrors new `accessible-generated-content` guide). No recommendation reversals found.

### b.19 — `css-layout` [css-layout->css] — referenced at principles.json:388 (adapt-to-the-form-factor/responsive-no-horizontal-scroll)

NEW: "Do NOT use `overflow: hidden` to mask layout issues — fix them at the source" (with the replaced-elements inline-gap example). Anchor positioning support note updated (Safari 27 only). Cross-reference retargeted from `css` to the new `responsive-design` guide.

### b.20 — Baseline-availability upgrades (referenced guides whose support claims changed; matters because repo convention is Baseline Widely Available gating)

- `physics-based-easing` (principles.json:246): linear() easing "Newly available" -> "Widely available".

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] Agent children inherit full parent environment exposing credentials
description:
Rule: tm-agent-inherits-full-environment (also vuln-triage unclassified / C3)
Location: runner/run-batch.mjs:500 (also fixer/fix.mjs:618)
Fingerprint: 4b23d0ea83d2adbf... (vuln-triage: fb32407ec65582cc...)
Behaviour: The batch runner passes { ...process.env, WEB_UPLIFT_LAUNCH_LOG } to the spawned agent, and fixer/fix.mjs:618 spawns the agent with no env option at all, inheriting the full parent environment. The child's context carries untrusted page text and has network egress. title: [factory-audit/threat-model] SSRF: page-controlled manifest href is fetched by the privileged Node process (F-003)
description:
## What
`evidence/cli.mjs` fetches page-controlled URLs from the privileged Node process with no scheme/host restriction and `redirect: 'follow'`. A malicious audited page can therefore make the auditor fetch cloud metadata, loopback, or private-range hosts, and the response body is persisted into `manifest.data` and the report artifacts.

## Evidence (verified in code at origin/master 21a3a53)
- `evidence/cli.mjs:2736-2738` — `manifestHref` comes straight from the live DOM: `(document.querySelector('link[rel="manifest"]') || {}).href`.
- `evidence/cli.mjs:2743-2744` — `await fetch(manifestHref, { redirect: 'follow', ... })`; on success `manifest.data = await res.json()` (line 2748), then `manifest.fields`/`manifest.icons` are projected into the resilience evidence and written to the report.
- `evidence/cli.mjs:1698` — the discoverability raw fetch also follows redirects from the target URL, so a redirect target is page-controlled too.
- The service-worker script fetch at `evidence/cli.mjs:2764` reads the script text but only tests a fetch-listener regex and does not persist it; SW registration script URLs are same-origin by web-platform rule, so this path is *not* a cross-origin SSRF (the station finding's text lumps it in).
- LINE-NUMBER NOTE: when this bead was first filed the audit target was 4cccc60 and these were lines 2713/2720/2741 and 1674-1678. `web-uplift-yu8` then landed (master `21a3a53`) and added ~24 lines near 1670, shifting them. The code shape is unchanged; the numbers above are the current master.

## Why it is real
The project's own threat model already records this as a **violated invariant**, not a hypothetical:
`~/agents/findings/web-uplift-factory-THREAT_MODEL.md` section 6, I2: "Page-derived URLs fetched by the Node process must be restricted to allowed schemes and must not reach loopback, link-local, or private-range hosts, including via redirects. This is currently violated (F-003)."
Section 4 lists it as an untrusted attack surface (manifest href + followed redirects). No prior bead tracked F-003 (checked `bd list --all`).

## Calibrated severity
P1. Station input: `high` from vuln-discovery, vuln-verify and vuln-triage; `medium` from threat-model. Reachability is direct from any audited page and the response body lands in a published artifact. Note the store recorded every finding as CRITICAL (known normaliser bug, fleet-eqv), so this is a hand calibration from the station reports.

## Station citation
Factory audit run 2026-10-06T00:22Z (target `/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-factory` @4cccc60), rule `TM-003-ssrf-page-controlled-fetch` / `ssrf-page-derived-fetch` / `vuln-triage/ssrf-unvalidated-outbound-fetch`; reports under `/home/exedev/agents/runs/*-web-uplift-factory-20261006-00*/report.json`.

## Bounded next step
Before every Node-side fetch of a page-derived URL: allow only `http`/`https`, resolve the host and reject loopback, `169.254.0.0/16`, RFC1918/CGNAT and metadata endpoints, use `redirect: 'manual'` (or re-validate each hop), and cap the response size. Resolve the manifest relative to the already-validated target origin rather than trusting an absolute href.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text:
COORD IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (2026-10-06T00:38Z). Assigned to web-uplift-net-bodies. P1, treat as the priority bead; but it edits evidence/cli.mjs, which is still in flight in yu8, so START IT ONLY AFTER the merger reports the yu8 push, on a fresh branch off the new master.

SCOPE — harden every Node-side fetch of a page-derived URL:
- evidence/cli.mjs:2713/2720-2725 manifest href -> fetch(..., {redirect:'follow'}) -> res.json() persisted into manifest.data/report.
- evidence/cli.mjs:1674-1678 the discoverability raw fetch, which also follows redirects from the target.
- Do NOT over-fix the service-worker script fetch at :2741: SW registration script URLs are same-origin by web-platform rule, so it is not a cross-origin SSRF and the finding text wrongly lumps it in. Say so in the bead if you leave it.

REQUIRED MITIGATION (cover the whole surface, not just the first URL):
1. Scheme allowlist: only http and https. Reject file:, data:, blob:, ftp: and anything else.
2. Host/IP restriction: resolve the hostname and reject loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), link-local (169.254.0.0/16 incl. 169.254.169.254 metadata, fe80::/10), RFC1918 (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) and IPv6 unique-local (fc00::/7).
3. IP LITERAL ENCODINGS: handle decimal, octal, hex, IPv4-mapped IPv6, and bracketed IPv6 forms — do not rely on a regex over dotted-quad only. Prefer parsing via the platform URL parser plus an IP parse, or normalise before checking.
4. REDIRECTS: this is where a naive fix fails. Node fetch follows redirects internally, so either set redirect:'manual' and validate EVERY hop's scheme+resolved host before following, or otherwise prove each hop is re-validated. A redirect to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 must be refused.
5. DNS REBINDING: validating the hostname once is not enough if the name re-resolves. At minimum re-validate per hop; if you can pin/verify the resolved address actually connected, do that and record the limitation honestly if you cannot.
6. Fail CLOSED: on resolution failure or any rejection, skip the fetch and record a reason; never persist a body you did not validate. Cap the response size so a huge or endless body cannot blow up memory.
7. Keep legitimate behaviour: a normal http(s) same-origin or CDN manifest (e.g. the playground fixtures) must still be fetched and parsed exactly as before.

TESTS (non-vacuity required): a local test server that (a) serves a manifest href pointing at a loopback/private address and asserts it is refused and no body is persisted; (b) redirects to such an address and asserts refused; (c) still serves a legitimate manifest and asserts it is fetched+parsed. Pin the existing fixtures too so a regression shows.

PROCESS: one scoped change, branch off the post-yu8 master, push fleet/net-bodies early, run the relevant focused test first then one fleet-gate with CHROME_BIN/CHROME_PATH unset, report sha + command + exit code + tip==gated-tip, then IN_REVIEW. Review goes to a cross-family subagent and I will ask it to ATTACK the mitigation (encodings, redirects, rebinding). Do not change runner/agents.mjs here — that is tia.

title: no Baseline oracle: fix mode decides browser support from model memory
description:
SKILL.md fix mode tells the model to "assume Baseline Widely available is
safe" and to follow the guide's fallback advice otherwise. Nothing in the
repo supplies Baseline status. grep for web-features across the source
returns nothing; it is not a dependency. guidanceCatalogVersion pins the
Modern Web Guidance catalog but MWG guides are advice, not a support
oracle.

So the single rule that decides whether a fix is safe to ship is answered
from model memory, which is precisely the knowledge that rots fastest and
which this project exists to stop relying on.

Fix: add web-features as a dependency and expose a lookup the model can call
during both audit and fix, returning the Baseline status (widely / newly /
limited, plus the low and high dates) for a feature id. Record the resolved
status on every finding whose fix proposes a modern feature, so a report
states "anchor positioning, Baseline newly available since <date>" rather
than asserting it from memory.

Pin the web-features version alongside guidanceCatalogVersion so a run is
reproducible.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW (deepseek lane) of origin/uplift/dwg-baseline-oracle-impl @ 1fcb405. Verdict: FAIL as-is - the design is sound but the oracle returns wrong or missing answers for a material share of the queries the SKILL tells the model to make, which is the "wrong answer that looks like evidence" class this repo keeps closing. Fixes are small and localised; details and exact directions below.

Gate: npm test PASSES (tests OK) in a worktree at the branch with a real `npm ci` (web-features installed). Everything below was measured, not read.

STRENGTHS (verified):
- O(1) hit path: compatIndex/nameIndex are built once at import and hits are Map.get. 1216 features, 7997 short keys indexed.
- Redirect resolution has a visited-set cycle guard and no dangling targets exist in the pinned data (checked: 10 single redirects, 0 dangling, 0 multi-hop chains).
- Schema change is additive and backwards-compatible: an existing report still validates, and a finding carrying the SKILL-named baseline shape (featureId/featureName/status/lowDate/highDate/fallbackMandatory) validates too.
- Install integrity: all five vendored pairs are byte-identical (knowledge/baseline.mjs, knowledge/principles.json, schema, both SKILL copies), the install plan now vendors web-features AND the oracle file, and the catalog checksum re-pin is CORRECT (sha256 e343ae75... matches both example reports).
- CLI: `web-uplift baseline <q> [--json]` wired with help text, exit 1 on unknown, error to stderr; regression test covers id lookups, BCD keys, names, () stripping, one redirect, unknown-with-suggestion and both CLI modes.

F1 (must fix) - the symbol forms the modern-CSS checks are ABOUT do not resolve. Only "()" is normalized; leading ":"/"::"/"@" are not, and the prefix list has no css.selectors. 9 of 40 queries taken from the checks' own detectableVia hints miss entirely: :has, :is, :where, :popover-open, :user-valid, ::part, ::slotted, @container, @view-transition. Reproduce: `node knowledge/baseline.mjs @container` -> exit 1, "Unknown web platform feature". Direction: strip a leading ::/:/@ (and keep "()"), try the stripped form against css.properties./css.types./css.at-rules./css.selectors., and keep the raw form as a last resort. ::backdrop resolves today only by accident of a suffix match.

F2 (must fix) - ambiguous short keys silently pick by data order, and it produces a WRONG answer on a real query. 1284 of the 7997 short keys are owned by more than one feature. Demonstrated: `min` is owned by eight features and resolves to css-typed-om (status limited, fallbackMandatory true), while the CSS math function the checks mean is css.types.min -> min-max-clamp (widely). `max` is the same. The prefix path that would find css.types.min exists but runs AFTER the bare-suffix hit, so ordering decides the answer. Direction: resolve prefixed/exact BCD keys before the bare-suffix index, and when a bare-suffix query is still ambiguous, say so (e.g. return the candidate ids) instead of choosing one.

F3 (must fix) - plural redirect_targets are silently truncated to the first. Two records in the pinned data have more than one target, and one is materially misleading: text-wrap-style -> targets [text-wrap, text-wrap-balance, text-wrap-pretty], statuses [low, low, false]. The oracle returns text-wrap (newly available, fallback mandatory) and never mentions that text-wrap-pretty is Limited. Direction: report every target (or refuse with an ambiguity note) rather than [0].

F4 (test coverage) - the regression test cannot catch F1/F2/F3: it only queries symbol-free ids/keys/names, and it asserts values the code produces. Add assertions for a symbol form (@container or :popover-open), an ambiguous short key (min -> min-max-clamp), and a plural-target record.

Follow-ups (recorded, not blockers):
- coverage.baselineCatalogVersion is a dead schema field: nothing reads or writes it and the SKILL never tells the model to record it. Either wire it (stamp it when a finding carries baseline) or drop it; the version is declared in principles.json but never carried onto a report.
- finding.baseline cannot be the oracle's CLI output pasted verbatim: the oracle emits id/name and the schema requires featureId/featureName, so the natural `--json` -> paste workflow produces an INVALID report (measured: missing featureId). Either emit the schema's names from the oracle or say the mapping in the SKILL.
- The new SKILL step gives only the in-repo path (`node knowledge/baseline.mjs`); every other invocation in the SKILL names the installed form too, which for this file is `.web-uplift/knowledge/baseline.mjs`.
- Perf, measured for context: ~270-405ms per CLI invocation, dominated by importing web-features (not the indexing). Fine for one-off queries; if a fix pass wants many, a batch mode would help. The miss path scans all features for suggestions (bounded at 5) - fine, just not O(1).
- .web-uplift/manifest.json churn: the commit bumps installedAt with no version change, which will conflict across lanes; consider ignoring that field in future install commits.
- The commit has no body for a 687-line feature that changes what the model is instructed to trust; worth a paragraph for the next reviewer.

Reviewer: deepseek lane. I did not merge anything; uplift-merger lands after the author closes F1-F3.

title: add targets primitive for WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 target size
description:
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) requires 24 by 24 CSS px for
pointer targets. Two checks reference target size in their hints
(be-inclusive/zoom-reflow-targets-and-media,
adapt-to-the-form-factor/input-modality-aware) but no primitive measures it,
so every audit hand-rolls the probe or skips it.

Hand-rolled probe on https://paul.kinlan.me/ found 40 of 61 interactive
elements under 24px in at least one dimension, including primary nav links
at 40x20 and 55x20. Whether those pass depends on the 2.5.8 spacing and
inline exceptions, which is exactly the judgement the model should be making
against real numbers rather than not making at all.

Fix: add a `targets` primitive that enumerates a,button,input,select,
summary,[role=button],[role=link], records bounding boxes, and applies the
2.5.8 exception structure descriptively: flag under-24 targets, mark which
are inline-in-text (exempt), and compute nearest-neighbour spacing for the
spacing exception. Descriptive signal, the model still judges.

Should run at both a desktop and a 360x800 touch viewport, since the answer
differs by form factor.

Per target: box in CSS px, areaPx, display, tag/role/id/name, underMin, inlineInText, spacingPasses, nearestTargetEdgeDistancePx, nearestTargetCenterDistancePx. Skips zero-size and hidden elements (counted), caps at 400 measured (matched/omitted counted: the 1s8 cap convention).
- Exceptions the spec spells out, read from geometry: inlineInText (text nodes beside the target in the same parent, and not a block-level box) and spacingPasses (a 24px-diameter circle centred on the box clears every other target's box AND every other undersized target's circle, i.e. edge distance >= 12 and undersized-centre distance >= 24). The UA-control and essential exceptions are NOT detected - the note says so and the model judges them. underMinNoKnownExemptionCount is the mechanical "needs judgement" number, not a verdict.
- Two passes by default: desktop-1280x720 and narrow-360x800; --viewport gives one pass. They are pure LAYOUT sizes, because with mobile emulation a page without a viewport meta lays out at Chrome's 980px default and the "360x800" pass would silently measure a 980px layout (I hit exactly that in the first cut: innerWidth reported 980x2178). applyConditions() now takes an internal viewportMobile flag (default true, so no other primitive's behaviour changes). Each pass reports the layout width/height it actually measured.
- README.md: added the targets row to the primitive table.

Cross-check against the bead's hand probe on https://paul.kinlan.me/ (live run, --wait 800):
  desktop-1280x720: 61 targets measured, 40 under 24px -> the hand-rolled probe's "40 of 61", reproduced exactly.
                    27 inline-exempt, 32 spacing-exempt, 0 with no read exemption.
  narrow-360x800:   60 targets measured, 28 under 24px, 20 inline, 14 spacing, 0 with no read exemption.
So the nav links at 40x20 that looked like failures in the hand probe are spacing/inline exempt under the spec's own exceptions - which is exactly the judgement the check needed to be able to make, and it is not a false failure.

Verification: npm test green (~31s). New testTargetsPrimitive covers the geometry fixture (undersized link in a sentence -> underMin + inlineInText; two adjacent 16x16 buttons -> underMin, not inline, spacingPasses false; two spaced undersized buttons -> spacingPasses true; a 48x48 button -> not undersized and spacingPasses null; a zero-size target -> skipped; both default passes reaching the same verdict), the cap on a 420-link page (matched 420 / measured 400 / omitted 20), and a page with no targets reporting zeroes rather than an absent field.

title: no first-party evidence path for console errors and uncaught exceptions
description:
The check follow-best-practices/no-console-errors has no first-party
evidence path. evidence/cli.mjs and evidence/cdp.mjs contain zero
references to Runtime.consoleAPICalled, Runtime.exceptionThrown or
Log.entryAdded.

The model can only judge this check by running Lighthouse, or by writing an
evaluate probe that runs after load and therefore cannot see the errors that
already fired during load. Under the atomic coverage contract that makes the
honest outcome not-run, which makes the whole run partial, which blocks the
scorecard.

Fix: enable the Log and Runtime domains during navigate() and accumulate
console errors, warnings and uncaught exceptions into the evidence output.
Cheapest landing spot is a shared collector in evidence/cdp.mjs navigate()
so every primitive can report what the page logged while it was being
measured, with a dedicated `console` primitive for the direct case.

Verify: a fixture page that throws on load must produce the exception in the
output.

title: add axe primitive with Page.setBypassCSP and vendored axe-core
description:
SKILL.md names axe-core injected through the evaluate primitive as the
prescribed accessibility evidence path. It silently fails on any site with
a strict script-src, which is to say on exactly the well-configured sites.

Measured on https://paul.kinlan.me/ (CSP script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
plus three named hosts):
  fetch(jsdelivr axe-core)      -> "Failed to fetch"
  <script src=...> injection    -> onerror fires, result "blocked"
  typeof window.axe             -> "undefined"

Page.setBypassCSP appears nowhere in evidence/cli.mjs or evidence/cdp.mjs
(grep count 0). With it enabled the same page loads axe and returns real
results: 1 violation, heading-order (1 node). So the capability is one CDP
call away and the audit is currently blind.

Fix: add an `axe` primitive that enables Page.setBypassCSP, injects a
vendored axe-core (no CDN dependency, no network requirement at audit time),
runs axe.run, and returns violations grouped by impact. Keep it descriptive:
the model still judges. Feeds be-inclusive/names-roles-labels,
sufficient-contrast, structure-and-focus.

Note the interaction with be-private-and-secure: bypassing CSP must be
scoped to the a11y primitive only, never left on for the headers/secrets
primitives, or the security evidence becomes invalid.

title: dom primitive truncates HTML/CSS at 200KB with no truncated flag
description:
The dom primitive truncates without saying so:

  outerHTML: document.documentElement.outerHTML.slice(0, 200000),
  css: collectCss().slice(0, 200000),

There is no truncated flag anywhere in evidence/cli.mjs (grep -c truncated
= 0). A model that greps the returned css for "@container" or "anchor-name"
on a site with more than 200KB of CSS gets zero matches and cannot
distinguish "the site does not use container queries" from "the evidence
was cut off before the rule".

That silently converts a truncation into a false pass on
component-level-responsiveness, anchored-positioning,
semantic-dismissible-primitives and respects-color-scheme.

For scale: paul.kinlan.me returns 79829 bytes of CSS, comfortably under the
cap, but nothing in the output tells the model that.

Fix: return { text, bytes, truncated } (or sibling cssTruncated /
htmlTruncated booleans plus the original length) so the model can see the
cap was hit and gather the rest another way. Apply the same treatment to the
other slice() caps that drop data silently (secrets findings capped at 30,
cookies at 50, images at 30, HAR lists at 10).

Verify: point dom at a page with >200KB of CSS and assert truncated is true
and bytes reports the real length.

title: discoverability: h1PresentInRaw false negative when h1 contains inline markup
description:
The discoverability primitive reports h1PresentInRaw: false for https://paul.kinlan.me/ even though the h1 is fully server-rendered. Evidence: rendered h1 (innerText): "Hello. I am Paul Kinlan." raw HTML:

\n Hello. I am Paul Kinlan.\n

evidence/cli.mjs:1368 does: rawLower.includes(h.toLowerCase().slice(0, 40)) innerText collapses the newlines and drops the inline span boundary, so the rendered string never appears verbatim in the stripped raw text. Any h1 containing an inline element (span, em, a, strong) or wrapped across lines produces a false negative. This feeds be-discoverable and be-agent-ready, so the tool reports a server-rendered site as missing its h1 from the crawler view. It is a wrong-answer bug, not a missing feature. Fix: normalise whitespace on both sides before comparison, and compare content tokens rather than a raw substring, consistent with how coveragePct is already computed via contentTokens(). Verify: re-run `node evidence/cli.mjs discoverability https://paul.kinlan.me/` and assert h1PresentInRaw is true. Add a fixture with an inline-span h1 to tests/regression.mjs.
