title: fix mode reports PASS on partial coverage, bypassing the atomic contract
description:
SKILL.md states a partial run must never produce a score or a completion
claim. aggregate/scorecard.mjs enforces that (it throws on
coverage.complete !== true). fixer/fix.mjs does not: countOutstanding only
counts findings whose principleId is not excused, and never reads
report.coverage at all (grep -c coverage fixer/fix.mjs = 0).

Consequence: a fix run over a report with 40 not-run checks and zero
findings prints "PASS: no outstanding issues remain." and exits 0. That is
the absence-of-evidence failure the coverage contract exists to prevent,
reintroduced through the fix path.

Fix: treat blocked and not-run check outcomes as outstanding work in
countOutstanding, and refuse to print PASS when coverage.complete is not
true. Report the exact executed/expected counts instead.

Depends on the scoreOf crash fix landing first.

  1. zero findings, 3 blocked + 2 not-run, coverage.complete false -> 'PASS: no outstanding issues remain.', exit 0
  2. the same rows but coverage.complete declared TRUE -> PASS, exit 0, score 100, AND a published scorecard.html

Shape 2 decided the design. coverage.complete cannot be the authority, because a report that declares itself complete while still carrying blocked rows is exactly the shape that must not pass. completionState reads the checkOutcomes ROWS and takes the WORSE of rows vs declared accounting, so a wrong self-declaration can only cost a run its pass, never grant one.

Also treated as incomplete: a report with no coverage accounting at all (pre-contract). It runs (that is the acl fix) but cannot claim a completed audit. Absent evidence is not evidence of absence.

Progress metric changed from findings-only to findings + unconcluded checks, so concluding a blocked check registers as progress. Without that, an iteration spent unblocking a check would have looked like no progress and stopped the climb early.

Goal mode gets the same guard, checked BEFORE the score, so a partial run cannot buy a pass with a good score on the checks it did conclude.

Scope note for the reviewer: aggregate/compare.mjs:243 has its own copy of countOutstanding with the same findings-only blind spot. Left alone deliberately - compare output is descriptive (before/after deltas), not a pass claim, so it cannot manufacture a false pass. Filed separately as a follow-up.

Test: testFixRefusesPassOnIncompleteCoverage - both shapes stop with exit 1 and name the unconcluded checks, a partial run cannot meet a score goal, a pre-contract report cannot claim completion, a genuinely clean report still passes exit 0. Verified by reverting fix.mjs to f7f44b4 and confirming the new test fails on 'PASS: no outstanding issues remain.'

Gate: node tests/regression.mjs -> tests OK, exit 0, run from the committed tree. Needs review by a different model family before landing.

cdpEndpointExposure serializes non-loopback host reachability probes in a for-loop, creating a sequential await waterfall on the browser startup critical path.

## Location & Evidence
- `evidence/cdp.mjs:649` (and vendored mirror `.web-uplift/evidence/cdp.mjs:649`)
- `for (const host of hosts) { const verdict = await connect(host, port, timeoutMs); ... }`
- `connect` defaults to `probeDevtools`, which waits up to `timeoutMs` (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`).

## Mechanism & Impact
On hosts with several non-loopback interfaces (e.g. Docker bridges, VPNs, link-local IPv6), an interface that drops packets or never refuses incurs the full timeout sequentially. In the worst case, this adds N x timeoutMs of serialized waiting before Chrome launch verification completes and audit work can start. Probes are independent, read-only reachability checks with no ordering dependencies.

## Station Citation & Severity Rationale
- Station: `perf-review` (`sequential-await-waterfall`). Run: 20261010T031848Z, target `origin/master@5eb6b44`.
- Severity: Station rated High. Mapped to P2 task because it blocks the startup critical path on multi-interface hosts.

## Remediation
Run per-host probes concurrently using `Promise.all`, then evaluate the results in the original hosts order to maintain deterministic notes and probe counts. Update both `evidence/cdp.mjs` and `.web-uplift/evidence/cdp.mjs` and ensure await census rules in `tests/regression.mjs` remain satisfied.

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] Installer follows pre-existing destination symlinks when writing into target project
description:
## What
The installer skips source symlinks during directory walks, but does not validate destination paths before writing files or creating directories in the target project.

## Location & Evidence
- `bin/web-uplift.mjs:352,355,379` (`applyStep` and `copyDir`)
- `copyDir()` uses `lstatSync` on the source tree (line 373) and skips source symlinks (web-uplift-z34), but writes to `dst` via `copyFileSync(src, dst)` without checking if `dst` is an existing symlink.
- In `applyStep()`, `copy-file` and `write` actions invoke `mkdirSync(dirname(step.to), { recursive: true })` and write with `copyFileSync(step.from, step.to)` or `writeFileSync(step.to, step.content)`.
- Node's `copyFileSync` and `writeFileSync` follow destination symlinks with `O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`.

## Mechanism & Impact
When an operator runs `web-uplift install` or `web-uplift update` in an untrusted checkout (where `--target` defaults to cwd), an attacker can pre-plant symlinks at expected destination paths (such as `.claude/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md`, `.web-uplift/manifest.json`, or files under `.web-uplift/schema/`) pointing to arbitrary files writable by the operator (e.g. `~/.bashrc` or `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`). The installer follows the symlinks and truncates/overwrites the target with fixed tool content (CWE-59 / CWE-62 file clobbering).

## Station Citation & Severity Rationale
- Station: `threat-model` (`tm-install-destination-symlink`), verified by `vuln-verify` and triaged by `vuln-triage`. Run: 20261010T031848Z, target `origin/master@5eb6b44`.
- Severity: Station rated low / routing critical. Mapped to P2 bug. Bounded to file clobbering with fixed content and requires installation into an untrusted checkout.

## Remediation
Reject destination symlinks before writing: check `lstatSync(dst)` on destination paths and refuse/unlink if symbolic; open files with `O_NOFOLLOW` or verify `realpath` stays within the project target root. Add a regression test in `tests/install-copy-symlink.mjs`.

title: pipe transport never rejects pending sends when fd 4 closes, so a mid-audit Chrome crash hangs callers with no deadline
description:
Found by the claude-opus-5-5 review of fleet/pipe-default-fixes @ 5da2310 as the GENERAL case of web-uplift-xnte, whose specific instance (the readiness wait) is fixed there.

DEFECT: createPipeTransport in evidence/cdp.mjs handles only 'data' and 'error' on the fromChrome stream. It never rejects the promises in its pending-send map when fd 4 closes or Chrome exits. chrome-remote-interface rejects them (node_modules/chrome-remote-interface/lib/chrome.js:254-258), and the port path fails fast on a dead browser, so the pipe is strictly worse than the transport it replaces for every call after launch.

WHY IT MATTERS: the readiness wait is bounded only because xnte made it race process exit. Every other send is bounded only by whatever deadline its CALLER passes, and the census's excluded:primitive-probe sites pass none. So a Chrome crash mid-audit hangs the audit on the pipe where the port path would have failed.

PROOF: under the reviewer's M1 mutation the pending send did not settle even after the fake browser exited at 30s.

SMALLEST FIX: when fromChrome emits 'close', reject every pending send with a clear error and mark the transport closed so later sends fail immediately instead of queueing forever.
close_reason: Closed

title: credential leak: a tab, LF or CR ends a swept run, so the tail of a URL userinfo survives in audit artifacts
description:
Found by the round-4 review of the 73y3 sweep as a PRE-EXISTING P2, and fixed on fleet/sweep-hardening @ c2682e1 rather than only tracked.

DEFECT: a URL parser strips tab, LF and CR ANYWHERE in the input, so an authority continues across them. SWEEP_RUN_BREAKS in evidence/credential-terms.mjs treated all three as run breaks, so a run stopped there, the fragment after it had no '@' left to make it userinfo, and it was copied out verbatim. A URL with a tab inside its userinfo therefore printed the tail of the password into evidence artifacts.

REACH: evidence/cli.mjs redactHeaderList, where an internal tab is a legal character in an HTTP field value, and CLI failure URLs. Console prose already splits at whitespace before the sweep sees it, which is why this was not caught earlier.

FIX: remove tab, LF and CR from the break set, so a run spans them exactly as the parser does. The price is over-redaction when a tab or newline precedes an '@' later in the same unparseable string, which is the safe direction. Three assertions (tab inside the userinfo, tab before the password, newline after the URL) plus a control that a tab in an unparseable string with no credential changes nothing. Mutation-proven: with tab put back into the break set the first assertion fires with the password visible in its own message.

title: headers() timeout under load reports headers missing - false audit findings and flaky full gate
description: headers() in evidence/cli.mjs (soon evidence/primitives/headers.mjs after web-uplift-ypds) waits for Network.responseReceived with a docPromise timeout of (opts.wait||5000)+3000, and the regression test passes wait:400 so the budget is 3400ms. Under heavy CPU load (full gate), the two-step navigate() plus event dispatch can exceed that, docPromise resolves null, respHeaders stays {}, and every security header is reported {"present":false,...,"issues":["missing"]}. Observed: full-gate FAIL on testHeadersPrimitiveFindsHeadersRegardlessOfNameCase for tree 4240079f (web-uplift-2gdo union), while the same test passed 4/4 on master AND 4/4 on the tip in isolation (worker classification, 2026-10-10). Two harms: (a) false GATE FAILs that stall landings; (b) worse, a slow browser makes a real audit report headers as MISSING -> false security findings. Fix: make headers() robust to a slow response - extend/scale the wait budget under load and/or retry the response wait, and prove it with a timing/mutation case, not just the happy path. Must be based on the post-ypds split structure to avoid conflicting with the queued evidence stack.
close_reason: Closed

title: [evidence] a credential in URL userinfo is never redacted by either branch of redactUrlCredentialValues
description:
Found while fixing web-uplift-53o1 (fleet/redact-proto-relative-fix, 2026-10-09), pre-existing and out of that bead's scope.

Repro (no browser):
  node -e "import('/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-mwg-drift/evidence/credential-terms.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.redactUrlCredentialValues('https://user:s3cr3t@example.test/a?token=NOPE')))"
Observed: https://user:s3cr3t@example.test/a?token=%5Bredacted%5D  - the query parameter is redacted and the password in userinfo is NOT.

Why it matters: redactUrlCredentialValues is the artifact redactor. evidence/cli.mjs applies it to redirect Location headers (several call sites) and to HAR entry URLs, and since web-uplift-lsn3 the console-evidence prose path uses it too. A URL with basic-auth userinfo therefore writes that password into reports/, evidence-out/ and the run log - the same artifacts this function exists to make safe to share, and the same class the tool already redacts as the Authorization header.

Note this is a deliberate scope boundary today, not an oversight: the function's own comment says it is a CREDENTIAL-scoped redactor that does not start rewriting fields the review never asked it to touch, and userinfo is not a query parameter. So the decision needed is whether userinfo joins the scope (redact the password, keep the username, keep the shape) or whether it stays out and the boundary is documented where the artifacts are described.

Smallest fix if it joins: in both branches, when u.password is non-empty, replace it with [redacted] before serialising (the absolute branch via URL.toString() after setting u.password, the relative branch in the rebuild), plus a test asserting the username and host survive.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW PASS 1 (antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro) on 1c67ea4: REQUEST CHANGES / BLOCK - two P1 LEAKS and a P2 policy finding. I reproduced all three before touching anything, and the first P1 is the reason the scope decision needs one adjustment, which I have made and am flagging rather than burying.

P1a - the username heuristic leaked real API keys. It kept a username unless isCredentialName or looksLikeToken accepted it, and BOTH answer false for real prefixes. Measured: ghp_REDACTED, sk_live_REDACTED, AKIA_REDACTED and glpat_REDACTED all return false for both tests. So 'https://ghp_<PAT>@github.com/' came back with the PAT intact, and 'https://<PAT>:x-oauth-basic@github.com/' kept the token and redacted only the password. A token used AS the username is a standard shape, and a heuristic that needs extending per vendor is a leak per vendor.

P1b - a URL the parser REJECTS was returned verbatim, credential included. Node and Chrome reject 'file://user:pass@/path', so both parse attempts failed and the raw string came back. Wider than reported: an authority whose ':' is read as an invalid port throws as well, so 'https://AKIA_REDACTED:AWS_SECRET_REDACTED@x.test/' leaked too. I found that one while measuring the first, not in the review.

SCOPE DECISION ADJUSTED, deliberately, and this is the part I want on the record: your instruction was "keep the username unless it is itself credential-shaped; if in doubt, redact the whole userinfo and say so". The review is a concrete demonstration that the "credential-shaped" judgement CANNOT be made here, so I am taking the in-doubt branch: the WHOLE userinfo is redacted whenever there is one, no shape judgement at all. That also resolves the review's P2 (policy split), because the flow recorder's sanitizeNavUrl already redacts userinfo unconditionally - the split is gone rather than documented. If you would rather keep the short username readable and accept the leak surface, say so and I will revert to the heuristic with the token shapes explicitly allowlisted, but I do not recommend it: the artifact makes no promise that a username is meaningful and does promise not to carry credentials. Each half is replaced only when it was there, so '//:pass@host' is not given a fabricated username (5m9f's shape is preserved and this branch is stacked on 5m9f so the two compose).

P1b's fix: the unparseable path now sweeps the userinfo in place, so every other character survives and an unparseable string with NO userinfo is still returned untouched (asserted, along with innocent prose containing '//' and '@'). It is not a blanket rewrite of the value.

The review's other finding was tests: the old "token-shaped username" assertion used a 40-character hex string, which is exactly what looksLikeToken was written to accept, so it proved the heuristic worked on itself. The tests now use real token SHAPES as the username and as a username-only userinfo, plus the file: and invalid-port shapes, plus controls.

FIX: fleet/redact-userinfo-hardening @ dcafbb0, stacked on fdf7880 (5m9f, untouched). Re-review dispatched (qwen3.8-max, a fresh family). Per your discipline I am NOT putting merge-queue on this bead yet: the reviewed sha 1c67ea4 is BLOCKED, and I will queue dcafbb0 when the re-review HOLDS, or move the tip to a new branch and mark dcafbb0 do-not-land if it does not.

Two things worth more than an apology. First, my own mutation runs caught the same behaviours, which means my pre-hand-off evidence was not strong enough to see this - the mutations I wrote tested the code I had written, not the policy I had chosen, and the policy is what leaked. Second, a FABRICATED sk_live_ fixture made GitHub push protection reject the push for a secret that does not exist. I did not allowlist it or use the unblock URL; the fixture now uses Stripe's TEST-mode prefix, so no fake is allowlisted. Fleet lesson, since every lane will hit it: secret-shaped fixtures belong behind a test-mode prefix on this repo, or the push is declined.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW OF THE REVIEWED TIP FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN IT, AND BOTH ARE IN A LINE I ADDED. Fixed on a NEW branch so the reviewed sha stays frozen: fleet/redact-userinfo-sweep @ 5385cb6, stacked on dcafbb0 (which stays as it is, and is contained in the new tip - nothing to un-land).

- P1, QUADRATIC. My sweep was one regex over every '//' reaching forward for an '@', and in a run of '/' every adjacent pair matches '//', so the scan restarted at every position. Reproduced on that tree: 213ms at 10kB, 854ms at 20kB, 2820ms at 40kB. The input is the AUDITED SITE's and the path is every response header value and every console line, so a page could hang the audit. Now a single forward pass that consumes each run whether or not it held an '@': 40kB in 3ms, and the cost is flat rather than quadratic.
- P2, LAST-@. The sweep stopped at the FIRST '@', but a URL parser ends the userinfo at the LAST one, so a password containing a raw '@' kept its tail in the artifact. Now the userinfo is read up to the last '@'.
- P3s taken: an empty username no longer gains a fabricated marker in the sweep (it matches the shape 5m9f established for the parseable path), and a backslash authority keeps its host instead of being reduced to a path.
- P3s filed rather than silently widened: web-uplift-k99c covers a special-scheme URL with no slashes after the colon (indistinguishable from an opaque path in a string that already failed to parse, and a mailto address is the everyday case) and the pre-existing nested-URL-in-a-query-value leak.

THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING, and it is the same class as the prose scanner finding one bead earlier (lsn3): I wrote an unbounded forward scan in the catch branch of the very function whose sibling scanner had already been reviewed for exactly that. The lesson did not transfer between two functions in one file. It is now enforced by a test and not by my memory.

AND THE TEST FOR IT WAS A PLACEBO AT FIRST, which I only know because I mutated for it instead of trusting it. My first version asserted an absolute millisecond bound; a shape-identical quadratic PASSED it, because V8 vectorises the character search and 8e8 byte-scans finish inside a second. It is now a SCALING assertion (4x the input must not cost 8x the work, minimum of three runs, so a loaded VM cannot make it flake). Verified in both directions: three consecutive runs pass on the fix, and restoring the quadratic fails it at 11.3x and at 16.0x. A timing test that has not itself been mutation-tested is decoration, and I would have shipped this one as decoration.

Mutations run, each restored byte-identically (md5 f0b171c6450ec78f280e1592609b8fe1): restore the old regex -> the exact-shape assertion fires; first-@ instead of last -> the raw-@ assertion fires; fabricate the empty username -> that assertion fires; drop the backslash authority -> the host assertion fires; shape-identical quadratic -> the scaling assertion fires.

Evidence: tests/credential-redaction.mjs OK (section 9 is the new coverage, with exact-shape asserts and controls), tests/log-redaction.mjs OK, tests/console-evidence-redaction.mjs OK, tests/secrets-coverage.mjs OK, tests/flow.mjs OK, and the vendored tree resynced at all 23 copies identical.

LANDING NOTE, and this matters for the queue: this branch is a deliberate STACK. Its merge-base is e3520f8, not current origin/master, because the fix sits on top of 5m9f (fleet/redact-empty-username @ fdf7880, already queued) and on the 73y3 hardening. The sweep branch CONTAINS dcafbb0 and fdf7880, so landing fleet/redact-userinfo-sweep @ 5385cb6 lands the whole cluster in the right order; landing dcafbb0 alone would ship the quadratic. I have not put merge-queue on 73y3 yet - the re-review of 5385cb6 is running with a fresh family, and I will queue it on the verdict.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
SECOND REVIEW ROUND OF THE SWEEP FOUND TWO MORE P1s IN MY WORK, both reproduced and both fixed on fleet/userinfo-sweep-linear @ 85873dc, which is contained in the landing tip (see below).

- A REAL LEAK, and a stupid one: the backslash delimiter literal was written with two backslashes in the SOURCE FILE, which JavaScript reads as ONE. Because a run starts at the delimiter's second character, a single-backslash authority consumed the first character of the userinfo and printed it: a string like https: backslash admin@x.test:99999/p came back with the first character of the credential visible in the artifact. Four backslashes in the source, i.e. two in the string, is the spelling that works.
- A SECOND QUADRATIC, by a different route than the first: the sweep located BOTH authority spellings with indexOf inside every iteration and each search restarted from the cursor, so a string repeating the authority start with no backslash re-scanned to the end once per start - 6ms at 40kB, 58ms at 160kB, 949ms at 640kB. Both searches are now located once and reused until the cursor passes them.

THE TEST LESSON, which is now three times in two beads and is the thing I would want read out of this record: my scaling fixture used a single run with ONE authority start, so the loop executed exactly once and was structurally BLIND to a quadratic that comes from re-searching for the spelling that does not occur. There are now two scaling fixtures, one single-start and one repeating the start, because each is blind to the other's failure. And I verified the new one is not decoration with a mutation that is OUTPUT-IDENTICAL and only slower - it fires at 11.0x. A correctness assertion cannot catch a complexity defect, and a fixture that never runs the loop's second iteration cannot either.

Honest note on mutation naming: for the backslash literal the assertion that fires is the one named 'one backslash is a boundary, not a delimiter', not the two-backslash case, because with the wrong literal the two-backslash input happens to come out right and the single-backslash one is what gets mangled. The assertion name says what it really checks.

LANDING: the fold means the branch for this bead is the same one as the rest of the chain - fleet/chain-await-census @ b12a169 (X), which contains 4rv, lsn3, 53o1, this bead, 5m9f, the hardening and the sweep fixes, plus the census fix as the newest commit. 85873dc, 5385cb6 and dcafbb0 are all contained in it and must not be landed on their own.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
THIRD REVIEW ROUND: REQUEST CHANGES, and it found a REGRESSION I INTRODUCED. Fixed on the chain branch; new landing tip below.

The regression: by searching for '//' and for two backslashes SEPARATELY, I made the MIXED pairs (backslash-then-slash and slash-then-backslash) match neither, so a URL using one of them came back VERBATIM with its password - worse than the version before my fix, whose single-backslash search had redacted those by accident. A special-scheme URL parser reads ANY pair from the slash-or-backslash class as the start of an authority, which is why those forms are authorities at all. The reviewer found this by tracing the parser by hand, not by running anything, which is worth recording: no amount of my own test-running would have produced it, because my tests only covered the spellings I had thought of.

THE FIX: ONE search over the whole class (/[\\/]{2}/g with lastIndex at the cursor), reused until the cursor passes it. That closes the mixed pairs AND removes the class of defect behind both earlier quadratics, because with a single search there is no second spelling left to re-search. Verified the caching is equivalent rather than plausible: the reviewer's own differential against a naive scan-every-position reference, with the reference updated to this change's spec, covered every string up to length 8 over ['/', backslash, '@', ':', ' ', '?', 'a'] - 6,725,600 strings - with ZERO disagreements.

Tests: three mixed-spelling assertions (both orders and the protocol-relative form); the scaling fixture now alternates BOTH spellings and runs at 160kB/640kB instead of 40/160, because the defect it guards measured 9.1x against an 8x bound at the smaller pair, a margin too thin to trust; and a comment that credited the wrong assertion is corrected - the two-backslash assertion passes even under the defective single-backslash search, and the ONE-backslash assertion is what pinned that defect.

Mutation results, honestly: keeping '//' and two backslashes but losing the mixed pairs fires the new mixed assertion with the password visible in its message, which is the regression's signature. Re-searching on every iteration, which is output-identical, does NOT fail - and that is the honest reading: with a single search the re-search is still linear, so the quadratic class is structurally gone rather than merely guarded by a timing bound. The timing test stays as a guard against a future multi-search design.

Two boundaries from the same review are filed on web-uplift-k99c rather than quietly widened: a special-scheme URL with zero or one slash-or-backslash before its userinfo is still unswept (it needs a scheme-aware anchor, and the prose scanner never hands those forms to the sweep), and the sweep stops a run at tab/LF/CR where the URL parser removes them anywhere.

LANDING: new tip = fleet/chain-await-census @ a2637f3. It supersedes 1b78325, b12a169 and f2037f2, none of which should be landed. Verified on it: credential-redaction OK (with the new mixed assertions), log-redaction OK, console-evidence-redaction OK, secrets-coverage OK, flow OK, --only AwaitCensus OK, vendored 23/23 identical, and the differential above. Round 4 verification is dispatched and X stays unqueued until it holds. j3re is rebased onto the chain tip at 7859759 with its census counts updated and every browser suite green.

IT CORRECTED A CLAIM OF MINE, which is the most valuable thing in the review. The caching code never hits its cache: cursor is set to end, end is always at least next+2, so the guard "next < cursor" is always false and findAuthority() runs on every iteration. A cached -1 is never reused either. Linearity therefore holds BY CONSTRUCTION - the reviewer's words are "the quadratic is gone by construction, not just guarded against" - which is exactly why the output-identical re-search mutation could not fail: that mutant IS the current code. My BEHAVIOURAL conclusion was right and my MECHANISM claim was wrong, and worse, the code comments assert a reuse that does not happen, which is a false statement about a security property. MY OTHER WRONG CLAIM, in the previous commit message: I raised the scaling fixture sizes because the defect measured 9.1x against an 8x bound at the smaller pair and the margin was too thin. The reviewer timed it: at the NEW sizes the two-spelling mutant measures 2.3x and PASSES, because both spellings occur close together so re-searching each one stays cheap. So increasing the size made that fixture less sensitive to the original defect, not more. The alternating fixture does catch a plausible future regression (a per-spelling search covering all four pairs and re-searching each pass takes 36s at the small size alone), and the ORIGINAL defect is pinned by the mixed-spelling correctness assertions, because a two-spelling search structurally cannot redact a mixed pair. Reach is redactHeaderList (an internal tab is legal in an HTTP field value) and CLI failure URLs; console prose already splits at whitespace. Its smallest fix is two lines - remove '\t', '\n', '\r' from the break set and add one assertion - and it notes the behaviour proves the authority genuinely continues across the tab. That is boundary (2) on web-uplift-k99c, which I filed as needing a bigger change; the reviewer's read is that it is cheap, and I agree after re-reading it.

description:

title: (BUG) console evidence persists a failed subresource request URL verbatim, credential query included (evidence/cdp.mjs attachConsoleEvidence)
description:
Found while fixing web-uplift-6fe (fleet/findings-redaction, 2026-10-09).

Repro (real browser, run from the worktree):
  node /tmp/mwg-secrets-repro5.mjs   # fixture: a page whose <script src="/missing.js?api_key=NOTAREALKEY_FIXTURE_URLQUERY1234567890"> 404s
Observed: the secrets artifact's console block contains
  {"kind":"log","level":"error","source":"network","text":"Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)","url":"http://127.0.0.1:<port>/missing.js?api_key=NOTAREALKEY_FIXTURE_URLQUERY1234567890"}
i.e. JSON.stringify(result) still contains the credential string. The 6fe fix redacted externalScriptFailures[].url, so the failure list is clean; the console entry is a DIFFERENT surface.

Cause: attachConsoleEvidence/attachConsoleCollector (evidence/cdp.mjs) copies the CDP Log entry url (and Network request urls) into the artifact with no credential redaction. Every primitive emits this block, so a page-derived credential in any request URL lands in every artifact written to disk (reports/, evidence-out/).

Expected: a page-derived URL that reaches an artifact goes through the same credential redaction the HAR path and the flow recorder use (evidence/credential-terms.mjs isCredentialName / evidence/cli.mjs redactUrlCredentialValues).

Scope note: cdp.mjs documents itself as a GENERIC harness that makes no judgements, and it is vendored into .web-uplift/evidence/, so the host rules (and whether redaction belongs in cdp.mjs or at the attachConsoleEvidence call sites in cli.mjs) are the placement question. Also check whether the exception/console TEXT can carry a URL (a bare-URL redactor cannot rewrite a URL embedded in prose, so decide whether text needs its own handling).

Evidence: /tmp/mwg-secrets-repro5.mjs output (console.entries[].url), commit f078d16 note, reviewer finding on web-uplift-6fe.

comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/lsn3-console-redaction @ c813f059, stacked on the 4rv tip a4cd289 as coord asked (so the four 4rv commits are in this branch by construction and land with it). Merge-base with origin/master is still e3520f8.

REPRODUCED FIRST, real browser (node /tmp/lsn3-repro.mjs - a page whose <script src="/missing.js?api_key=..."> 404s):
  before: "leaks query credential true" while "redacted in failure url true" - i.e. the failure list was clean and the artifact still carried the credential, through
  {"kind":"log","level":"error","source":"network","text":"Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)","url":"http://127.0.0.1:<port>/missing.js?api_key=NOTAREALKEY_FIXTURE_URLQUERY1234567890"}
  after:  the same run prints false, and the entry reads "url":".../missing.js?api_key=%5Bredacted%5D" with "repeat":2 (the retry still collapses), every other parameter and the diagnostic text intact.

WHY THE PLACEMENT (the question the bead flagged): cdp.mjs is documented as a generic harness and is imported BY cli.mjs, so it cannot import cli.mjs - the choice was a second copy of the redaction rule or moving the rule to the shared module. A second copy is exactly how this class of leak happened twice (6fe redacted one field, this one was missed), so the URL redactor and the redacted literal moved into evidence/credential-terms.mjs, where the HAR redactor's own comment already says the shared vocabularies live, and cli.mjs re-exports the function so every existing importer keeps working. The redaction then sits in attachConsoleCollector's record(), the single point the three entry paths (console, exception, browser log) converge on, so no caller can forget it - not the four primitives, not run-batch, not the fixer.

THREE SURFACES, because a URL field is not the only one:
1. url: redactUrlCredentialValues on the entry.
2. stack: the frame's url is redacted where the frame string is BUILT, because sweeping "fn (url:line:column)" as text would swallow the line and column.
3. text: a page that logs location.href puts a URL in prose, where no field-shaped redactor can see it, so a new redactUrlsInText rewrites absolute and protocol-relative URLs inside a string. It holds back trailing prose punctuation ("see https://x/a?token=SECRET, then stop.") so sentences are not mangled.
Dedupe runs on the REDACTED key, so a retry loop still collapses to one entry with a repeat count.

STATED BOUNDARIES, not left implied: the text matcher covers absolute and protocol-relative URLs, so a bare relative path inside prose ('/api/send?access_token=...') is not rewritten by it, and a credential with no URL around it is the secrets scanner's job. Redaction is by credential-named QUERY PARAMETER (the shared rule), so a credential embedded in a PATH segment is out of scope for this redactor. Both are in the test file's header.

TEST: tests/console-evidence-redaction.mjs (new, registered in tests/regression.mjs ALL_TESTS so `regression.mjs Console` runs it): the shared redactor's contract, then all three entry paths through the collector with a CDP client stand-in - a failed subresource twice (dedupe), an exception whose url and stack frame both carry a credential, a console error whose TEXT carries one, the innocents that must survive (a non-credential parameter, a URL with no query, a relative URL), the frame's line and column, idempotence over an already-redacted artifact, per-session isolation, and attachConsoleEvidence's existing contract. Mutation: removing the redaction fails on "NO console entry may carry a credential value"; dropping only the text sweep fails the same way - so the prose half is asserted, not merely commented. Both restored byte-identically by md5.
Also measured, not assumed: the text matcher's first version used \b before the scheme and silently matched NO protocol-relative URL at all - my own test caught that, which is why the assertion set includes that case.

SEPARATE FINDING, filed rather than folded in: web-uplift-53o1 [P3] - the moved redactor re-emits a protocol-relative input ('//host/path?x=1') as '/path?x=1', dropping the host. Pre-existing, not a credential leak, and I kept it out of this delta on purpose.

REVIEW: dispatched to an independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol) on the pinned delta; the verdict will be added here when it returns.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: console evidence (evidence/cdp.mjs attachConsoleCollector, the block every primitive attaches to its result) now redacts credentials at the one point its entries are built: url fields through redactUrlCredentialValues, a stack frame's url where the frame is built, and entry text through a new redactUrlsInText for a URL a page logged as prose. The shared URL redactor moved from evidence/cli.mjs into evidence/credential-terms.mjs (cli.mjs re-exports it) so the console path and the HAR path cannot drift, and tests/console-evidence-redaction.mjs covers all three entry paths plus the innocents and the dedupe behaviour, registered in ALL_TESTS.
WHY: a page-derived credential in any request URL was copied verbatim into every artifact (reports/, evidence-out/, the run log) by the console block, while the externalScriptFailures entry for the same request was already redacted - one surface was fixed and the sibling was missed.
EFFECT: a credential in a failed subresource URL, an exception URL, a stack frame URL or a page-logged URL no longer reaches disk, while the parameter name, the other parameters, the diagnostic text and the frame's line/column survive so the evidence stays useful.

title: [perf-review] waitForElement polling is inherently sequential, not a parallelizable waterfall
description:
This is the waitForElement step implementation: it polls pageAction every 250ms up to 20 times and breaks as soon as the element appears. Each poll must observe the state produced by the previous one, so the awaits are dependent and cannot be parallelized; firing 20 concurrent checks would defeat the purpose. It is a bounded (max 5s) deliberate poll on the flow-runner path, not independent network I/O.

comments.author: web-uplift-rev-2
comments.text:
LANDED REPRODUCTION (weekly review web-uplift-fio, reviewer lane rev-2, 2026-10-09; post-landing follow-up).

The hazard this bead names already materialized on master this week: a one-sided fix landed the source copy and not the vendored one, and the merge gate never runs the guard that catches it.

Measured on the current tree (origin/master f83372c, rev-2 worktree):
- `fleet-check --status 5a4fa73` -> PASS, cmd "npm test". `cat ~/.fleet/check.conf` -> CHECK_CMD="npm test", no CHECK_FAST_CMD.
- `grep -n cdp-copy-sync tests/regression.mjs` -> two COMMENTS only (4140, 6271); the guard is never spawned or imported by the gate. It runs only from .github/workflows/cdp-copy-sync.yml, i.e. post-push, not at land time. Same shape for tests/changelog-version-check.mjs (0 references in regression.mjs).
- The drift landed: 09d52f2 ("chore(runner): refuse --resume in unisolated batches") and 985ef46 ("docs(runner): disclose isolated resume pointer trust") edited runner/run-batch.mjs + runner/README.md without the .web-uplift/ copies. At 985ef46 the vendored runner/run-batch.mjs was 35219 bytes vs source 35918, and it was missing exactly the landed refusal of `--resume` with `--i-know-this-is-unisolated` (the REFUSED block at source line ~120) and the matching README disclaimer. Repaired only by the later follow-up commit 196c8a6 ("chore(runner): sync vendored mirrors").

Exact repro (no edits; detached worktree under /tmp):
  git worktree add --detach /tmp/drift 985ef46
  cd /tmp/drift && node tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs ; echo $?   # -> exit 1, "2 of 22 vendored copies have drifted"
  grep -c cdp-copy-sync tests/regression.mjs                # -> 2 (comments only)

Consequence: the committed in-repo .web-uplift/ tree is what this repo's own in-session agents are told to run (AGENTS.md: `node .web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs`), so for two master commits the agent path carried a runner without a just-landed safety refusal. CI catches it only after master already has the stale tree.

One next action: run the byte guard in the gate (drive tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs from tests/regression.mjs, as that file already does for skill-write-contract.mjs). It is pure Node builtins, ~1s, no `npm install`, so it costs nothing at land time and closes the window. web-uplift-emv deferred local wiring on 2026-10-05 as "optional" because CI runs; that decision predates the landed drift above.

Fix owner: an implementer lane (test-gate change, 3 lines in tests/regression.mjs).

comments.author: web-uplift-factory
comments.text:
DESIGN DIRECTION EVALUATION (response to coord on web-uplift-zeu4 / web-uplift-diaq):

We choose option (b): Keep the test guard as an essential safety net alongside future generation.

Reasons:
1. Immediate safety without collision: Two workers currently have active, in-flight edits under .web-uplift/ (worker A on runner/flow-record.mjs, worker B on evidence/cli.mjs). Attempting to gitignore and delete .web-uplift/ now (diaq) would collide with their worktrees or clobber uncommitted edits. The guard in 6ha1 is non-destructive, touches none of their four files, and secures the repo against one-sided drift immediately.
2. Verification of generation: When diaq lands postinstall/prepare generation, the guard in tests/regression.mjs serves as the verification step in CI to prove that generation actually executed and produced 100% byte-identical mirrors.
3. Non-.web-uplift tracked mirrors: install-surface.mjs also tracks .claude/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md -> .pi/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md, which is committed to version control so Pi agents can load the skill. That mirror is outside .web-uplift/ and cannot be gitignored; the guard verifies it.
4. Zero overhead: The guard runs pure Node builtins in ~0.2s and adds no dependencies.

Branch fleet/6ha1-sync-guard @ a190ca5 is ready to land.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text:
VERDICT: PASS (independent review lane; I executed the guard and the focused tests, not just read the diff).

DELTA PINNED: e3520f8..a190ca5. tip a190ca5, tree 8ce19f2e43f4a555b640dc1ef92d230fd804eb62.
origin/master == e3520f81601f751b22a608e9150e994a19738072 at review time, so the pinned base is
current. Diff is 4 files: AGENTS.md +6, package.json +1 ("sync:vendored"), tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs
+123/-15, tests/regression.mjs +46. No .web-uplift/** path and no canonical runtime file touched.

METHOD: scratch detached worktree `git worktree add --detach /tmp/rev6ha1 a190ca5` (main checkout
untouched, worktree removed afterwards). Branch ref still a190ca5; no branch edits made.

WHAT IT COMPARES (read from the diff): pairs come from install-surface.mjs, the same module the
installer reads, so COPY_DIRS = VENDORED_DIRS (evidence, aggregate, runner, schema) walked
recursively and COPY_FILES = VENDORED_FILES + TRACKED_COPY_FILES. Byte equality is sameBytes() over
Uint8Array (not text), and missing/unreadable are distinct states. The clean run enumerates 23
pairs == 22 tracked .web-uplift files (manifest.json excluded by design: written at install time
with a fresh timestamp) + the .pi mirror. The file set is dynamic (union of walkDir keys on both
sides), so a file added on only one side is a failure, not an omission.

EXACT COMMANDS AND RESULTS (/tmp/rev6ha1):
1. clean tree: `timeout -k 30 300 node tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs` -> exit 0, "all 23 vendored copies identical".
2. canonical drift: `printf '\n// drift probe\n' >> evidence/cli.mjs` then the guard -> exit 1,
   "1 of 23 vendored copies have drifted" plus the sha256s and a unified diff. Revert -> exit 0.
3. vendored drift (the bead's actual mode): append to .web-uplift/runner/run-batch.mjs -> exit 1
   "vendored copy has drifted from its source"; `rm runner/remaining-work.mjs` -> exit 1 "source is
   missing"; `rm .web-uplift/runner/flow.mjs` -> exit 1 "vendored copy is missing"; a file present
   only in evidence/ -> exit 1. All reverted, guard clean again.
4. non-.web-uplift mirror: clean run prints ".claude/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md == .pi/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md"
   (no false positive), and appending one line to .pi/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md -> exit 1 (really
   covered). .codex/skills/web-audit is a symlink to .claude and is correctly not compared.
5. gate teeth: with .web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs drifted, `timeout -k 30 300 node tests/regression.mjs
   --only CdpCopySync` FAILS inside testCdpCopySyncGuard (tests/regression.mjs:4218-4222); clean tree
   -> "ran 2/117 tests matching [CdpCopySync]: OK", exit 0. Mutating the guard so sameBytes() returns
   true makes testCdpCopySyncMutationGuard fail, so the new test is not vacuous.
6. resync safety: `node tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs --sync` on a canonical-drift tree exits 0, prints the
   drift report (unified diff) to stderr first, then names every file and direction
   ("synced: evidence/cli.mjs -> .web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs"); re-guard clean. A vendored-only
   orphan (source side missing) is refused with exit 1 instead of being deleted, so it cannot
   one-sided-overwrite silently. `--from-vendored` restores the canonical side from the vendored copy.

FINDING (filed as a review-finding bead, P3, not a blocker): `--dry-run` exits 0 on a drifted tree
even though the file's header states "Exit 0 when every pair is identical, 1 when any differ or one
side is missing" (tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs:21 vs the dry-run branch at :154-158). No in-repo caller
uses --dry-run today, so impact is a future false green if anyone wires it as a check.

OBSERVATION (no bead; pre-existing code unchanged by this diff): walkDir() uses statSync (follows
symlinks) with no depth cap, while the installer's copyDir() uses lstatSync (skips symlinks) with a
depth cap of 64. A symlink-dir cycle inside evidence|aggregate|runner|schema makes the guard crash on
ELOOP instead of reporting drift (proven in an isolated /tmp fixture with --repo). It still exits
non-zero, so it fails safe.

UNVERIFIED (not executed, by instruction or scope): full `npm test`; `npm run test:fast` beyond
--dry-run (its cached fleet-check verdict was not re-created); the historical incident commits
09d52f2/985ef46 were not re-checked.

No blockers. Merge verdict: OK with the P3 notes above.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW on fleet/flow-record-injection @ 9169919 (merge-base origin/master = 7517ce2; 2 commits: 25ff984, 9169919). P2.

REPRO FIRST (real browser, /tmp/mwg-sg5-repro.mjs: one page that attacks the recording channel, then real trusted input driven through CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent so the operator's own gestures are real). Round 1 (the bead's original finding) at the pre-fix tree: the page called the page-global `__wuRecordStep` and its navigate step to https://evil.example/collect?api_key=ATTACKER_KEY_123, its change step for #pwd and its `__done` all reached flow.json.
Round 2, after an independent review broke the first fix (reviewer on 25ff984, REQUEST CHANGES): the page hooks the PAGE-GLOBAL JSON.stringify and forges with whatever token it catches, and it dispatches synthetic events. On the reviewed tip 25ff984 the SAME page: page could SEE the binding = function; token stolen = YES; forged a step with the stolen token = YES; that forgery PERSISTED in flow.json = YES; a synthetic click on a "Delete my account" button was recorded = YES; 14 steps recorded against 5 legitimate. On 9169919: page can see the binding = undefined; no theft; no forgery; no synthetic step; 5 steps recorded (setViewport, navigate, click, change, click) with the typed password change at `value: "" redacted: true`. A trusted typed change is still recorded, which is the proof that the isTrusted check cannot pass by breaking recording.

FIX (four layers, each one making a different attack unreachable):
- ISOLATION: the emitter is injected with `worldName: RECORDER_WORLD` and the binding is added with `executionContextName: RECORDER_WORLD`, so the page's own scripts cannot see or call the recording channel at all (mechanism probed in this Chrome build first: the binding is callable from that world, reads the DOM, and `typeof window.__wuProbe` is undefined in the page world).
- TRUST: `if (!e.isTrusted) return;` in the click, change and Done listeners. A page can dispatch events but cannot have them recorded, and cannot end a recording by clicking our overlay. Silent by design (a page can dispatch in a loop; a page-triggered log line is a log flood).
- AUTHENTICITY (kept from round 1): a per-recording token generated in Node, closed over in the injected script, plus this script's own reference to the native JSON.stringify taken before any page script runs.
- SHAPE (kept from round 1): validateRecordedStep rebuilds click/change steps from an allowlist with bounds; refusals are counted, reported and never persisted. Now keyed with Object.hasOwn, because `type: "__proto__"` / `"constructor"` used to resolve to a non-array and throw out of the handler instead of refusing.

REVIEW: independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol; implementer deepseek-flash). Pass 1 on 25ff984: REQUEST CHANGES, BLOCK - the two P1s above plus two P2s (the inherited-property throw, and a test gap: no test passed a really-emitted payload through the Node handler). All four fixed in 9169919. Pass 2 on 9169919: VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues found. It noted that its own browser verification was limited to the artifacts I supplied (my fault in round 1: the TIP artifact I handed it was stale, copied while the worktree was on another branch; regenerated with md5sum matching the live tip).

RESIDUALS the reviewer raised and I am NOT fixing here, for coord to route if wanted: (1) a page can influence the SELECTORS recorded from a genuine interaction, and validation bounds a selector's shape, not what it resolves to at replay time - a pre-existing replay/DOM-drift risk, not a bypass of this channel; (2) a page can remove the overlay, and a recording with no operator Done has no timeout (pre-existing); (3) main-frame navigation steps sit outside the 2,000-step binding cap (pre-existing, and the cap is a page-flood guard, not the recorder's own ceiling).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: runner/flow-record.mjs now runs the capture emitter and its CDP binding in an isolated browser execution world (RECORDER_WORLD) that page scripts cannot see into, records only trusted (user-agent-produced) click/change events including its own Done control, keeps the per-recording token plus a captured native JSON.stringify as a second layer, and refuses any step type or field outside the click/change allowlist (own-key lookup, so `__proto__` and `constructor` refuse instead of throwing). tests/flow.mjs covers synthetic-event refusal, the isolation wiring on both CDP calls, the inherited-type refusals, and feeds a really-emitted click payload through the Node handler.
WHY: a page could add steps the operator never took to flow.json - a navigate step to its own URL or a change step naming a password field and a value - and the operator would then REPLAY them. The first fix (a token in the page world) was bypassable: the emitter had to call the page-global JSON.stringify, so a page that replaced it read the token and forged steps; and the listeners accepted synthetic events, so a page could get its own clicks signed.
EFFECT: recording a journey can no longer be scripted or polluted by the page being recorded: a hostile page's steps, and its attempts to end the recording early, never reach flow.json, while real gestures (click, typing, Done) record exactly as before. An operator whose own harness drives the page programmatically will find those synthetic events are not recorded (documented in the README).

title: mwg-drift-classify --extract to a pipe truncates the corpus at 65536 bytes and still exits 0 (tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs:708-710)
description:

Repro (executed, local, no network):
  mkdir -p /tmp/bigpkg/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/big
  for i in $(seq 1 400); do printf '# g%s\n' "$i" > /tmp/bigpkg/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/big/big-guide-$i.md; done

  node tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs --extract /tmp/bigpkg --version 1.0.0 -o /tmp/big-out.json; wc -c /tmp/big-out.json   # 188941
Observed: the piped output is truncated at exactly the 64 KiB pipe buffer; the same run with -o writes 188941 bytes. -o is documented as optional and stdout is the default destination, so a piped extraction silently emits invalid JSON and exits 0 (process.stdout.write at tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs:708 is followed immediately by process.exit(0) at :710).
Expected: the emitted corpus is complete, or the tool fails loud.
Evidence: tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs:700-711; the byte sizes above. (The truncated artefact does fail loud when it is next parsed, which is why this is P2 and not higher.)

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/mwg-classify-pipe @ bb3cf29 (3 commits, merge-base origin/master = e3520f8; nothing of anyone else's in the delta - 3 files, 269 insertions).

REPRODUCED FIRST, with a package whose corpus is larger than the pipe buffer:
  piped:               131072 bytes, exit 0
  -o /tmp/big-out.json: 232941 bytes
  # the piped JSON did not parse
and the bead's own numbers did not reproduce with its own command: the 400-file fixture in the report emits 24541 bytes here, which is UNDER the buffer and comes through intact, so the truncation the bead attributes to it was measured on a bigger corpus. Same defect, and I sharpened the repro rather than claiming the smaller one failed. The size dependence is the shape of this bug: it only appears once the output outgrows the buffer.

THE SAME DEFECT WAS ONE FUNCTION AWAY, and I measured it rather than reasoning about it: a 12000-guide delta emitted 638339 bytes to a file and exactly 65536 through a pipe, exiting 2. So the classification report and its --json line are fixed too, with the same emitter.

FIX: `writeStdout()` writes every byte to the descriptor synchronously (writeSync in a loop, so a short write is not mistaken for completion) and reports a consumer that goes away instead of swallowing it - `| head` now fails the run with the byte count written, because a corpus nobody received is a failed extraction, not a successful one. `-o` already failed loud (writeFileSync throws EPIPE) and is unchanged.

REVIEW: independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol; implementer deepseek-flash). Pass 1 found something bigger than the bug: my branch had been created from the CDP branch tip instead of master, so the delta I handed over carried three web-uplift-4rv commits. That is a process failure on my side (I trusted the branch creation instead of checking the merge-base) and it is exactly what the review gate is for; the branch was rebuilt onto master and the delta is now three files. Its other findings: EAGAIN on a non-blocking stdout was treated as a broken pipe; the helper and test used Node Buffer, which AGENTS.md forbids ("ESM only; no Node Buffer (use TextEncoder/Uint8Array/atob/btoa)"); the closed-consumer case leaned on scheduling. Pass 2: the stall deadline was absolute rather than per-progress, the classification "baseline" was another pipe rather than a file, and the failure message named the wrong payload. All fixed. Pass 3: VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues.

EAGAIN IS NOW DRIVEN, NOT ARGUED (the reviewer gave the method, and I took it): a small python launcher sets O_NONBLOCK on the WRITE end of a pipe and drains it slowly, so the writer is told EAGAIN many times before its 915 KB corpus is through; the test asserts the run still exits 0 and the bytes are byte-identical to the file-descriptor baseline. Mutation-checked: with the EAGAIN branch disabled that case fails with exit 1, so it is exercising the path rather than passing incidentally. The case prints SKIPPED if python3 is missing, so it cannot pass quietly on a host that cannot run it - the merger's gate host has python3.

MUTATION CHECKS: restoring process.stdout.write() fails the extract case by size (146176 piped vs 915248 with -o) and the classify case by size; each time the fix was restored byte-identically (md5 checked, never `git checkout --` on an uncommitted fix).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs emits its payloads with a synchronous, loop-safe writeStdout() (writeSync over the whole payload, EAGAIN treated as backpressure with a per-progress stall deadline, a broken pipe reported with the byte count and a non-zero exit) instead of process.stdout.write()/console.log() immediately before process.exit(). Both the extracted corpus and the classification report are routed through it. tests/mwg-drift-extract-pipe.mjs (new, wired into the fast gate) generates its own fixtures and pins: piped == file-descriptor bytes and parse, the closed-consumer failure, the classify report through a pipe, and a real non-blocking stdout.
WHY: process.stdout.write()/console.log() to a pipe is not lossless and process.exit() does not wait for it, so piping a payload larger than the pipe buffer silently truncated it while exiting 0 - the tool reported success for output nobody received.
EFFECT: `web-uplift`-style drift extraction and classification can be piped safely: a corpus or report larger than 64 KiB arrives whole (verified byte-identical against a real file descriptor), a consumer that stops reading now fails the run with how many bytes it got, and a slow reader's backpressure is handled instead of being mistaken for a broken pipe.

IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/mwg-basis-floor @ 059fa9c (2 commits, merge-base origin/master = e3520f8, 4 files).

REPRODUCED FIRST, both halves, on the bead's own fixtures:
  $ echo '{"catalogueVersion":"1.0.0","rules":[]}' > /tmp/basis-empty.json
  $ node tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs --verify-basis tests/fixtures/mwg-drift/corpus-old.json --basis /tmp/basis-empty.json

  $ node tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs --old-corpus .../corpus-old.json --new-corpus .../corpus-new-reversal.json --basis /tmp/basis-empty.json
  Delta summary: 0 reversed, 1 changed, 0 new   -  "implemented-rule-guide (guide text modified upstream (no implemented rules))"
  the same classification with tests/fixtures/mwg-drift/basis-fixture.json:

So the empty registry did not merely verify vacuously: it turned a reversal into an ordinary change, exactly as the bead says.

FIX 1: one check in validateBasis, which BOTH entry points already go through (verifyBasisAgainstCorpus and classifyDelta), so it fails loud everywhere:
  FAIL: basis registry file declares no rules: an empty registry verifies nothing and silently disables REVERSED detection, so a reversal would be reported as an ordinary change instead
exit 1 in both modes. A registry whose rules FIELD is missing keeps its own distinct refusal.

FIX 2, found while answering the reviewer's question about other weakened registries, and measured before fixing: a registry whose rule names a guide ABSENT from the baseline fails verification but classification ran on with it and reported "0 reversed, 1 changed" (exit 2) - the same silent loss, one level up, because a rule with no guide in the baseline has no anchors to notice that guide's text moved. The per-rule corpus check is now basisCorpusViolations(basis, corpus), shared by verification and classification, so the two cannot disagree about whether a registry is usable. Classification now exits 1 with "N basis-vs-corpus violation(s)"; verification's message and exit code are unchanged.

ALSO: tests/regression.mjs case 20 iterated basis.rules, so an empty array made every assertion in that loop vacuous; it now asserts the committed registry declares at least one rule before looping.

REVIEW: independent family (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash; implementer deepseek-flash). VERDICT: HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues. It verified the load-bearing question itself - whether an empty registry should verify OK with a warning - and argued fail-closed from this repo's own contract ("a blind check must never exit 0", exit 1 means "classifier is blind or inputs are invalid"), from the severity of a missed reversal (REVERSED is reported first and loudest because a reversed rule generates broken repairs), and from the existing precedent that an empty baseline corpus is refused. It also independently re-derived that both my mutation checks are load-bearing (reverting the empty-rules check fails the verify AND the classify case, the latter on the CHANGED output assertion).

Tests: tests/mwg-drift-basis-floor.mjs (new, registered in the suite and matched by the fast gate's Mwg filter): the control (the fixture registry still verifies and still detects the reversal, so the refusal is not "classification always fails"), the empty-registry refusal in both modes with no classification output, the absent-guide refusal in both modes, and the distinct missing-rules-field refusal. Mutation-checked twice: disabling the empty-rules check fails the test with the old "OK ... 0 rule(s) verified"; disabling the classification-side corpus check fails it with the old exit 2 and "0 reversed, 1 changed"; each fix restored byte-identically (md5 checked). `node tests/regression.mjs Mwg` runs 7 tests: OK.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: tests/mwg-drift-classify.mjs refuses a basis registry that declares no rules (validateBasis, so both --verify-basis and classification fail loud with exit 1 and a message naming the disabled detector), and classification now also refuses the corpus violations verification already refused (basisCorpusViolations, shared by both paths: a registered guide missing from the baseline, or an anchor no longer verbatim in it). tests/mwg-drift-basis-floor.mjs (new) pins all of it; regression case 20 asserts the committed registry declares at least one rule; docs/mwg-drift-check.md now says an empty registry fails loud too.
WHY: a registry with rules:[] verified "OK (0 rule(s) verified)" and removed the tool's only reversal detector, so every reversed guide was re-filed as an ordinary change; the same happened with a rule whose guide was absent from the baseline.
EFFECT: a stale, empty or mis-targeted rule registry can no longer produce a successful-looking drift report with no reversal detection - the run stops with exit 1 and names the violation, so a monitor's green result means the reversals really were checked.

title: secrets primitive counts a failed or timed-out external-script fetch as scanned and swallows the error (evidence/cli.mjs:2768,2779,2787; a39dd3d / web-uplift-61i)
description:

Attribution: git blame shows evidence/cli.mjs lines 2768-2771 are a39dd3d ('cap and deadline the secrets primitive's in-page script fetch', web-uplift-61i).
Observed (code read, against the same file's own doctrine at evidence/cli.mjs:218-224 - "A cap that drops evidence must say so"):
  1. the in-page catch returns { text: '', truncated: false } on a fetch rejection OR when the AbortController deadline fires, and the Node-side loop then does an empty catch - a script that was never read is indistinguishable in the output from a script that read cleanly and found nothing;
  2. the summary reports externalScriptsScanned: scriptUrls.length (:2787, and the announceCap at :2779) - the number of URLs ATTEMPTED, not the number that succeeded, so the reported coverage is an over-claim;

5. Non-exploitability: The path can only be set by the trusted operator on the command line. Because this path is exclusively operator-controlled and cannot be influenced by the page or page-exposed agent, no behaviour change is forced on evidence/cli.mjs.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/cdp-endpoint-guard @ 490fbe6 (rebased onto origin/master = e3520f8; 3 commits; merge-base e3520f8).

NOTE ON THE BEAD BODY: the DESCRIPTION is withheld ("[withheld]"), so I worked from the title and the named path evidence/cdp.mjs:436 - "the DevTools endpoint is exposed for the life of every audit" - and I am recording what I measured rather than what I assumed.

MEASURED FIRST, with the tool's own launch path (/tmp/mwg-4rv-probe.mjs):
  CDP port                        : 44183 (--remote-debugging-port=0, a free port)
  this host non-loopback address  : 10.42.0.42
  loopback connect (127.0.0.1)    : CONNECTED
  non-loopback connect            : refused/error: ECONNREFUSED
  kernel socket entry             : LISTEN 0 0 127.0.0.1:44183 0.0.0.0:*  users:(("chrome",pid=1504478,fd=70))
So Chrome 154 headless ALREADY binds loopback on this VM, and a connection over the host's own non-loopback address is refused. This is a hardening plus a claim-verification, not a live off-host exposure, and I would rather say that plainly than inflate it. The real exposure that remains is local: the endpoint has no authentication at all and stays open for the whole run, so any local process can attach to it. That residual is in the README and cannot be removed without replacing the CDP client transport (see the scope note at the end).

FIX, in evidence/cdp.mjs. The launch pinned nothing (the address was whatever Chrome defaults to, and the default differs by headless mode), so it now passes --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 AND measures the claim two ways, refusing to start rather than exposing an audit:
- FROM THE KERNEL, which is the decisive check: readBoundListeners(pid) reads the browser pid's socket inodes out of /proc/<pid>/fd and the LISTEN rows for those inodes in /proc/net/tcp and /proc/net/tcp6, and the launch fails unless every listener on the port is loopback. It covers IPv4 and IPv6 (including a 0.0.0.0 or :: wildcard), it is attributable to OUR browser rather than to anything else holding that port number, and it does not depend on reachability, firewalls or proxies.
- BY REACHABILITY, when the binding cannot be read (macOS, Windows, no /proc) and as a second opinion: connect to the endpoint over every non-loopback address this host has, IPv6 included, and ask /json/version who is answering. Only a DevTools-shaped answer counts, so an unrelated daemon or a transparent proxy on that address cannot refuse a healthy audit.

A refusal is marked fatal, so launchChrome does not retry it: before that, attempt 1 could detect exposure and attempt 2 could be accepted on an indeterminate probe, handing back an exposed browser ("launch recovered on attempt 2/3").

TESTS: tests/cdp-endpoint-exposure.mjs (266 lines, wired into the fast gate's registry). Real sockets and the real kernel throughout: the /proc decoder including its byte order; real 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::1 and :: listeners each classified, with the :: wildcard refused by the binding; cross-pid attribution (a helper process's wildcard listener must not mark our browser); the probe against real plain-HTTP and DevTools-shaped servers on 0.0.0.0 (a plain listener must NOT refuse a launch); the decision table including IPv6 and link-local with its zone; a real healthy launch cleared by its own binding with no unresolved note; and the refusal asserting no retry (the probe ran exactly once), run attribution, browser killed, profile removed.

REVIEW: independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol; implementer deepseek-flash). Pass 1: REQUEST CHANGES, 2 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 P3. Both P1s were real and are fixed above (the retry-then-fail-open path, and IPv6 blindness - my own test had ENSHRINED that blind spot by asserting an IPv6-only host returns not-exposed). P2: the probe counted any completed TCP handshake as exposure, so a foreign daemon or a proxy could have refused a healthy audit (now it asks /json/version); and the 300ms probe timeout could turn a real exposure into "unconfirmed" under load while the comments claimed only "refused" means loopback-only (now 1s, and the README states that an undecided outcome proceeds with a logged note). P3: a source assertion matched the helper's declaration instead of the call site. Pass 2 on 88cd51f (the same content, before this rebase): VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues, and it explicitly endorsed the two design choices - the kernel binding as the primary check, and proceeding with a logged note when neither check can decide (failing closed there would make audits unrunnable behind a proxy, for no measured gain).

Mutation note: writing the kernel check found a real bug in my own decoder - /proc byte-swaps inside each 32-bit word but keeps WORD order, so reversing the words turned ::1 into 0:1:0:0:0:0:0:0 while still looking plausible. There is now a test for exactly that.

SCOPE LEFT FOR A SEPARATE BEAD (not doing it here, said so in the delta): the full fix for the local-attacker residual is --remote-debugging-pipe (stdio fds 3/4, no TCP listener at all). That needs a CDP transport that is not chrome-remote-interface's HTTP/WebSocket client, so it is an architectural change, not a hardening. Happy to take it as its own bead.

Verification on the rebased tip 490fbe6: tests/cdp-endpoint-exposure.mjs tests OK (real browser launched and closed inside the test), tests/flow.mjs tests OK, tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs all 23 vendored copies identical.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: the audit browser's CDP endpoint is pinned to loopback explicitly (--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1) and then verified at launch, first from the kernel (/proc/<pid>/fd + /proc/net/tcp{,6}, IPv4 and IPv6, attributed to the browser's own pid) and then, where that cannot be read, by probing every non-loopback address and asking /json/version whether Chrome DevTools is answering. A refusal is fatal: the launch does not retry, kills the browser and records the failure. README documents the checks and the local-user residual.
WHY: the DevTools endpoint has no authentication and lives for the whole audit, and who could reach it depended on a Chrome default rather than on this tool.
EFFECT: an audit can no longer start with its unauthenticated DevTools port reachable from another host - a non-loopback bind now fails the launch with the address named - and a healthy loopback-bound launch is confirmed rather than assumed, on IPv4 and IPv6.

title: flow redaction: token-shaped URL PATH segments and bare-fragment tokens survive unless the previous segment is exactly token|secret|key|session (runner/flow-record.mjs:134,188-225; 6cb610f/fb9af75 claim)

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW on fleet/findings-redaction @ 9d87e91 (merge-base ce619d8).

REPRO (pre-fix tree)
  sanitizeNavUrl('https://example.com/reset-password/a8f9c0e2d4b6')  BEFORE: verbatim   AFTER: /reset-password/[redacted]
  sanitizeNavUrl('https://example.com/#ya29.a0AfH6SMBxxxxxxxx')      BEFORE: verbatim   AFTER: /#[redacted]
  sanitizeNavUrl('https://example.com/token/abc123')                 BEFORE: /token/[redacted] (the only arm that worked)
  sanitizeNavUrl('https://user:pass@example.com/x')                  BEFORE: https://user:pass@example.com/x   AFTER: https://%5Bredacted%5D:%5Bredacted%5D@example.com/x

FIX: PATH_VALUE_MARKERS keeps its unconditional behaviour; ROUTE_VALUE_MARKERS (auth/verify/reset/password/code/otp/confirm/activate/invite/...) redact the next segment only when it is itself value-shaped, so /auth/callback and /settings/password/change survive while /verify/483920 and /code/123456 redact. Token-shaped path segments and bare fragments are redacted with no marker at all (hex ids, JWTs, ya29.* tokens, long opaque runs), and URL userinfo is scrubbed.

REVIEW ROUND 2 (same reviewer, both directions): the first version's token shapes over-redacted real URLs, all reproduced then fixed in f078d16: bundle.min.js/style.min.css/archive.tar.gz/release-1.0.0/en-US.messages.json (JWT rule), /auth/v1, /auth/oauth2, /auth/2fa, /auth/step1, /settings/password/step2 (marker + any digit), OrderConfirmation123/UserProfileStep2Page/SummerSalePromo2024 (long-opaque rule). Their false negatives are closed too: /verify/ABCDEF and /verify/A1B2C3 (all-letter/alphanumeric OTP) now redact, and base64url tokens with -/_ (sK_9-dF0_xZ2aB123456) are caught. Found while adding their UUID case: the phone heuristic matched a 12+ digit run inside a dashed value and rewrote /orders/<uuid> as a phone; it now requires a separator between every group and anchors the whole value (real phones still redact, bare ids/dates/UUIDs do not). Second pass: VERDICT HOLDS.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: runner/flow-record.mjs sanitizeNavUrl now redacts the value-shaped things that have no NAME to classify: a segment after a route marker when it is token/PII/OTP-shaped, a token-shaped path segment or bare fragment anywhere in the URL, and URL userinfo. evidence/credential-terms.mjs looksLikeToken owns the token-shape decision and refuses slugs, filenames, multi-dot asset names, version strings and bare UUIDs.
WHY: 6cb610f/fb9af75 claimed path and fragment redaction, but the only path signal was an exact token|secret|key|session marker, a bare opaque fragment was never classified, and userinfo was never scrubbed - so /reset-password/<token> and #ya29.* survived into flow.json.
EFFECT: reset/verify/OTP links and OAuth-style fragments in a recorded journey are redacted; real routes, slugs, version strings and asset filenames, and resource UUIDs still replay exactly.

title: Review sweep can never clear: closed beads are invisible to 'bd list --limit 0 --json', so a closed bead's 'reviewed' label is unreadable and its landing is flagged unreviewed forever (fleet remote/review-cadence.sh:66)
description:
Reviewed web-uplift-3if (review-sweep, 53 rows) as a POST-LANDING review; this is a follow-up, not a block.

Repro (real bd on this VM, run in ~/web-uplift):
  bd list --limit 0 --json       | jq length   # 8    (non-closed beads only)
  bd list --limit 0 --status all | jq length   # 144
  bd list --limit 0 --json | jq '[.[]|select(.id=="web-uplift-d2l")]'          # []   (closed bead invisible)
  bd list --limit 0 --status all --json | jq '.[]|select(.id=="web-uplift-d2l")|.status'  # "closed"
  bash /tmp/rev1-repro.sh   # constructed: SAME bead with labels ["reviewed"]
                            #   CLOSED -> "1 landing(s) without a 'reviewed' label"
                            #   OPEN   -> "0 landing(s) ... nothing to review"
  bash ~/fleet/tests/review-cadence.test.sh   # PASSES: the bd stub echoes a fixed $BD_DUMP
                            # regardless of status, so the closed-bead case is untested.

Observed: remote/review-cadence.sh:66 loads 'bd list --limit 0 --json' and resolves the bead ids in each
landing subject against it (bead_exists/bead_labels). bd excludes closed beads by default, so bead_exists()
is false for every closed bead. landed_rows() then treats the landing as having no resolvable id:
- a subject that is not 'Merge fleet/...' (every single-commit landing, e.g. 73fc31a 'fix(security): keep
  Chrome's OS sandbox on by default (web-uplift-d2l)') is DROPPED from the sweep entirely;
- a 'Merge fleet/...' subject is kept with ids='-', and has_reviewed_label() is then SKIPPED, so the row is
  reported unreviewed even if the label is present.
In web-uplift today: 52 of the 53 sweep rows are 'Merge fleet/<x>' merges whose beads are closed, and the
substantive unreviewed landings (73fc31a/d2l, d7501af/wgy, f9dd253/z34, a39dd3d/61i, ...) are not rows at
all. 0 of 144 beads carry 'reviewed'. So the sweep is simultaneously noisy (closed merge landings, permanent)
and blind (real commits), and its clean state is unreachable.

Expected: a reviewer's `reviewed` label must be readable after a bead is closed. Fix: read beads with
`bd list --limit 0 --status all --json` (or resolve ids against all beads) and add a regression case with a
CLOSED bead carrying `reviewed` to tests/review-cadence.test.sh.

Impact: VM-wide - the same script runs on every project VM (and on the hub via hub-tick.sh), so every
project's sweep under-reports and over-reports the same way, and the OVERDUE escalation stays permanently on.

Evidence: /tmp/rev1-repro.sh (reproduction), /tmp/rev1-sweep.txt (full sweep output), fleet remote/review-cadence.sh:66,
fleet tests/review-cadence.test.sh:36-46,98.
Fix owner: coord -> fleet/cadence owner (PaulKinlan/fleet remote/review-cadence.sh; not this repo). Escalated.
close_reason: Superseded by fleet-qfs6 (fleet tooling, assigned Shelley); hub independently confirmed the same closed-bead invisibility bug. Repro + proposed fix (--status all + a closed-bead regression) are on this bead.

title: [factory-audit/vuln] Flow replay performs real form submissions and clicks submit controls against live sites, no opt-in gate
description:
Severity: MEDIUM (threat-model + vuln-discovery + vuln-triage concur; rule tm-flow-replay-mutates-live-targets).
Location: runner/flow.mjs:131 (verified present at origin/master dba6c2c).
The replayer executes recorded or hand-authored steps literally: keyDown Enter on a focused control calls form.requestSubmit(), and click/doubleClick steps click any matched control including submit buttons. A recorded journey, a Chrome DevTools Recorder export, or a CI-authored flow.json can create accounts, send email, place orders, or delete data on the audited production site during an audit. No dry-run, no confirmation, no gate.
Evidence: if(f&&f.requestSubmit){f.requestSubmit();return {ok:true,detail:'submitted form'};}

title: [factory-audit/vuln] secrets primitive reads page-controlled scripts with no size cap or deadline
description:
Severity: MEDIUM (vuln-discovery/vuln-triage) / LOW (threat-model, vuln-verify); using the triage severity. Rule tm-secrets-unbounded-scan.
Location: evidence/cli.mjs:2732 (verified present at origin/master dba6c2c).
The secrets primitive enumerates script[src] on the audited page and, for each of the first 20, evaluates an in-page fetch of the page-controlled URL and returns the full body text to Node via Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue. Unlike every Node-side fetch of a page-derived URL in the same file (safeFetch/readBodyCapped, FETCH_MAX_BYTES = 2 MiB), this path has no byte cap and no deadline: a hostile or broken page can hang the audit or exhaust memory, and decides what the scanner ingests.
Evidence: const js = await evaluate(client, `fetch(${JSON.stringify(su)}).then(r=>r.text()).catch(()=>'')`, { awaitPromise: true });
Remediation (factory proposal): cap the fetched body in the page before returning (ReadableStream with a fixed byte budget, body.slice) and apply the same deadline the Node-side path uses.
Note: distinct from web-uplift-01k (closed false positive: interpolation at :2513) and from the 991 quote-escaping fix; this is the unbounded-read aspect.
Source: nightly project-audit re-test 2026-10-09 (agents 64a3b72), filed manually from the embargoed store /home/exedev/va4-findings-20261009/.
close_reason: Closed

title: [factory-audit/vuln] Chrome renderer sandbox disabled unconditionally for every audited page
description:
Severity: MEDIUM (factory project-audit 2026-10-09, threat-model + vuln-discovery + vuln-triage concur; rule tm-chrome-no-sandbox-always).
Location: evidence/cdp.mjs:414 (verified present at origin/master dba6c2c).
launchChromeOnce always passes '--no-sandbox' in the fixed argument vector, so every evidence primitive navigates attacker-controlled pages with the OS sandbox disabled while running as the operator's user. A renderer RCE exploited via an audited page becomes code execution in the operator's account (HOME, ssh-agent sockets, the fleet VM's credentials).
Evidence: the literal '--no-sandbox' in the fixed launch args (cdp.mjs:414).
Remediation (factory proposal): add --no-sandbox only when necessary (detect root / restricted-container), otherwise run with the OS sandbox enabled, plus an explicit operator override flag/env; document the trade-off.
