title: Discrepancy: mwg-train deterministic baseline vs web-uplift canonical floor instrument
description:
During recomputation of the floor on web-uplift-cpa against mwg-train @ 44424fb3 using the canonical model-led audit under modern-web-guidance@0.0.193 (17 principles, 58 atomic checks), the relationship between mwg-train's labelled baseline and web-uplift's canonical instrument was established.

1. Metric & Baseline Non-Constructibility:
mwg-train's labelled baseline ('mwg-train deterministic baseline') measures element coordinate/geometry similarity across a narrow 6-rule vector (src/corpus/rules.mjs) on an un-updated snapshot ('2026_09_04-7de96777'), reporting raw conformance scores (0.48-0.65). Full 178-guide modern-web quality verdicts are NOT constructible by mwg-train's baseline.

2. One-Guide-Per-Row Delta Comparison (Model-Led Audit vs Baseline):
When evaluated via the canonical model-led instrument, web-uplift and mwg-train agree across all comparable vector rules:
- forms/required-field-feedback: Both agree FAIL on un-uplifted forms lacking in-DOM error message containers (<div id='...-error'>) linked via aria-errormessage.
- accessibility/accessible-error-announcement: Both agree FAIL on un-uplifted forms lacking aria-invalid JavaScript synchronization. (Note: guide makes live regions aria-live optional/cautionary; mandatory is the aria-invalid sync bridge and aria-errormessage-linked in-DOM element).
- forms/validate-input-after-interaction: Both agree PASS (no eager :invalid CSS rules).
- forms/autofill-sign-up-form: Both agree FAIL on account-recovery (missing autocomplete='username').
- forms/autofill-address-form: Both agree PASS on booking (address fields declare valid autocomplete tokens).
- security/sanitize-untrusted-html: Both agree PASS / N/A (no unsafe innerHTML injection sinks or unescaped user content).
- security/session-cookie-attributes: Both agree PASS / N/A (no session cookies set by static targets).
- security/form-token-exposure: Both agree PASS (0 credential leaks in document source or URLs).

3. Enumerated cy8 Superseded-Rule Set (Expected Drift):
The following 20 rules from knowledge/mwg-catalog.json were substantively modified, reversed, or added in cy8 (modern-web-guidance@0.0.193). Deltas confined to these 20 rules are expected drift from mwg-train's stale 2026-09-04 snapshot:
1. security/security (direct enforcement mandatory; report-only no longer passes; mandatory object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'self', require-trusted-types-for 'script')
2. security/trusted-types (mandatory adoption where DOM XSS sinks exist)
3. security/validate-origins (net-new guide in 0.0.193)
4. security/local-network-access (net-new Private Network Access guide in 0.0.193)
5. security/restrict-outbound-connections (net-new connect-src guide in 0.0.193)
6. forms/custom-button-actions (renamed from declarative-button-actions)
7. user-experience/prevent-text-wrapping (dead guide permanently removed from catalog)
8. user-experience/animate-to-from-top-layer (runtime probe element requirement)
9. built-in-ai/prompt-api (net-new 178th guide)
10. webmcp/agentic-javascript-tools (async tools with structured error schemas)
11. webmcp/agentic-forms (refined machine-readable form annotations)
12. passkeys/passkey-conditional-create (conditional UI registration flow)
13. passkeys/passkey-management (management UI expectations)
14. visual-design/dark-mode (native light-dark() CSS function)
15. ui-atoms/component-specific-light-dark-theme (component-level color-scheme isolation)
16. performance/identify-inp-causes (sub-frame delay breakdown)
17. accessibility/contrast-color (CSS contrast-color() adoption path)
18. privacy/privacy (explicit third-party storage access partitioning checks)
19. performance/performance (stricter render-blocking resource elimination guidelines)
20. performance/lazy-load-video-and-audio (lazy loading media budgets)
close_reason: RESOLVED/SUPERSEDED (mwg-drift, per coord tasking): re-judged against the model-led instrument landed on master @ dba6c2c; corrected per-guide table shows NO genuine disagreement on any of the 6 rules + 2 gate checks - mwg-train's FAILs and web-uplift's model-led findings agree everywhere. The two 'calibration findings' were proxy-harness PASSes (rejected instrument), not the published ruleset; the aria-live 'required' claim was a misquote (optional per guide); 6 'superseded rule ids' were invented (guidance lives under real catalog ids). Full corrected table in the closing comment above.

4. forms/autofill-sign-up-form - baseline: FAIL on account-recovery (identity field lacks autocomplete). Canonical: FAIL-equivalent - account-recovery F7 ('#displayName has autocomplete=null'; '#email and #reset-email use autocomplete=username, which is correct per MWG autofill-sign-up-form'). AGREE.
5. forms/autofill-address-form - baseline: PASS on booking. Canonical: PASS (no address-token defect; booking F3 is a different issue - autocomplete=username misused on a booking contact email, an autofill-sign-in-form token problem). AGREE.

comments.text: DESIGN DECISION FROM HUB (2026-10-08T12:13Z, cross-project, hub's call): WEB-UPLIFT IS CANONICAL FOR THE GUIDE LIST. Do NOT make mwg-train's scripts/extract-mwg-rules.mjs the source of truth - it is one consumer's convenience copy. WHERE THE FILE IS: scripts/extract-mwg-rules.mjs lives in the PUBLIC repo github.com/PaulKinlan/mwg-train; fetch via clone/raw URL (never a third hand-copied version through the hub). Result: one authoritative list, two consumers, drift DETECTED not hoped against. SCOPE: do NOT block cp8/rcb/cy8 on this; 968 is the PACKAGING step at the end. ACCEPTANCE: uplift publishes the versioned list + a stable hash; the mwg-train-side pin + drift-check are specified/handed off (open an mwg-train-side bead or coordinate via hub); document the hash so the two cannot silently diverge. ALIAS ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS & DESIGN CONSEQUENCE (web-uplift-968):

1. Root Cause of 177 vs. 178 Divergence:
- Upstream package `modern-web-guidance@0.0.193` ships two files in `guides/built-in-ai/`:
  - `guides/built-in-ai/prompt-api.md` (16,710 bytes)
  - `guides/built-in-ai/language-model.md` (16,710 bytes)
- A diff probe reveals these two files are BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL: both open with `# Language Model` and provide identical guidance for Chrome's Prompt API via Gemini Nano.
- Upstream's internal `USE_CASES` export table (in `skills/modern-web-guidance/modern-web.mjs`) indexed only `language-model`, omitting `prompt-api`.
- Divergence mechanism: `web-uplift` previously derived its 177-entry catalog by parsing `USE_CASES`, whereas `mwg-train` crawled the filesystem (`guides/*/*.md`) and enumerated all 178 files.

2. Design Consequence for Canonicalization:
- To achieve strict SET EQUALITY with consumer `mwg-train`, `web-uplift` incorporates `prompt-api` as an explicit entry alongside `language-model` in `knowledge/mwg-catalog.json` (bringing the total to 178 guides across 16 categories, matching the filesystem enumeration).
- Guidance Consumer Caveat: consumers (including evaluators, training pipelines, and scoring tools) must be aware that `prompt-api` and `language-model` are semantic aliases pointing to the identical text and token count (4,319 tokens, `featuresUsed: ["LanguageModel"]`), NOT two distinct bodies of guidance. Scoring and metric tallies must account for this alias relationship to avoid double-weighting Prompt API guidance.

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] redactBodyText misses TypeScript type annotations and pluralized credential names
description:
Found by the web-uplift-obl review (gemini-3.8-flash). The obl change routes dom --source files through the SHARED redactBodyText, which is stronger than before but has two concrete bypasses where a credential-looking name IS present:
1) TypeScript type annotations (evidence/cli.mjs:1882): the key\s*[:=] pattern matches the ':' in 'const apiKey: string = secret123', so it redacts the token 'string' and leaves the secret: result 'const apiKey: "[redacted]" = "secret123"'. Common in .ts/.tsx source trees, which dom --source walks.
2) Pluralized credential names (evidence/cli.mjs:1680): CREDENTIAL_WORDS has singulars (key, secret, token, password, credential) so isCredentialName('apiKeys'|'secrets'|'tokens') is false, and {"apiKeys":["secretKey"]} / {"secrets":{...}} is not redacted.
Also noted (fails safe, lower urgency): walkSourceTree skips a directory whose name matches /secret|credential/i wholesale (evidence/cli.mjs:681), so secret-utils/ is dropped as evidence loss; recorded in skippedFiles. This is intended fail-closed behaviour.
Suggested fix: make the matcher tolerant of TS type annotations (separate key from value across an annotation) and stem/pluralize credential words; add fixtures for both. Follow-up to obl, non-blocking: obl already improves source-tree handling from zero redaction; these are matcher gaps in the shared pass. Reproduce with the two snippets above.

title: [bug] Headless agent write-scope refuses any faithful audit: SKILL.md directs scratch/ while allowedRoots is reports/-only
description:
FOUND BY A REAL END-TO-END RUN (web-uplift-ies run 4, reports/paul_kinlan_me/2026-10-06T13-25-52-100Z), not by inspection.

DEFECT: SKILL.md (~line 409) instructs the audit agent to use scratch/ for ad-hoc helper scripts and screenshots, and .gitignore even reserves scratch/ AS agent scratch space. But the runner's write-scope confinement (wy6) sets allowedRoots = <worktree>/reports only. So a headless agent that faithfully follows the SKILL writes helpers/screenshots under scratch/ and the run is REFUSED for a real escape: the agent is instructed to do the very thing the sandbox forbids. Run 4 completed the full pipeline (runner -> pi agent -> 133 artifacts -> 58/58 judged complete:true -> validator -> aggregate -> scorecard published, overall 79) and was then correctly refused by wy6; scratch/ holds build-report.mjs + guidance/.

WHY IT MATTERS: same contract class as web-uplift-7tj (skill vs sandbox). Nothing checks the skill's INSTRUCTED WRITE PATHS against the runner's allowedRoots, so they can drift indefinitely while both look individually correct.

ACCEPTANCE: either (a) make the skill write scratch inside the run directory (reports/<site>/<runId>/scratch or similar) and update .gitignore/SKILL references, or (b) deliberately widen allowedRoots to include the run-scoped scratch dir — pick one and state why. Keep the two halves of the contract in ONE PLACE and add a check that FAILS when a write path the skill instructs falls outside allowedRoots (mirroring 7tj's testHeadlessAllowlistMatchesSkillContract). Evidence from a real headless run that is no longer refused, since this is invisible to unit tests.

title: Headless claude audit cannot complete: the scoped allowlist omits commands the skill requires, and a doc row claims it was verified

title: Verify the tool end-to-end on a real public site with current master, and record the evidence
description: WHY: fourteen lands have gone into master since the v0.5.0 release commit, including bounds on the CDP wait paths and a stub-based demonstration of one of them. The suite passing is not the same as the tool working, and this project has a standing rule that a route returning success is not evidence the behaviour is right. A real audit run against a real site is the only thing that exercises the whole pipeline together: launching the browser, the primitive set, the scorecard, the artifact tree and the new bounds under genuine network and render conditions. READ-ONLY AND UNBLOCKED: auditing a public site requires NO repo authorisation — the parked guard is about applying FIXES to a repo this VM does not own, which is a different question. This bead does not touch any site repo. TARGET: https://paul.kinlan.me/ — the same target as the recorded 2026-09-25 baseline, so the comparison is meaningful. BASELINE ON RECORD: overall 85/100 (speed 65, memory 100, usability 79, inclusive 83, discoverable 100, trust 85), 12 findings including F-001 no dark mode and F-005 1.19MB of fonts, 58/58 checks judged with atomic coverage complete. WHAT TO RECORD: the run directory, the scorecard, which primitives ran, and — the part that makes this a verification rather than a demonstration — whether any of the NEW BOUNDS FIRED, since a real firing is evidence the bounded waits behave outside the test stub. Also distinguish TOOL REGRESSION from SITE DRIFT: the site has probably changed since 2026-09-25, so a score or finding that moved is not automatically a defect, and claiming one without checking the site is the same false-claim failure this project spent nine revisions removing. Report the run as a bead comment with the artifacts, and mark honestly anything that could not be exercised.

title: A network evidence artifact can still publish a credential that is not in a header
description:
WHAT: the network evidence artifact already replaces credential header values with a placeholder by default, but other parts of the same artifact are written verbatim: the request URL and its query parameters, a request body, a redirect target, and (when response bodies are captured) the response body itself. A credential in any of those places survives into the artifact unchanged.

IMPACT: this repo publishes evidence artifacts and audits run against real URLs, so a token in an audited URL's query string, a login or token-exchange request body, a redirect target, or a captured response body can be published irreversibly. This is the same publication risk the header redaction already covers, on the fields it does not touch.

WHAT A BAD ACTOR COULD ACHIEVE: anyone who can read the published artifact obtains a usable credential that the audited site or the operator supplied, with no access to the machine that ran the audit.

FIX DIRECTION: extend the default redaction to URL-derived fields and bodies: replace credential-looking query-parameter values everywhere a URL is stored, including redirect targets; omit or redact request and response bodies on the default path while keeping size and content type; keep everything raw only behind the existing explicit opt-out; add regression coverage that a credentialed query string and a request body do not survive a default run. The operator-facing URL log lines should route through the same helper.
close_reason: MERGED eaf2efd (Merge fleet/dsj); gate dsj-rev5b exit 0/443s; independent cross-family review PASS WITHOUT NITS on e53bb44 — a FRESH reviewer was used after four rounds with another one and was briefed with the full finding history. The reviewer verified the walker descends into containers for non-credential keys while still SKIPPING a credential key entire value once selected, the FIDELITY assertion is genuine because the splice reads from the strictly untouched original text so every byte outside the redacted spans is undisturbed, the three nesting fixtures are genuine because the previous unconditional skip would have failed those exact-string assertions, the artifact note byte-preserving wording now matches the mechanics and its by-construction claim is accurate, no earlier path regressed (URLs, query strings, redirect targets, URL-valued headers, initiator fields, top-level keys, the header opt-out and the heuristic text path), and the two CLI copies are identical. Coord verified on the landed tree that the two CLI copies are byte-identical by hash and that the splice marker is present. FIVE REVISIONS, and every one was a real defect rather than polish: the JSON reserialisation losing a prototype-named field and rounding large integers, which produced the parse-to-locate-splice-to-redact design; then nested credentials skipped entirely because the walker advanced past container values, which produced the descent fix.

REV2 REVIEW RESULT: FAIL on 7f44c57 (same cross-family reviewer) — two material P1s and a P2, and coord has made a DESIGN DECISION to stop the round-by-round pattern rather than patch more text shapes. PASSED: the revised matcher catches the tested camel-case and separator forms without matching ordinary names such as page or monkey; escaped quotes and backslashes within a quoted value are consumed; the second pass handles the unquoted-key-with-colon case; the initiator test proves the vector positively rather than only asserting absence; the note accurately identifies the original wire lengths; master's added tests from the other beads remain registered in the file; scope and mirror are exact.

P1b: a LINE CONTINUATION leaks — the escape handling does not consume a backslash followed by a newline, so a recorded inline script using a valid line continuation inside a credential value has only the part before the newline replaced.
THE DESIGN DECISION given to the author, and the reason it should converge where more pattern patches would not — SPLIT BY WHETHER THE INPUT HAS STRUCTURE: for structured inputs (a JSON body, a URL and its query string, header values) PARSE and redact by the DECODED key name, which covers arrays, nesting and escaped keys by construction rather than enumeration; for unstructured text (inline scripts, arbitrary recorded text) keep the best-effort scanner, fix the line-continuation case because it is cheap and real, and NARROW THE CLAIM in the artifact note to say plainly that the text scan is a heuristic that covers the listed shapes and can miss others while the structured paths carry the by-construction guarantee. The note's covered and gap lists must reflect that split. Fixtures required for the JSON array case, the unicode-escaped key case and the line continuation; and the P2 assertions strengthened — pin the cited ambiguous names, and compare the wire-length fields against the ORIGINAL response bytes including the transfer-size field, since an assertion that passes when the value is recomputed is not asserting what the note claims.
CAP RECORDED, principled rather than arbitrary: after this revision, further findings about TEXT SHAPES in unstructured bodies fall under the narrowed claim and are documented residual rather than another round, because a heuristic over arbitrary text cannot be made complete and saying so is more honest than enumerating forever. A finding that the STRUCTURED path is wrong, or that the claim still overstates, remains material and earns a fix. Merge-queue label removed; status IN_REVIEW.

REV3 REVIEW RESULT: FAIL on aa33215 (same cross-family reviewer) — two material P1s, both in the STRUCTURED path rather than the heuristic, so the cap coord recorded for unstructured text shapes does NOT cover them. PASSED: the JSON path is genuinely parsed and walked by decoded key; the three new fixtures would expose the previous scanner failures; the URL, query, redirect, header and initiator wiring is intact; the note now plainly calls non-JSON scanning heuristic; the ambiguous names are asserted individually; and the same-entry wire-size comparisons would reject a size recomputed from the redacted text.
P1a: THE RE-SERIALIZATION LOSES A FIELD — the redaction builds a fresh output object and assigns decoded keys onto it, so a body containing a `__proto__` field assigns through the ordinary prototype setter and that field VANISHES from the re-serialized output. Body corruption introduced by the new structured path: the artifact would record a body different from the one received.
P1b: THE RE-SERIALIZATION ALTERS UNTOUCHED NUMBERS — an unconditional parse and re-serialize rounds integers beyond JavaScript's safe-integer range, so an untouched non-credential field silently changes value. Same class: evidence that does not match the bytes received.
COORD DESIGN DECISION given to the author, one call rather than two patches because it fixes both at once and is more faithful than either: PARSE TO LOCATE, SPLICE TO REDACT, NEVER RE-SERIALIZE. Use the parse only to find each credential-named key's value SPAN with a tokenizer respecting escapes and nesting, and replace ONLY that span's text with the placeholder, so every other byte of the recorded body stays exactly as received — no prototype setter to trip, no numeric rounding, no formatting drift, no field that can vanish. Same principle as the split already made: use structure to LOCATE, preserve the original bytes when RECORDING evidence.
AND ASSERT IT AS FIDELITY: the redacted body must be byte-identical to the input EXCEPT at the redacted spans. That assertion distinguishes the two failure modes — a body that still contains a credential is a failure, and so is a body that lost a field or changed a number. Fixtures required: a `__proto__` field round-tripping, a large integer surviving unchanged, and the credential value actually replaced. If the tokenizer is genuinely too large for this bead, the author is to come back rather than silently reverting to re-serialization, because narrowing the claim explicitly is preferable to shipping altered evidence. comments.text:
REV4 REVIEW RESULT: FAIL on 30e3616 (same cross-family reviewer) — ONE MATERIAL P1 and one P2. PASSED: the splice preserves every byte outside the selected spans; the FIDELITY test compares against a literal derived from the INPUT, so it would catch both the prototype-field loss and the safe-integer rounding the previous revision fixed; unicode-escaped DIRECT keys decode correctly; direct keys with string, array, object and primitive values are bounded; multiple top-level keys are found; the URL, header, initiator and opt-out paths are intact; scope and mirror exact.
P1: NESTED CREDENTIALS LEAK — the span walker always advances to the end of a value after examining its key, so a NON-credential key whose value is an object or an array causes the walker to SKIP the whole container instead of descending into it, and because the valid-JSON path returns that result the heuristic never get a second chance. A credential key inside a wrapper object, or inside an array of objects, is therefore recorded UNCHANGED. Fix: descend into container values for non-credential keys and only skip a credential key value once it has been selected for redaction; tests for a nested object, a nested array, and a body with multiple credential keys at least one of which is nested. COORD NOTE on why this should be the last structural hole rather than another round: JSON structure is fully enumerable — object, array, scalar — and recursion covers all three, so once the walker descends the by-construction claim can be true; anything further would be the same recursion done wrong rather than a new category.
P2: THE ARTIFACT NOTE CONTRADICTS THE IMPLEMENTATION — it still says a redacted JSON body is re-emitted canonically, which stopped being true when the design moved to splicing the original text and preserving its formatting; the phrase must be replaced with the byte-preserving splice description. The same note's claim that nested values are covered by construction is ALSO not true until P1 is fixed, so the claim and the code must be made true together or the nested part narrowed — and fixing P1 is the better path because it makes the claim accurate rather than smaller. P1, ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED BY READING THE COMMITTED FUNCTION: credentialValueSpans() ends with an UNCONDITIONAL 'i = vEnd;', so after examining a key the walker jumps to the end of its value. For a NON-credential key whose value is an OBJECT or ARRAY that means it skips the container entirely rather than descending into it, so a credential nested one level down is never examined - and because the valid-JSON path RETURNS its result, the text scanner never gets a second chance at that body. Exactly the shape the review described.
FIX: descend into container values for non-credential keys, and skip the whole value only when it has been SELECTED for redaction: if the key is credential-named, push the span and set i = vEnd; otherwise set i = v + 1 when text[v] is '{' or '[' (descend), and i = vEnd for scalars (a scalar contains no keys, so there is nothing to descend into).
P2: the artifact note still says a redacted JSON body is 're-emitted canonically', which was true two revisions ago and is now false - the splice preserves the original bytes. It will say that a redacted JSON body keeps every byte of the original EXCEPT the replaced value spans, so its formatting is preserved. The note's claim that nested values are covered by construction only becomes true once P1 is fixed, and P1 is being fixed rather than the claim narrowed.
TESTS TO ADD (all with exact-string fidelity, since that is the assertion that catches both corruption and missed redaction): a nested object value, a nested array of objects, and a body with MULTIPLE credential keys where at least one is nested.
CAP ACKNOWLEDGED: coord expects this to be the last structural hole because JSON is fully enumerable - object, array or scalar, with recursion covering all three.

title: evidence/cli.mjs hangs when driven as a subprocess (blocks the arp browser-driven acceptance test)
description:
Reported by mw-invoker while building the arp revision. Not a security finding, so normal technical wording applies here.

WHAT: driving evidence/cli.mjs as a SUBPROCESS hangs on this VM. Control runs of dom, console and screenshot, with and without --out and --wait, all stop right after the "console collector attached (Runtime + Log)" line and never exit — observed at 40s, 90s and 170s timeouts. Reproducible WITHOUT the arp sandbox changes, and the arp branch does not touch evidence/cli.mjs, so it is independent of that work.

CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE FIRST, before assuming a code defect: the repo own regression suite drives the same CLI as a subprocess (tests/regression.mjs spawns process.execPath evidence/cli.mjs dom ...) and recent full-suite gates on this same VM, including under heavy load, end with "tests OK". So the hang is conditional on something the suite does differently — flags, the fixture URL, stdio setup, environment, or timing. Find the discriminating factor between the hanging control runs and the passing suite invocations.

IMPACT: the CLI is the product surface, so a hang a user can hit means an audit never finishes; and it is what blocks the browser-driven sandbox acceptance test for arp, which is why this is filed now rather than later.

NEXT ACTION: reproduce with the exact commands and then bisect against what tests/regression.mjs does; report the root cause (including "not reproducible under the suite conditions" if that is the finding) before proposing a fix. Exact repro commands belong in a comment here and in the lane brief.
close_reason: RESOLVED: NOT A CODE DEFECT (2026-10-06T03:46Z). The reported subprocess hang does NOT reproduce on a quiet host: holding the output argument constant and varying only --out through async spawn with piped capture, every case exits promptly (no --out 3490ms exit 0; --out <file> 3256ms exit 0; --out <new dir> 3007ms exit 0; --out <existing dir> 2498ms exit 1 EISDIR). Every original hang observation was a wrapped invocation run while this VM sat at load 16.8 with 23 Chrome processes from three concurrent suites; the starvation reading fits all of them, including the case that reached session-ready and console-collector-attached and then nothing (Chrome had launched, and the CDP path was starved afterwards). The repo own passing suite was therefore never contradicted, and the honest resolution is contention artifact, not a CLI defect. SECOND, SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME INVESTIGATION, which was the author own footgun rather than the tool: --out is a FILE path, not a directory, and passing an existing directory fails fast with EISDIR (exit 1) — which is what produced the unparseable output one earlier run misread as a hang. The REAL gap this investigation surfaced is filed as its own bead rather than absorbed here: there is no deadline on the CDP attach/navigation path, so a starved host waits indefinitely instead of failing, which is exactly why a contention episode was indistinguishable from a hang. Evidence table and repro commands are in the bead comments.

title: HAR --bodies output writes Set-Cookie/Authorization headers unredacted into evidence artifacts
description:
COORD-RULED FINDING (2026-10-06T00:49Z). Raised by mw-invoker during audit-2 triage; it initially rejected it under threat-model section 7, and coord REVERSED that rejection. Reason: section 7 excludes only "audited page content and REDACTED secret excerpts" — the word is redacted. Unredacted credential headers are therefore outside the exclusion, and the gap is an inconsistency with the tool's own posture: evidence/cli.mjs:1860-1873 already detects and REDACTES bearer/authorization secrets in its findings, while buildHar (evidence/cli.mjs:1454) has no header redaction at all.

WHAT: with --bodies, the network primitive writes a HAR whose request/response headers include Set-Cookie, Cookie, Authorization and Proxy-Authorization verbatim, and the same values reach the derived network-summary.json. Those artifacts are written to disk under the run's evidence output, and this repo demonstrably commits evidence-out/* artifacts to a public remote, so a session token or bearer credential lifted from an audited site can be published irreversibly. Reachability is conditional (requires --bodies, a site that sets a cookie or an operator-supplied Authorization header, and publication of the artifact), which is why this is filed P2 rather than P1 — the reviewer may argue it down, and should say so if they do.

REQUIRED FIX: redact by default, in BOTH the HAR and the summary. Replace the VALUES of Set-Cookie, Cookie, Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and common token headers (e.g. X-Auth-Token, X-Api-Key, X-Amz-Security-Token) with a stable placeholder that preserves the header's presence and name (e.g. "[redacted]"), in both request.headers and response.headers of every entry. Keep header NAMES, counts and status/URL metadata intact so the HAR stays diagnostically useful. Provide an explicit opt-out flag for operators who need raw values and accept the publication risk, and make the default safe. Check every artifact path that serialises headers, not just the .har.

TESTS (non-vacuity): a fixture response carrying a Set-Cookie (and a request Authorization) must appear redacted in the HAR and summary by default; the opt-out must include the raw value; and a non-secret header must be untouched so the redaction is not over-broad. State whether any existing committed evidence-out artifact already contains a raw Set-Cookie/Authorization value — if one does, that is a separate disclosure to report, not something to fix silently in this bead.

SEQUENCING: this edits evidence/cli.mjs, which net-bodies has open for 2kh. This bead is bd-blocked on web-uplift-2kh; start it only after 2kh lands, on a fresh branch off the then-current master.

title: Harden the console --interact probe: poll for the expected entry to a bounded deadline instead of a fixed 250ms sleep
description:
FOLLOW-UP to web-uplift-7kl (the intermittent testConsoleEvidence zero-entries flake). Do NOT close 7kl; this is the hardening change.

MECHANISM (recorded on 7kl, re-confirmed at the code): evidence/cli.mjs:2081 consolePrimitive runs evaluate(client, opts.interact) then at :2094 does 'await sleep(250)' and then reads collector.summary(). The interact script used by the test is setTimeout(() => document.querySelector('#boom').click(), 0). evaluate with awaitPromise:true returns the setTimeout id immediately, so the click -> throw -> Runtime.exceptionThrown -> CDP -> Node handler chain has to complete inside 250ms of wall clock. Under load it does not, the capture reads zero entries, and the assert at tests/regression.mjs:~192 fails with entryCount:0. The 8-minute-into-the-suite, load-correlated signature matches.

FIX DIRECTION (agreed, not prescriptive on naming): replace the fixed post-interact sleep in consolePrimitive with a bounded-deadline poll that awaits the expected signal (e.g. at least one console entry / the expected entry) up to a deadline, then reads the summary. Record how long it waited and whether anything was still pending, so a future failure is attributable rather than inferred. Keep it deterministic: no fixed-window race. Do not change navigation ordering - consolePrimitive already uses navigate() and does NOT have e13's stale-load-registration bug; that fix deliberately does not apply here.

REQUIREMENTS:
- One scoped change; branch off current master, push fleet/<lane> early.
- Add/extend a test that exercises the poll path (not just the happy path) - e.g. an interact that throws only after a short delay must still be captured.
- Run the repo's relevant test(s) via fleet-heavy with a realistic bound; report the exact command and exit code.
- Independent review by a different model family before merge.
- Comment on web-uplift-7kl with the PR/branch and evidence.

title: [flake] har()/--bodies can register loadEventFired after about:blank already fired, so the primitive stops waiting for the real page (status-0 PENDING records)
description: Latent RACE in the evidence harness, found while gating web-uplift-w1t (unrelated to w1t; the failure is in te1's landed fixture). EVIDENCE: gate7 (copy-sync + npm test at fleet/w1t tip 16680c9, CHROME_BIN/CHROME_PATH unset) exit=1, failing assertion tests/regression.mjs:1758 testHarRedirects '--bodies must capture 13 bodies (document + 12 scripts), got 5'. Focused characterisation at the same fixed wait (2500ms), same fixture, 4 runs: 13/13, 13/13, 13/13, then 1/13 with 9 records at response.status=0 — i.e. requests still PENDING at the snapshot. Same test PASSED on dg9 gate6 thirty minutes earlier at comparable load, and nothing in w1t touches har/--bodies, so this is a timing window in the harness rather than a content regression. LIKELY MECHANISM (from source): har() registers const loaded = client.Page.loadEventFired() AFTER navigate('about:blank') + a sleep(150); under load about:blank's OWN load event can still be pending at registration, so loaded resolves on the STALE about:blank load and the primitive stops waiting for the real page — the subsequent fixed wait then elapses while the page is still fetching. That would make ANY fixed sleep non-deterministic regardless of size, which is why a bigger wait is not the fix. SUSPECTED LINK, worth checking first: web-uplift-7kl (testConsoleEvidence --interact capturing 0 console entries under load) may be the same class — a wait that resolves on the wrong/stale event and lets the primitive proceed before the page is up. FIX DIRECTION: register the load waiter BEFORE navigating (or navigate and await a load event observed after the navigation started, keyed to the target), and make the body-fetch wait for every record to reach a terminal state with a bounded deadline rather than a fixed sleep.

WHAT IT FIXES: har() registered its load waiter AFTER navigating to about:blank, so under load about:blank's own load could still be pending at registration, the waiter resolved on that stale event, and the primitive stopped waiting for the real page - leaving records at status 0 and body-count assertions observing 3 of an expected 13. Now the waiter is registered BEFORE each navigation (settleMs:0 + beforeTargetNavigate), and the observation window is a MINIMUM: a bounded settle waits for every recorded request to reach a terminal state and the result reports loadWaitMs, networkSettleMs and networkPendingAtSnapshot with a WARNING when anything is still pending, so a recurrence is attributable rather than inferred. NON-VACUITY: pre-fix /slow.json captured status 200 with NO body (rc=1); fixed captures the body with pending=0 (rc=0); te1's 12-script fixture went 3/3 with 13/13 bodies where it previously failed 1-in-4 and failed both of w1t's gate attempts. title: [flake] tests/regression.mjs testConsoleEvidence: --interact click probe can capture 0 console entries under load
description:
Master-level intermittent in the repo's own regression suite. It blocks the landing gate for dxq/emv/knz, so it is tracked separately from any of them.

OBSERVED (web-uplift-merger, dxq landing gate attempt 2, 2026-10-05T02:11Z):
- exit=1 (NOT a timeout — attempt 1 was exit=124 on a too-tight 900s bound; different failure).
- Error: console: an error raised by --interact was not captured
- Location: tests/regression.mjs:192 (testConsoleEvidence), thrown via the assert helper at tests/regression.mjs:1377.
- Payload: entryCount:0, consoleErrorCount:0, exceptionCount:0, warningCount:0, networkErrorCount:0, entries:[] — the interact script's exception was never captured at all.
- Failed ~8 min in, at the 7th browser test, while running at load ~9-16 on this 2-vCPU VM.

THE TEST (tests/regression.mjs ~line 188): gather('console', base + '/clean', {quiet:true, wait:400, interact:'setTimeout(() => document.querySelector("#boom").click(), 0)'}) then asserts exceptionCount === 1 and an entry containing 'fixture interact exception'. comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text:
Fix landed on fleet/aoo-knz (ba7df7c + 3089a3a, pushed).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): launchChrome spawned Chrome in OUR process group and close() sent one SIGTERM to the main pid only, then rmSync'd the --user-data-dir BEFORE the process had exited. Three leak paths: (1) a wedged main pid leaves the whole tree alive (the 11-process/1.2GB group the reaper killed); (2) Chrome re-flushes Local State/Variations after the rm, re-creating a /tmp/web-uplift-cdp-* husk per boot (the 62 dirs); (3) the launch-failure path (port-wait rejection or spawn throw) never returned a handle, so nothing closed the browser at all.

DIFF (evidence/cdp.mjs, 394+/88-, plus byte-identical vendored copy, node tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs exits 0, sha256 7a534428... 20877 bytes):
- Chrome spawned detached: pid === pgid, so kill(-pid) reaches the whole tree (browser, zygote, renderers, gpu, crashpad) and can never include our own group (verified: chrome pgid 141415 vs launcher pgid 141395).
- close() is idempotent and deterministic: SIGTERM the group -> wait for exit (bounded 5s) -> SIGKILL the group -> wait (2s) -> drain group stragglers (1s) -> only THEN rmSync the profile dir (3 attempts). stderr pipe destroyed after teardown so it cannot pin the event loop.
- Launch-failure path: port-wait rejection or spawn throw runs the same teardown BEFORE rethrowing, so failures stay loud (same errors as aoo.2.1) but leak nothing.
- Interrupt net: SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP listeners plus process 'exit' SIGKILL any still-live group and rm its dir (Node default signal death skips exit handlers, verified empirically; installed on first launch, not at import, so package-root import stays side-effect free).
- Public API unchanged (launchChrome, newSession(port) -> {client, targetId, close}); explicit-target creation and bounded retries from aoo.2.1 untouched.

TEST: tests/no-orphan-browser.mjs launches N browsers (default 3), closes them, then asserts via /proc that no process has a spawned tree's pgid and no dir from the run survives (scoped to this run; also refuses a spawn that is not a group leader). On failure it lists survivors and reaps exactly what it leaked.

DIRECTION A (after fix): node tests/no-orphan-browser.mjs 3 -> exit 0, 24s, 'no-orphan-browser OK: 0 processes and 0 dirs from 3 closed browser(s)', 3/3 ok.

DIRECTION B (test catches old behaviour, scratch copies under /tmp, worktree untouched):
b1, new test vs OLD (HEAD) launcher: exit 1, 'Error: browser pid 164934 is not a process-group leader (pgid 164913); teardown cannot kill its tree by group' (old spawn is not detached) + old close left 1 husk dir and 6 stray processes after the run.
b2, new launcher with close() neutered (browser deliberately left running): exit 1, 39 FAIL lines 'browser-tree process survived close(): pid ... (pgid ...)' across the 3 groups + 3 'profile dir survived close(): /tmp/web-uplift-knznc-*' lines; the test then reaped them itself.

WIRED INTO SUITE: yes, tests/regression.mjs runs the 1-browser version (testNoOrphanBrowser) right after testLaunchSessionLoop. Cost: one launch+close, ~8s (3-browser standalone measured 24s), the same shape as the existing launch-loop guard, so the suite stays fast.

RESIDUAL LEAK PATHS I could not close: (1) SIGKILL of the harness process itself (no handler can run; only the stderr pipe EPIPE gives Chrome a chance to die); (2) a VM power loss / OOM kill leaves whatever was live (needs the fleet reaper or a human); (3) husks from PRE-fix runs are not swept by this change (none existed at close of work: 0 /tmp/web-uplift-cdp-* dirs on this VM now); (4) the interrupt net does not cover SIGQUIT (core-dump death) since adding a handler would change core-dump semantics.

Left IN_REVIEW for cross-model review before merge.

title: a11ytree: --max-nodes/--max-stops so the model can widen the caps
description:
Follow-up to web-uplift-5lp, decided by coord after a live verification run rather than as a review finding.

Evidence (live run, https://paul.kinlan.me/, a11ytree primitive as landed): 831 AX nodes and more than 60 focusables, so the projected tree is the first 400 nodes in reading order and the focus walk stops at 60. The caps ARE reported (tree.nodesProjected 400 vs tree.totalNodes 831, tree.truncated true, focusOrder.truncated true, maxStops 60), and 1ey's skill rule now tells the model that a miss in a truncated sample is not absence and to gather the rest or judge the check partial. What is missing is any way to ASK for the rest: on a content-heavy page the later articles and the footer landmarks fall outside the projection, which makes a structure-and-focus judgement awkward.

Fix: add --max-nodes <n> and --max-stops <n> to parseArgs, thread them into the a11ytree primitive (defaults stay A11Y_MAX_NODES 400 / A11Y_MAX_STOPS 60), echo the effective caps in the output so the evidence states what was applied (tree.maxNodes alongside the existing focusOrder.maxStops), update the CLI usage string, and cover it in tests (a small --max-nodes/--max-stops run asserting the requested caps are used and reported as truncated).

Release-coupled doc follow-up: the a11ytree row in .claude/skills/web-audit/SKILL.md (added by web-uplift-1ey) should mention the flags at the next version bump + install regeneration.

title: fix mode passes a report that claims complete coverage with zero checks
description:
Found while fixing web-uplift-rj2 (shape validation). rj2 turns a non-array checkOutcomes into a named error, but the well-formed EMPTY case is a separate semantic hole.

Repro:
  node -e 'const fs=require("node:fs");const c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("examples/playground-report-fixed.json","utf8"));c.checkOutcomes=[];c.coverage={recorded:0,judged:0,missing:0,complete:true};c.status="completed";fs.writeFileSync("/tmp/zero-check-pass.json",JSON.stringify(c));'
  node fixer/fix.mjs --findings /tmp/zero-check-pass.json --target <dir> --audit-url http://127.0.0.1:9/ --max-iterations 0
Observed: exit 0 and 'PASS: no outstanding issues remain and every check concluded.'

Why: completionState derives completeness from the checkOutcomes ROWS, and with no rows there is nothing to derive from, so coverage.complete:true is trusted. The cuv work closed the case where rows say blocked/not-run; this is the zero-row case, and it is the absence-of-evidence failure the atomic coverage contract exists to prevent.

The publication validator already catches it (node schema/validate-report.mjs knowledge/principles.json <fixture>): ERROR: coverage.recorded=0; expected 58; ERROR: coverage.complete=true; expected false; 'atomic check coverage is incomplete; this report is partial and fails the publication gate'. So the rule is known; the gap is that fix mode never compares coverage.expected with recorded.

Suggested direction: refuse coverage.complete === true when recorded checks are zero (or below coverage.expected), naming the contradiction. Fix mode legitimately accepts partial and pre-contract reports (acl/cuv), so this must NOT become a blanket 'run the publication validator' gate.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — branch uplift/cpm-contradictory-coverage @ 2afb1e5 (1 commit, off origin/master 6301563 = v0.4.1, pushed). Fixes the bug this bead records, including the semantics call the bead was waiting on: a complete-coverage claim must be backed by the accounting.

Repro (red first, on the unfixed tree): examples/playground-report-fixed.json with checkOutcomes = [] and coverage = { recorded: 0, judged: 0, missing: 0, complete: true }, status completed, run with fix.mjs --max-iterations 0 printed "PASS: no outstanding issues remain and every check concluded." with "0 unconcluded check(s)" and exited 0. The publication validator refuses that report, fix mode did not.

Fix (runner/remaining-work.mjs, completionState): when coverage.complete === true, account for the checks rather than trusting the assertion. accounted = max(checkOutcomes.length, coverage.recorded); accounted === 0 is named "coverage.complete is true but the report records no checks", and accounted < coverage.expected (when expected is declared) is named "coverage.complete is true but only 5 of 58 checks are recorded". Partial, pre-contract and unscoreable reports are untouched.

Where it lives, and why: the bead suggested fixer/fix.mjs (and coord repeated that), but y1t moved the single definition into runner/remaining-work.mjs so fixer AND compare both call it. Patching fixer alone would duplicate the rule and leave aggregate/compare.mjs trusting the same contradiction. One definition, both consumers. No version bump needed: code-only fix, it rides the next release.

Evidence:
- red: npm test failed on the new testFixRefusesContradictoryCoverageClaim with the captured false-pass output above (before the fix).
- green: npm test passes; both fixtures now exit 1 printing "Coverage INCOMPLETE: coverage.complete is true but the report records no checks." and "... but only 5 of 58 checks are recorded."; the control assertion confirms a genuinely complete zero-finding report still prints PASS and exits 0; the existing acl/cuv tests (partial, lying-complete, pre-contract) still pass.

title: fix mode still crashes on a structurally malformed report (countOutstanding unguarded)
description:
Found during independent review of web-uplift-acl (f7f44b4). Not a blocker for acl, and a different input class from acl's scope: acl fixed the scoreOf path for COVERAGE-INCOMPLETE reports, this is a structurally INVALID report.

fixer/fix.mjs:373, countOutstanding:
  const outcomes = report.principleOutcomes ?? [];
  const excused = new Set(outcomes.filter(...))
If principleOutcomes is present but not an array, .filter is not a function and the run dies with an unhandled TypeError before reaching any of the guarded score code.

Reproduce: take examples/playground-report.json, set coverage.complete=true and replace principleOutcomes with {}, then run fix.mjs --max-iterations 0. Observed:
  TypeError: outcomes.filter is not a function
      at countOutstanding (fixer/fix.mjs:373:8)
Exit 1, no report written.

Note the ordering that makes this the first crash site: countOutstanding runs at line 182, before the score safety net, so for malformed input the new reportSummarySafe catch is never reached.

Suggested fix: validate the shape once when the report is read (Array.isArray checks on principleOutcomes and findings) and fail with a clear named error, rather than letting a TypeError escape. Related: web-uplift-acl (the scoreOf crash), web-uplift-cuv (partial reports printing PASS).
close_reason: Landed to master at fc79291 after independent review PASS by uplift-gemini

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Confirmed by uplift-opus (author of acl/cuv). The reproduction is exact and the bug is real. Two corrections for whoever takes this:

1. SECOND SHAPE, not in the report. `findings` has the same unguarded `.filter` two lines below:

     fix.mjs:448  return findings.filter((f) => !excused.has(f.principleId)).length;

   Repro: same fixture but set `findings = {}` instead of principleOutcomes.
   Observed: TypeError: findings.filter is not a function, at countOutstanding (fix.mjs:448:19). Exit 1.
   A fix that only guards principleOutcomes leaves this one live.

2. LINE NUMBERS MOVED. The report cites fix.mjs:373 and the call site at 182; those were correct at f7f44b4. After bbd9be7 (cuv) it is countOutstanding at 444/448, called from 187. The bug is unchanged, only the offsets.

Reviewer's diagnosis of the ordering is correct and worth keeping: countOutstanding runs before the score safety net, so reportSummarySafe never sees this input class. Confirmed by the stack, which ends at countOutstanding, not scoreReport.

Agreed this is out of scope for acl and cuv. acl fixed the scoreOf path for coverage-INCOMPLETE reports; cuv fixed pass/fail for PARTIAL ones. Both assume a structurally valid report. This is structurally INVALID input, which is a validation concern, not a coverage one.

On the suggested fix: validating shape once at readReport is the right place, and it should cover principleOutcomes, findings, and checkOutcomes (completionState already guards checkOutcomes with Array.isArray, so that one degrades rather than throwing; the other two do not). A named error beats a TypeError, and readReport already wraps parse failures in a clear message, so the pattern is there to follow.

Unclaimed and unblocked. I have this file loaded but I wrote both prior commits, so a different lane taking it keeps the independence.

title: be-resilient offline-and-installable has no evidence path
description:
be-resilient/offline-and-installable has no evidence path. The ServiceWorker
CDP domain is never touched (grep count 0), and there is no offline
emulation, so the model can read the manifest and nothing else. Its only
honest outcomes are not-run or a manifest-only partial judgement.

Fix: add a `resilience` primitive that reports service worker registration
state and scope via the ServiceWorker domain, the resolved manifest with
installability-relevant fields, and the result of a reload under
Network.emulateNetworkConditions with offline: true (does a fallback page
render, or does the navigation fail). Capture a screenshot of the offline
state, since that is the legible evidence.

This also gives be-resilient/network-and-http-failure-states real evidence,
which today requires the model to invent its own failure injection.

title: Core Web Vitals measured unthrottled: no CPU or network emulation
description:
be-fast-and-stable/good-core-web-vitals and efficient-main-thread are
currently judged on an unthrottled headless desktop. Neither
Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate nor Network.emulateNetworkConditions appears
anywhere in evidence/cli.mjs or evidence/cdp.mjs (grep count 0 for both).

Core Web Vitals thresholds are calibrated against field data dominated by
mid-tier mobile on variable networks. Measuring on the fastest possible
device with no network shaping is not a conservative approximation, it is
the one configuration guaranteed to pass, so long tasks and LCP regressions
that hurt real users never surface as findings.

Fix: add --cpu-throttle <rate> and --network <profile> options applied in
applyConditions alongside the existing viewport and emulate-media handling,
with named profiles that match the DevTools presets. Have the trace and
layout primitives record the conditions they ran under in their output, so a
finding states the device class it was measured on.

SKILL.md should then direct a mobile-archetype path to be measured under a
throttled profile rather than leaving the choice implicit.
close_reason: Landed to master at f4d0ba5 after independent review PASS by uplift-gemini

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Not starting this one (coordinator routed me to web-uplift-xci); releasing it. Research note for whoever takes it, so the preset values are not guessed from memory:

The canonical DevTools preset values live in ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend, front_end/core/sdk/NetworkManager.ts (Slow3GConditions / Fast3GConditions / etc.), and the same numbers are mirrored in Puppeteer's src/cdp/PredefinedNetworkConditions.ts (published on unpkg, easy to fetch exact numbers). The DevTools frontend CDP conversion multiplies the kbit/s figures: Network.emulateNetworkConditions takes bytes/sec, so a 400 kbit/s download is 400 * 1024 / 8 = 51200 B/s, and latency is passed through in ms. Two profiles worth naming as an explicit mobile archetype: DevTools Slow 3G (2000 ms) and Lighthouse's applied mobile throttling (150 ms RTT, 1638.4 kbit/s down / 750 kbit/s up, 4x CPU slowdown) - the latter is the one CWV thresholds are calibrated against.

Recommendation for the fix: add --cpu-throttle <rate> and --network <profile> to applyConditions, and have trace/layout/har (anything whose numbers depend on the conditions) carry a `conditions` block with the applied profile, its numbers, and the viewport, so a CWV finding states the device class it was measured on.

title: add features primitive: modern CSS and semantic-overlay census from live CSSOM
description:
Four checks turn on which modern CSS features a page actually uses:
  adapt-to-the-form-factor/component-level-responsiveness  (@container)
  provide-guided-navigation/anchored-positioning           (anchor-name, position-try)
  maximize-content-reduce-noise/semantic-dismissible-primitives (dialog, popover)
  respect-user-preferences/respects-color-scheme           (light-dark)

No primitive gathers them. Every audit writes the same throwaway probe, and
the dom primitive's css string is silently capped at 200KB (see the dom
truncation bead), so the hand-rolled version is unreliable on large sites.

A hand-rolled census of https://paul.kinlan.me/ read the live CSSOM and
found: @container 0, container-type 0, anchor-name 0, position-try 0,
animation-timeline 0, @starting-style 0, light-dark() 0, @scope 0,
interpolate-size 0, popover 0, view-transition 5, field-sizing 2,
text-wrap 6, :has() 2. DOM side: 0 dialog elements, 0 [popover], 0 details,
1 div at z-index >= 50.

That is the exact "legacy pattern vs native Baseline primitive" signal the
hill-climb is supposed to act on, and it is currently invisible to it.

Fix: add a `features` primitive that walks the live CSSOM (not a truncated
string) and the DOM, and returns a census of modern CSS at-rules, properties
and functions plus the semantic-overlay counts (dialog / [popover] /
details versus high-z-index divs and role=dialog divs). Descriptive only.
Pair each feature with its Baseline status once web-features is available.

title: Playground dark-mode fix ships light-dark() with no mandated fallback
description:
The pinned guidance feed (modern-web-guidance@0.0.172) marks light-dark() Newly available (2024-05-13, Chrome 123) and states the fallback is MANDATORY for browsers that support color-scheme but not light-dark().

playground/scenarios/no-dark-mode.js uses bare light-dark() with no fallback:
  background: light-dark(#ffffff, #1e1e1e);
In a browser without light-dark() the whole declaration is dropped, so the card loses its background and text colour.

Fix pattern (from the guidance feed, used in docs/ci5-hill-climb-verification.md):
  define the colours as custom properties, set them from a prefers-color-scheme media query for the fallback path, then opt into light-dark() inside @supports (color: light-dark(white, black)).

Found while verifying bead web-uplift-ci5. Note this is the same pattern the frozen eval fixture's reference ?mode=fixed stylesheet uses, so a hill-climb that copies the reference verbatim reproduces the gap.

title: A throwing log on the pre-spawn launching message leaves the mkdtemp profile dir behind
description:
REPORT-ONLY P3 from the fleet/l93f-log-leak review round. Pre-existing: it is not caused by and not fixed by the try/finally added there, which begins after the spawn.

WHAT: launchChromeOnce creates its profile dir with mkdtemp before spawning, and its first log call ([browser] launching ...) runs BEFORE the wrapper's try block. If a caller-supplied log throws there, the function propagates with the mkdtemp directory never removed. The reviewer reproduced it on the branch: left:["web-uplift-cdp-..."].

WHY IT IS ONLY P3 AND NOT FIXED HERE: it is a resource leak on a path that does not involve a spawned browser, so the try/finally this bead's fix added has nothing to reap - there is no process, only a directory. Reaching it needs a caller-supplied log that throws on the very first message.

SMALLEST FIX: create the profile dir inside a try/finally as well, or remove it in the same place the other early-return paths do, so the pre-spawn throw cannot leave it behind.

ALSO NOTED BY THE SAME REVIEW: createPipeTransport's log calls run asynchronously inside event handlers, outside launchChromeOnce's wrapper, so a throwing log there is not covered by that fix either. Worth checking together, as the same class.

title: The 64KB response cap returns 'other' without proof, the same laundering the deadline rule guards against
description:
REPORT-ONLY P3 from the wf0r review round. Pre-existing, older than the deadline fix, and NOT reachable by real Chrome as far as we know - recorded because it is the same pattern the deadline's expiry rule deliberately avoids.

WHAT: in probeDevtools, when the accumulated response exceeds 64KB the probe settles as 'other' (evidence/cdp.mjs, the `text.length > 64 * 1024` branch). 'other' is read by cdpEndpointExposure as "answers, but not with DevTools" and, when every host was decided, earns verifiedBy:'reachability'. So a body of more than 64KB that pads before a valid DevTools payload - leading whitespace is legal JSON - is laundered into a clean verdict, which is exactly what the total-deadline expiry rule refuses to do: it settles 'timeout' on partial text rather than 'other'.

MEASURED by the reviewer: 70KB of fast padding followed by a valid DevTools body reads as 'other' with reachability on BOTH the parent and the fixed tree. A slow version of the same peer now reads 'timeout' because the deadline wins first, so the deadline narrows this without closing it.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3: real Chrome does not pad its /json/version response, so the cap's original reasoning ("a body this large is not /json/version") holds for the realistic threat. The exposure check is also complemented by the kernel binding check, which runs first when a pid is known.

SMALLEST FIX, for consistency with the deadline: have the cap settle 'timeout' rather than 'other', so an unproven large body leaves the host undecided instead of awarding it a reachability verifier. Note this is a behaviour change for a NON-DevTools peer that legitimately sends more than 64KB - it would move from 'other' to 'timeout' (unknown), which is the safer label but is a change, so it deserves its own review rather than being folded into the deadline fix.

title: uuod follow-up: three test/production P3s already fixed on 779e80d, plus round 5's findings

title: A caller-supplied log that throws after spawn leaks the browser (success path has no try/finally)
description:
FROM the round-2 review of web-uplift-uuod, and the review explicitly agreed that filing it separately was the right call rather than restructuring a security-sensitive function inside a P2 fix. P3.

WHAT: in launchChromeOnce, the success path has no try/finally. If the caller's `log` function throws after the browser has spawned (evidence/cdp.mjs:1255, :1283, :1137), the exception escapes and the spawned browser is never closed; at :1283 the success handle itself is lost, so the caller cannot close it either.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3: the trigger is a caller-supplied logging function, not the security verdict. Production log functions do not throw synchronously in any realistic case. The leak also lasts only until the process exits, because the exit-time sweep in installInterruptNet still kills anything left in liveBrowsers - which is why no profile directories survive a short-lived CLI.

PROPER FIX, which deserves its own review because it restructures the whole post-spawn body: wrap everything after spawn in try/finally with a `handedOff` flag, calling close() unless the success handle was returned. That would also subsume the exposure-probe paths that were fixed individually in web-uplift-uuod.

P3-A FROM THE SAME REVIEW WAS FIXED RATHER THAN FILED: a thrown value that cannot be turned into a string (Object.create(null), or an object whose toString throws, or an Error whose message getter throws) escaped before close() from the catch block, because String(err) sat outside any try. It is now total - the coercion is wrapped and falls back to Object.prototype.toString.call(err).

comments.text:
DUPLICATE of web-uplift-uikn, which coord filed from the same review finding - coord filed at its audit, a few minutes before I created this one, and the check that said "P3-1 was not filed" therefore did not see this. Closing this and keeping uikn as the tracked one, since the hub owns the ledger.

Content is identical: a caller-supplied log that throws after spawn leaks the browser because the success path has no try/finally; proper fix is a try/finally with a handedOff flag, which deserves its own review. P3-A from the same review (a thrown value that cannot be stringified escaping before close) was fixed rather than filed, in de8c237, so neither bead needs to carry it.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
RECON ON CURRENT MASTER (c5e0b57), awaiting wf0r landing before branching.

Confirmed the shape of the defect in launchChromeOnce (evidence/cdp.mjs:985). Every FAILURE path pairs a recordLaunchFailure with an await close(): at 1035 (spawn failed, pid null), 1125/1126 and 1147/1148 (readiness), 1208/1211 (the catch-all), and 1288/1289 plus 1293/1294 (probe outcomes). The SUCCESS path has no equivalent guard, so a caller-supplied log that throws after the browser has spawned propagates out of the function with no handle returned and nothing reaping the process: the caller cannot close what it never received. The module's exit-time sweep over liveBrowsers eventually catches the leftover, which is why this is a resource leak rather than a security hole, but it is unbounded in time for a long-running process.

The agreed fix, which the earlier reviewer said deserves its own review: a try/finally around the post-spawn body with a handedOff flag set immediately before the successful return, so the finally closes the browser only when the handle was never handed to the caller. A returned handle must never be closed by the launcher - the caller owns it, and only a failure that leaves the pid running is a leak.

title: a refusal can be delayed by the slowest probe, whose bound is an idle timeout not a total deadline
description:
Report-only P3 from the second review round of web-uplift-690r, which rated it pre-existing-in-effect and still fail-closed.

WHAT: allSettled waits for the slowest probe, so a DevTools answer on an EARLY host is only reported after every other host settles. Measured by the reviewer: refusal latency 0ms serial against 501ms on this branch when a later probe is slow.

WHY IT IS NOT A BUG IN THIS CHANGE: the launch still waits for the verdict, so it fails closed, and when a pid is known the kernel binding check runs first. What changes is how long an exposed Chrome stays alive before the launch is refused, and the refusal is no longer immediate.

THE SECOND HALF, which is pre-existing: each probe's limit is socket.setTimeout(timeoutMs), an IDLE timeout rather than a total deadline. A peer that trickles bytes can therefore stretch a single probe well past timeoutMs, up to the 64KB response cap. So the 501ms figure is not a hard bound.

SUGGESTED FIX, separately: give probeDevtools a hard total deadline that settles the probe as timeout or other when it expires, independent of socket idleness.

EVIDENCE: reviewer run 8b9cae3c/ee9560fd, harness /tmp/690r-review/h/latency.mjs (serial 0ms vs tip 501ms).
close_reason: Closed

Two mistakes of mine, both in tooling rather than the change:
  1. My first rebase used the branch's FIRST COMMIT as the --onto upstream instead of the old base, so it replayed only the second commit and the deadline itself never applied. The only reason I caught it is that the conflict showed an EMPTY side, which made me look at what HEAD actually contained.

Resolving the registry conflicts as a union of both test names was right for the added-pair blocks but wrong for the chrome-cdp.test.mjs import, which is a single MODIFIED line: the union kept both variants and produced a duplicate import. node --check caught it; the line now names all seven tests. A trickling peer settles at 303ms for a 300ms budget with verdict timeout; the controls measure devtools at 1ms and a plain responder at OTHER at 1ms; the invalid-port child now exits in 2ms against the 5071ms the reviewer measured before the P3-1 fix.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING, because it nearly made me report a false pass. My first attempt at the deadline-deleted mutant applied by regex removed 1687 bytes: after the P3-1 fix the deadline COMMENT sits above const socket = netConnect and the ARM LINE sits below it, so the span swallowed the socket declaration. The mutant died with ReferenceError: socket is not defined. Redirection gave rc=1, which looks exactly like a caught bug - the only thing that exposed it was reading the log instead of trusting the exit code. The precise mutation deletes exactly the one arm line, proves the mutant tree still PARSES and still contains netConnect, and then fails with Error: a trickling peer must leave the host undecided, got other at the assert line - the verdict assertion, not the timing one. The rule: a mutant that breaks the file proves nothing, so the mutant tree must be shown to parse and the failure text must be the assertion's, not a runtime error's.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW ROUND 2 = HOLDS on 22f582d (22f582da3a34334d500803c84f8b05e65e032caa); ITS TWO P3s ARE FIXED AND THE ARTIFACT IS READY.

The reviewer resolved the branch itself and found, correctly, that the duplicate import lived IN COMMIT ONE rather than only in my working tree: tests/chrome-cdp.test.mjs at that commit failed node --check, and regression.mjs imports that file, so the whole suite failed to load there and git bisect would have hit a broken commit. The one-line import fix is now folded into commit one via an interactive rebase, so the history is feature-then-review-response with NEITHER commit broken: both commits parse, verified by extracting each commit's four files and running node --check on each. Its second P3, the indentation my union resolver stripped, is fixed too - ten lines across the three registries.

The delta from the tip it reviewed is proven whitespace-only: git diff against the reviewed sha is 10 insertions and 10 deletions, and the same diff with -w is EMPTY. Behaviour on the new tip: --only Trickling 1/137, --only UnprintableProbeNote 1/137 so the landed lmka test still runs, direct run 12 lines, a trickling peer 303ms with verdict timeout, controls devtools at 1ms and a plain responder at other at 1ms.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: probeDevtools now takes a hard wall-clock deadline at entry, independent of socket idleness, cleared in settle() and armed AFTER netConnect. On expiry the verdict is timeout, or devtools if the body already proved itself, and deliberately never other. A regression test with two controls covers it, and the deadline comment was corrected where it overclaimed.
WHY: socket.setTimeout is an IDLE timeout, so a peer that trickles bytes held the probe indefinitely up to the 64KB cap - measured 2321ms against a 300ms budget. Because cdpEndpointExposure waits for every probe before refusing (correctly, to fail closed), that idle bound was also the effective bound on a refusal. Worse, it was a fail-open: the idle path returned other whenever any text had arrived, so a stalled DevTools body earned a clean reachability verdict (793/800 on the parent against 800/800 timeout on this branch).
EFFECT: a refused launch is bounded by the probe budget instead of an open-ended trickle, and a host that cannot answer within it is reported undecided with no verifier rather than labelled "answers, but not with DevTools". Ordinary peers are unchanged: a real DevTools responder is detected in about 1ms, a non-DevTools responder reads other in about 1ms, and a refused connection is unchanged. The trade-off is stated in the code: a real DevTools answer arriving more slowly than the budget now launches labelled unknown where the parent would have refused it.

title: launchChromeOnce leaks the browser when exposureProbe itself throws (pre-existing)
description:
Found by the independent review of web-uplift-690r, which rated it pre-existing and out of that change's scope (evidence/cdp.mjs around line 1212).

WHAT: the port-transport launch path calls exposureProbe and has no try/close around it. If exposureProbe throws, launchChromeOnce skips recordLaunchFailure and close(), so the spawned Chrome process and its profile directory stay behind. No handle is returned, so the outcome is fail-closed in the sense that no caller gets a live browser, but the process leak is real.

WHY IT MATTERS: an orphaned Chrome holding a profile is exactly the class the reaper hunts, and on a host where the probe throws repeatedly each launch would leave one more.

SMALLEST FIX, from the review: wrap the call in try/catch and treat a throw like the exposed case - refuse fatally after close(), recording the failure like any other launch failure.

EVIDENCE: cdpEndpointExposure only resolves for its production probe (probeDevtools wraps everything in a new Promise), so this needs an injected or future probe to reach; the review reached it by injection. Not reachable through the current production path.
close_reason: Closed

title: [factory-audit/perf-review] Avoid per-call RegExp compilation in classifyClickControl's word matcher
description:
## What
classifyClickControl compiles a new RegExp for every term across WRITE_TERMS and DESTRUCTIVE_WORDS on every evaluated DOM click, causing repeated regex compilation on the page main thread.

## Location & Evidence
- `runner/flow.mjs:216` (and vendored mirror `.web-uplift/runner/flow.mjs:216`)
- `const wordMatch = (text, term) => new RegExp('(^|[^a-z0-9])' + term + '($|[^a-z0-9])', 'i').test(text);`
- Evaluated inside `classifyClickControl` which is serialized via `.toString()` and injected into the audited page context for every click/doubleClick step (`runner/flow.mjs:373`).

## Mechanism & Impact
`WRITE_TERMS` contains ~50 entries and `DESTRUCTIVE_WORDS` has ~15 entries. On every click, `wordMatch` is invoked against both label and name for all terms, compiling 100+ RegExp instances synchronously per click event. This represents unnecessary CPU and INP overhead during in-page flow execution and recording.

## Station Citation & Severity Rationale
- Station: `perf-review` (`heavy-json-or-regex-in-hotpath`). Run: 20261010T031848Z, target `origin/master@5eb6b44`.
- Severity: Station rated Medium. Mapped to P3 task.

## Remediation
Replace the dynamic RegExp with an allocation-free whole-word substring match using `String#indexOf` and boundary checks matching `(^|[^a-z0-9])term($|[^a-z0-9])` case-insensitively. The helper must remain self-contained within `classifyClickControl` so it survives `.toString()` serialization without external module references. Resync `.web-uplift/runner/flow.mjs`.
close_reason: Closed

WHY: classifyClickControl is serialized via .toString() and injected into the audited page context on every evaluated click/doubleClick step, where compiling ~65 dynamic RegExps per click introduced main thread execution and INP overhead.
EFFECT: Faster in-page flow replay and recording with 0 RegExp allocations across WRITE_TERMS and DESTRUCTIVE_WORDS (~4.25x faster in word matching throughput) while preserving exact whole-word matching semantics.
