title: launchChrome can return a handle for a browser that already exited during the exposure probe
description:
Pre-existing, found by the claude-opus-5-5 review of fleet/pipe-close-polish @ 540d7e7, which correctly did NOT attribute it to that change.

DEFECT: on the port path the DevTools endpoint promise resolves as soon as Chrome prints its listening line, so if Chrome then exits before or during the subsequent exposure check, the exit listener's reject is a no-op on an already-resolved promise. launchChrome then returns a SUCCESSFUL handle for a dead browser. The reviewer reproduced it with a fake that prints the DevTools line and exits 3: launchChrome returned a handle with exitCode=3.

NOT CAUSED BY 540d7e7: the same holds before the port-path stderr detach, because the resolution has already happened.

SMALLEST FIX: after the exposure probe resolves, assert the process is still alive before returning the success handle, and fail the attempt with the usual describeLaunchFailure detail if not, which also makes a crashed launch retry as it should.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
Source: the claude-opus-5-5 review of fleet/pipe-close-polish @ 540d7e7 (the dynamic re-review, which ran its own mutations in a /tmp copy). The reviewer found this while probing the port-path stderr detach for the awkward case - a Chrome that prints its DevTools line and then dies - and explicitly did NOT count it against that branch, because resolving the endpoint promise first means the later exit cannot reject it, whether or not the listener is detached.

Reproduced by the reviewer: a fake that prints the DevTools listening line and exits with code 3 leaves launchChrome returning a handle with exitCode=3. So the caller gets a success object for a browser that is already gone, and the attempt is never retried, which is the part worth fixing: a launch that dies during the probe should retry like any other failed launch.

Recorded here rather than in the branch it was found on, per coord's rule that a pre-existing finding gets its own bead rather than riding someone else's change.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
CLAIMED by web-uplift-mwg-drift. Queue position per coord: behind met0/diaq/1lif and the ear, and it lands with its own review.

APPROACH, recorded now so it does not have to be re-derived later (from the reviewer's description, which is exact enough to act on):
- Where: the port path, after the exposure probe resolves and BEFORE the success handle is returned. The pipe path needs the same question asked of it, because a pipe has no endpoint promise to resolve but the child can still die; check both rather than only the path the reviewer happened to test.
- What: assert the child is still alive (and the transport still usable) at that point. If it is not, fail the attempt through the existing failure path with describeLaunchFailure's detail, so the diagnosis is the same shape as every other launch failure rather than a new error format.
- Why it is not merely cosmetic: failing there means the retry logic sees a failed attempt, which is the actual defect - today a browser that died during the probe is reported as a successful launch and is never retried.
- Test to insist on: a fake that prints the DevTools listening line and then exits non-zero, asserting launchChrome REJECTS (and, if the retry budget allows, retries), plus a control where the same fake stays alive and the launch SUCCEEDS. Without the control, a launcher that simply failed every launch would pass.

Do not fold this into e93a028 or 540d7e7: both are frozen and waiting to land.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
FIXED on fleet/py0e-liveness @ 5654356, based on current master (post-diaq) and touching NO .web-uplift/ files, per the structural note that all pre-diaq vendored edits are obsolete. in_review; a claude-opus-5-5 review is in flight.

REPRODUCED BEFORE FIXING, on current master: a fake that prints the DevTools listening line and exits 3 leaves launchChrome returning a SUCCESS handle - "launch RETURNED A HANDLE. proc.exitCode=3 alive=false", handle.port=1. The endpoint promise resolved on the announcement, so the exit listener's reject was a no-op on a settled promise.

AFTER: "launch REJECTED (good): Chrome launch failed after 3 attempt(s); reasons: the browser exited (code 3, signal null) before the launch completed". Note it RETRIES three times, which is the actual repair - the attempt is now seen as failed.
CONTROL: the same announcing fake that stays alive still launches (port=1, alive=true), so a launcher that failed every launch could not pass this test.

MY FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX WAS INSUFFICIENT, and the new test caught it: checking process state alone is a race, because exitCode and signalCode are only set once Node has OBSERVED the exit, so a browser that died microseconds earlier still looks alive. The test passed once and then failed on that version. The fix now waits out a bounded 250ms exit settle before checking. That settle costs up to 250ms on a SUCCESSFUL launch; a CDP-level liveness round trip would be exact and free but the launcher has no session yet at that point, so the trade is stated in the code rather than hidden and is called out for the reviewer to challenge.

MUTATION, characterised honestly rather than claimed as a clean kill: with the settle removed, the new assertion FAILED 1 run in 4 and passed the other three. That is the true shape of a timing bug, and it is why the evidence is "5/5 with the settle, 1-in-4 failure without it" rather than a single decisive run.

Census: four new sites, all bounded:pre-existing-mechanism (the two settles and the two teardowns), 11 -> 13.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW 5654356: HOLDS (claude-opus-5-5, dynamic - it ran everything and did its own experiments: three code versions x four cases x 10 launches, /proc/<pid>/stat logging at the check, and median timings). Its words: "the code fix is correct, and I found no defect in it". All findings were in the tests or the comments.

WHAT IT ADDED THAT I HAD MISSED: the PIPE path is the one that matters. Every production caller uses the default pipe transport (evidence/cli.mjs, runner/run-batch.mjs, runner/flow.mjs), and on master that path returned a dead handle 10 runs out of 10. On the pipe path the check WITHOUT its trial window caught 0 of 10. So the half of the fix I had treated as symmetry with the port path is the substantial half.

TWO OF MY CLAIMS WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED. (1) The cost is FIXED ~250ms on every successful launch, not a ceiling - waitForProcExit only returns early once the process has exited - measured ~267ms port, ~335ms pipe against ~35ms and ~119ms without. "Up to 250ms" understated it. (2) "A CDP-level liveness round trip would be exact and free" was false, and its /proc logging is why: on the pipe path the browser was still RUNNING (R/S) and exited 2-7ms later, so ANY instant check passes, CDP or not, and there IS a live pipe so "no session yet" was untrue. It is a short TRIAL WINDOW, which is the right design.

FIXED on fleet/py0e-findings @ b647daf, stacked on 5654356: the missing pipe test (P2, in tests/cdp-pipe-transport.mjs, its fake speaking the --remote-debugging-pipe contract directly - fd 3 in, fd 4 out, no Buffer), the retry assertion so making this failure fatal would break the test, both corrected comments, the new block moved above the wedge comment it had split, and the direct run of that file now executing every test - which was STILL OPEN ON MASTER, because the fix for it had ridden the withdrawn 540d7e7.

ONE MEASURED DISAGREEMENT, recorded in the code rather than smoothed over: review expected a synchronous exposureProbe stub to make the port case deterministic and measured 10/10. I measure the OPPOSITE - with the stub that case caught 0 of 8, against about 1 in 4 with the real probe - because the stub removes the pauses the race needs, i.e. it removed coverage rather than flakiness. I reverted it. The deterministic guard is the pipe test: with the settle removed it failed 8 runs of 8.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
STUB DISAGREEMENT RESOLVED, by re-running the first reviewer's OWN harness rather than re-asserting my numbers. /tmp/rvw/drive.mjs with its own variants and fakes, port transport, N=6 per cell:
  master   + real probe -> 6/6 dead handles (the defect)
  nosettle + REAL probe -> 6/6 CAUGHT (rejects with the new reason)
  nosettle + SYNC stub  -> 6/6 dead handles, i.e. caught NOTHING
My 0-of-8-with-the-stub matches that 0-of-6 exactly, and it confirms the direction I measured: the stub removes the very pauses the race needs, so it removes coverage rather than flakiness. With the REAL probe the no-settle version IS caught - 6 of 6 on that harness under load, against about 1 in 4 for me unloaded - so the real-probe rate is load-dependent, and my unloaded number was the low end rather than the wrong end.

WHERE THE FIRST REVIEW WAS RIGHT AND WHERE IT WAS NOT: its TABLE said "settle removed | 10/10 dead" for the stub row, which agrees with me - dead handles are the defect escaping. Its PROSE recommended adding the stub and reported the settle-removed version failing 10 of 10 with it, which does not. title: redactUrlCredentialValues: two unparseable-URL userinfo boundaries the sweep deliberately does not cover
description:
Review findings from the 73y3 sweep review, filed as boundaries rather than silently ignored. Neither is a regression introduced by the fix; both are shapes that reach the redactor and keep a credential.

(1) A special-scheme URL written WITHOUT slashes after the colon is not swept: 'https:user:secret@x.test:99999/a' and the backslash variant come back verbatim, because the sweep anchors on two slash-or-backslash characters. In a string that already failed to parse, 'scheme:text@' is indistinguishable from an opaque path, and a mailto address is the everyday case, so sweeping it would redact innocent prose to cover a shape that needs BOTH a missing separator and an invalid port to arise. Fixing it properly needs a scheme-aware anchor plus a rule for telling an opaque path from a broken authority.

(2) Pre-existing and outside 73y3's whole scope: a nested URL inside a query value whose name is not credential-shaped leaks, raw or percent-encoded: '?next=https://user:secret@y/' is left alone. The shared redactor only rewrites the value of a credential-named parameter, so a URL smuggled through an arbitrary parameter name survives. This is the same class as the prose scanner's problem (a URL inside a larger string) and would want the URL-start scanner applied to parameter values.

Both need a decision about how far to redact versus how much innocent text to damage, which is why they are beads and not a quiet widening of the sweep.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text: Third boundary of the same family, added while fixing the review finding that searched for one backslash instead of two. A URL written with a SINGLE backslash before its userinfo ('https:\user:secret@x.test:99999/a') is left verbatim: two characters are the only spelling the sweep treats as an authority boundary, because a lone backslash is a path separator in ordinary prose, and the string only reaches the sweep at all when it has already failed to parse (so it needs both that spelling and an invalid port). The important difference from before: it is now left ALONE rather than mangled - the old code treated the single backslash as a delimiter and printed the first character of the userinfo. Whether a lone backslash should be redacted needs the same decision as the sections above, so it belongs here rather than in a quiet widening.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
Two more boundaries of the same family, both from the third review round of the sweep rather than from my own sweep of edge cases.

(1) A special-scheme URL with ZERO or ONE slash-or-backslash before its userinfo is not swept at all, so it keeps its credential: 'https:user:secret@x.test:99999/a', 'https:/user:secret@...', 'https:\user:secret@...'. The reviewer showed this is NOT the same as the prose case: the in-text scanner's URL_START requires a slash immediately after the scheme colon, so it never hands these shapes to the sweep, and for the special schemes every browser reads 'scheme:' followed by any number of slashes - including none - as an authority. So these are URL attempts, not prose, and they are the same class as the mixed pair that was fixed. The fix belongs in one place: treat a special-scheme name + ':' + zero or more [\/] as an authority start, which closes the no-slash, one-slash, one-backslash and mixed forms together without matching a bare backslash in ordinary text.
(2) Pre-existing: the sweep ends a run at tab, LF or CR, but a URL parser REMOVES those characters anywhere in the input, so in a string like 'https://us<TAB>er:pw@x.test:99999/' the run stops early and the remainder of the userinfo is left behind. Fixing it means stripping (or skipping) those three characters when locating the run, which changes run semantics, so it is filed rather than done quietly.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
CLAIM RELEASED. I filed this from the third review round of the 73y3 sweep and am no longer working it, so it is unclaimed and ready for coord to route. The boundaries are exact and do not overlap the frozen branch: this is follow-up work in evidence/credential-terms.mjs, and any fix belongs on a NEW branch stacked on a2637f3 rather than on fleet/chain-await-census, which is frozen.

Order of value if someone picks it up: (1) the special-scheme anchor form, because it is the same class as the mixed-pair defect that was already proven to leak - a special-scheme name plus ':' plus zero or more slash-or-backslash characters is an authority start, and today only two-character pairs are seen; (2) the tab/LF/CR run-break mismatch, which needs run-finding to skip the three characters a URL parser removes anywhere, so it is a bigger change and should carry its own regression tests; (3) the nested-URL-in-a-non-credential-named-query-value case, which is pre-existing and documented rather than introduced.

Three assertions plus a control were added, and a mutation that puts '\t' back into the break set fires the first assertion with the password visible in its own message. The reach is redactHeaderList, where an internal tab is legal in an HTTP field value.

So this bead now covers boundaries (1) and (3) only: the special-scheme anchor form (still leaking on master, pre-existing, needs a scheme-aware anchor rather than a wider pair search) and the nested URL in a non-credential-named query value (pre-existing). title: [evidence] a protocol-relative URL with a password but no username is re-emitted malformed
description:
Review finding (P3, minor) on web-uplift-53o1, tip 17c30c1, from antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash. Pre-existing shape edge, not introduced by that fix and not a leak - 53o1's verified tip is deliberately left in place rather than moved for it.

Repro (no browser):
  node -e "import('/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-mwg-drift/evidence/credential-terms.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.redactUrlCredentialValues('//:s3cr3t@x.test/a?token=NOPE')))"
Observed: //:s3cr3tx.test/a?token=%5Bredacted%5D   - the '@' is missing, so the password and the host run together.
Expected: //:s3cr3t@x.test/a?token=%5Bredacted%5D

Cause: the re-emitted userinfo appends '@' only when u.username is non-empty:
  const userinfo = `${u.username}${u.password ? ':' + u.password : ''}${u.username ? '@' : ''}`;
For '//:s3cr3t@x.test/..' the WHATWG parser gives username '' and password 's3cr3t', so no '@' is appended.

Smallest fix, one condition: use (u.username || u.password) ? '@' : ''.

Scope note: only protocol-relative inputs that ALSO carry a credential-named query parameter reach this branch (the function returns the raw string when nothing is redacted), and a password-only userinfo is exotic, which is why this is a P3 rather than something worth moving a reviewed tip for. Related: web-uplift-73y3 is the separate question of whether userinfo credentials should be redacted at all.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW PASS (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, different family): VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no findings. Ticketed tip stays fleet/redact-empty-username @ fdf7880.

It attacked (a) properly instead of checking my one example, and did it against Node's WHATWG parser rather than against the code's own assumptions: '//:@host/' and '//@host/' resolve to EMPTY username and password, so hasUserinfo is false and the rebuild emits no stray '@' - which matches URL.toString() in the absolute branch; '//::@host/' (password is ':'), '//:@@host/' (first '@' is part of the password), '//user:p@ss@host/' (internal '@' belongs to the password) and a percent-encoded '@' in the username all redact and rebuild correctly; and a password-only userinfo on an IPv6 host with a port ('//:%5Bredacted%5D@[2001:db8::1]:8080') keeps its brackets and port. It also confirmed the interaction with 73y3 (the leading ':' now makes the empty username explicit, so the marker cannot be read as part of the host) and with 53o1 (userinfo is inserted between '//' and u.host, with leading whitespace and port untouched).

It also backed the boundary I recorded rather than taking my word for it: per RFC 3986 section 3.3 a single leading slash is a path-absolute reference, not an authority, and ':' and '@' are legal pchar characters, so '/:s3cr3t@x.test/a?token=..' is a path and only its query credential is redacted - treating it as userinfo would break legitimate Location values like '/:param' or '/@user/feed'.

Caveat it stated: it did not run the Chrome-dependent full suite; it ran tests/credential-redaction.mjs, tests/console-evidence-redaction.mjs and tests/log-redaction.mjs, and the browser coverage is the merger's full gate.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: the protocol-relative branch of redactUrlCredentialValues emits '@' for any non-empty userinfo instead of only when a username exists, so a URL with a password and an empty username keeps a valid authority; tests/credential-redaction.mjs section 8 pins password-only userinfo, the same with a query credential, parity with the absolute branch, and a no-userinfo control, all through both exported redactors.
WHY: '//:s3cr3t@x.test/a?token=..' was re-emitted as '//:%5Bredacted%5Dx.test/a?token=..', the redacted userinfo running into the host, so an artifact or HAR entry showed a host that was never requested.
EFFECT: the recorded URL is the one that was requested; no change to what is redacted, since web-uplift-73y3 already redacted that password.

title: [fejl residual] page-side isSensitiveField element adapter is still hand-written; the test does not assert source identity
description:
Raised by mwg-drift while withdrawing its duplicate fejl branch. The fix that LANDs (web-uplift-fejl, commit 4a2830c on fleet/flow-record-residuals) single-sources the word data and the classifier functions from evidence/credential-terms.mjs, but runner/flow-record.mjs:495 still keeps a HAND-WRITTEN element adapter for isSensitiveField (where mwg-drift's version runs the module's own function). Its test proves the word-data path behaviourally but does NOT assert source identity, so a hand copy that is behaviourally identical yet textually drifted would still pass - the exact silent-drift failure mode fejl named.

Expected: generate the element adapter from the module source (or inject it), and add an assertion that the page-side implementation is derived from the module rather than a copy.

Reference implementation (stricter, already has two HOLDS from independent review): mwg-drift's fleet/flow-record-classifier @c69a281 - needs a rebase onto current master if reused, or take the idea. Non-blocking; post-landing follow-up. Owner: coord to route (mwg-drift after 53o1).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/fejl-adapter-source @ 72b37fe (one commit, based on origin/master 526a1ed). Independent review dispatched (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol); the verdict goes on this bead when it returns.

WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY: the failure this bead names is the one fejl exists to prevent, one layer down. After the landed fejl fix, the page script's word data and word-matching helpers were injected from the module - but the element adapter (isSensitiveField) was still a hand-written rewrite of the module's function, and the test proved only that the two AGREED BEHAVIOURALLY. A copy that behaves identically while drifting textually - a renamed local, a branch the test list never exercises, a subtle reordering that happens to give the same answers on the covered inputs - would pass the entire suite while being a second implementation of the rule that decides what gets written to flow.json, the file this tool tells operators to treat as a secret.

FIX: the adapter IS the module's function now. makeCaptureJs injects hasSensitiveWord (which the module's isSensitiveField calls) and isSensitiveField itself, verbatim, and the page keeps a one-line wrapper whose only job is to bind the capture flags the module takes as options to the CAPTURE_* constants the script was configured with. The hand-written rewrite is deleted; the call site (const sensitive = isSensitiveField(el)) is unchanged.

TEST (tests/flow.mjs, new section 5): nine generated classifiers (hasSensitiveWord, isSensitiveField, isSensitiveAutocomplete, isSensitiveName, isSensitiveWord, splitName, member, isCredentialWord, isPiiWord) must each appear in the generated script exactly once, verbatim from the module; the wrapper must contain the delegation WITH both flags bound; and the deleted hand-written adapter's shape must be absent.

THE MUTATIONS ARE THE POINT, because this bead exists precisely because a behavioural test could not see the difference:
- a hand-written adapter that is BEHAVIOURALLY IDENTICAL but textually drifted (renamed locals) fails with "must contain the module's isSensitiveField exactly once (found 0)";
- an exactly IDENTICAL duplicate copy fails with "(found 2)" - so a textually faithful second implementation is caught too, which a pure "includes" assertion would have missed;
- dropping the flag binding fails the delegation assertion.
Each restored byte-identically by md5 (files backed up before mutating).

Also checked rather than assumed: the module's adapter is a SUPERSET of the hand-written one for real elements (it reads autocomplete/ariaLabel/placeholder as properties and falls back to getAttribute, so an element whose property is set without the attribute is now caught where it previously was not); the change listener still skips hidden inputs before classifying, which agrees with the classifier's own captureHidden handling; and every injected function is both defined and used (no dead code left behind by the removal - measured, minimum two occurrences each).

Verified: tests/flow.mjs tests OK (the mutant-word and autocomplete-agreement sections still pass, so the injected word data is unchanged), tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs tests OK - a real browser, so the generated script still records in the recorder's isolated world - tests/credential-redaction.mjs tests OK, tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs all 23 vendored copies identical, regression filters Console, Evidence, Flow, Sensitive and Record all tests OK.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: makeCaptureJs now injects the module's own hasSensitiveWord and isSensitiveField into the page script, and the page keeps only a one-line wrapper binding CAPTURE_HIDDEN/CAPTURE_SENSITIVE to the module's options; the hand-written element adapter is removed. tests/flow.mjs section 5 asserts source identity and single definition for all nine generated classifiers, the flag-binding delegation, and the absence of the old shape.
WHY: the element adapter was the last hand-maintained copy of the sensitive-field classifier, with only behavioural coverage, so a textually drifted but behaviourally identical copy could silently decide what the recorder writes to flow.json.
EFFECT: a drift in the element classifier is now impossible by construction rather than by testing, and any second copy - including a faithful one - fails the suite with a message naming the function.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW PASS 1 on 72b37fe (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol): REQUEST CHANGES / BLOCK, one P2 in-delta - and it was RIGHT, which I confirmed in a real browser rather than in a mock.

The P2: passing the element straight to the module changed WHICH FIELDS GET RECORDED. The module also accepts a plain descriptor object, so it falls back from a property to getAttribute() for fields an element may not have. A <select> has no placeholder IDL property, so an inert placeholder attribute - never rendered by a select - made the field sensitive and the recorder blanked a legitimate value that the old hand-written adapter had retained.

Real-browser evidence, because the whole question is a DOM property-versus-attribute distinction and the reviewer was right that a test double can model it wrongly:
- Chrome facts on the actual page: `'placeholder' in select` is false, `select.getAttribute('placeholder')` is 'Email'.
- Fixed tree, real <select name="city" placeholder="Email">, changed by a trusted ArrowDown: recorded step is {"value":"London"} with NO redacted flag.
- Same page, with ONLY that one read mutated back to the attribute fallback: {"value":"","redacted":true}. So the browser check is sensitive to exactly the bug, and the bug was real rather than an artifact of the mock.
I also checked the other direction: property-only `autocomplete` is semantically EQUIVALENT (it is a reflected IDL attribute), so no test can or should distinguish it. The placeholder read is the only non-equivalent one.

FIX (3a8c073 on fleet/fejl-adapter-source-fix, stacked on the reviewed 72b37fe which is left frozen): the page wrapper builds the descriptor explicitly with the property/attribute choices the old adapter made - type/name/id/labels/placeholder as properties, autocomplete and aria-label as attributes - and hands that to the module. The wrapper still decides nothing itself; classification remains the module's.

Fix-review also taken: the delegation assertion is now two independent facts (a descriptor call, both capture flags bound) so a legitimate reformat cannot fail it, and the "no second implementation" guard is rule-level - the `type === 'password'` branch must appear exactly once in the page script - rather than matching the old adapter's exact shape, which any rewrite would evade. Harness gained triggerChangeOn(), because mockEl merges properties and attributes into one namespace and so cannot express "attribute yes, property no".

Tests: inert placeholder attribute on a select must not blank its value; the same element WITH a real placeholder property must still be redacted (so the guard is about the distinction, not about ignoring placeholders). Mutations: restoring the attribute fallback fails exactly that select assertion (measured); passing the element straight through fails the delegation assertion; a hand-written or duplicated adapter still fails the exactly-once guard. All restored byte-identically by md5.

One correction to my own earlier comment on this bead, since the reviewer flagged it: I claimed tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs verified that the generated script "still records in the recorder's isolated world". It does not - it exercises replay, not the recorder path. The browser evidence above is what actually drives the recorder, and it is in this comment rather than in a test: the committed mock test catches the same mutation, and adding a Chrome launch to the suite for this would cost CPU for a case a purpose-built element shape already covers.

Verified on 3a8c073: tests/flow.mjs tests OK, tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs tests OK, tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs all 23 vendored copies identical, regression filters Console, Evidence, Flow, Sensitive and Record all tests OK. Review pass 2 dispatched (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, fresh family); the bead stays IN_REVIEW and the landing tip for this bead is now 3a8c073.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: makeCaptureJs now injects the module's own hasSensitiveWord and isSensitiveField and keeps a wrapper that builds the SAME DOM descriptor the removed hand-written adapter read (type/name/id/labels/placeholder as properties, autocomplete and aria-label as attributes) before delegating, so classification is the module's and the reads are unchanged. tests/flow.mjs asserts source identity and single definition for the nine injected classifiers, delegates-and-binds-flags, one password rule in the page script, and that an inert placeholder attribute on a select does not blank its value.
WHY: the element adapter was the last hand-maintained copy of the sensitive-field classifier, so a textually drifted copy could silently decide what the recorder writes to flow.json; making it generated then briefly changed which fields get recorded, because the module's descriptor fallbacks treat a select's inert placeholder attribute as a signal.
EFFECT: a drift in the element classifier is impossible by construction rather than by testing, and no legitimate value is blanked by an attribute the browser never renders as a placeholder.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW PASS 2 on the fixed tip 3a8c073 (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, fresh family): VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no findings. Landing tip stays fleet/fejl-adapter-source-fix @ 3a8c073.

It did the thing that actually settles a fidelity question rather than trusting the tests: a field-by-field table of the old hand-written adapter against the descriptor the wrapper now builds against what the module reads - type, name, id, autocomplete, aria-label, placeholder, labels, the falsy guard and the flags - and concluded no real element is classified differently in either direction, with no false negatives (nothing newly recorded that used to be redacted). It also enumerated the property/attribute divergence cases and showed which can even reach the change listener: a select and a form-associated custom element can, SVG/XML/div/span/contenteditable cannot, because the listener requires 'value' in el and a trusted change. It confirmed attr()'s guard for exotic objects and that a live NodeList passed as `labels` is consumed synchronously by Array.from, so there is no iteration race.

It also validated two judgement calls I had asked it to attack rather than accept: keeping the test guard in tests/flow.mjs rather than adding a Chrome launch to the quick suite (the distinction is IDL property presence, which the VM harness reproduces exactly and which is standardised across engines, unlike the native shadow-DOM traversal that flow-shadow-browser exists for), and the rule-level "exactly once" assertion for the password branch being strictly stronger than the brittle negative regex it replaced.

Caveat it stated itself, recorded here rather than glossed: it reviewed statically and could not execute the suites, so the run evidence remains mine (tests/flow.mjs, tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs, cdp-copy-sync, regression filters Console/Evidence/Flow/Sensitive/Record), and the real-browser select evidence is the throwaway Chrome check described in the previous comment.

title: [evidence] redactUrlCredentialValues re-emits a protocol-relative URL as a path, silently dropping the host
description:
Found while fixing web-uplift-lsn3 (fleet/lsn3-console-redaction, 2026-10-09). Not a credential leak, and not introduced by that branch: the function was moved verbatim into evidence/credential-terms.mjs.

Repro (no browser):
  node -e "import('/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-mwg-drift/evidence/credential-terms.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.redactUrlCredentialValues('//x.test/a?token=SECRETVALUE1234567890')))"
Observed: /a?token=%5Bredacted%5D   - the host and scheme-relative prefix are GONE.
Expected: //x.test/a?token=%5Bredacted%5D

Cause: new URL(raw) throws for a protocol-relative string, so the relative fallback path runs and re-emits only `${u.pathname}${u.search}${u.hash}` - which drops the host whenever the input was '//host/path'. The credential is still redacted, so this is a fidelity bug rather than an exposure: an artifact or HAR entry shows a URL that was never requested.

Where it bites: redactUrlCredentialValues is used for redirect Location headers (evidence/cli.mjs, several call sites) and now for console-evidence urls/text. A protocol-relative Location ('//cdn.example/next?session=...') is uncommon but legal.

Smallest fix: in the relative fallback, if the parsed URL has a host (i.e. the input began with '//'), re-emit it as `//${u.host}${u.pathname}${u.search}${u.hash}`. Existing relative-path behaviour must not change.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/redact-proto-relative-fix @ 17c30c1 (two commits: db26365, 17c30c1), stacked on fleet/lsn3-separator-holdback @ 03b9277 because both edit the same function and an independent base would conflict in evidence/credential-terms.mjs. e976a29 (the first attempt) is BLOCKED by review and is deliberately left where it is; the final tip is 17c30c1.

REPRODUCED (before/after, no browser):
  before: //x.test/a?token=SECRET -> /a?token=%5Bredacted%5D      <- host silently gone
  after:  //x.test/a?token=SECRET -> //x.test/a?token=%5Bredacted%5D
Cause: new URL('//x.test/a?token=..') throws without a base, so this fell into the relative-path fallback, which re-emitted only pathname+search+hash. Not a credential leak - the value was redacted either way - which is why it hid for so long: the output looked plausible while the artifact or HAR entry showed a URL that was never requested. It bites the HAR redirect Location path (evidence/cli.mjs) and, since lsn3, the console-evidence prose path.

FIX (three parts, all measured):
1. The relative fallback re-emits the authority when the input is protocol-relative.
2. Leading whitespace counts, because an HTTP field value may carry it and the URL parser strips it - testing only for '//' at index 0 left exactly the same host-loss (found by sweeping after the first fix).
3. Userinfo is re-emitted too, and the comment stating the opposite ("unchanged behaviour for the absolute branch too") was simply wrong: the absolute branch keeps 'user:pass@' via URL.toString(). Neither branch REDACTES userinfo - that is a separate scope decision, filed as web-uplift-73y3 [P2] with the repro.
The whitespace the parser stripped is re-appended rather than normalised away: this function redacts one value, it does not tidy a header value into a different string.

REVIEW (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, independent family): pass 1 = REQUEST CHANGES / BLOCK, 4 findings. Findings 1 (leading whitespace), 2 (userinfo + wrong comment) and 4 (missing edge assertions) were the corrections I had already made locally from my own edge-case sweep before the verdict arrived - which is precisely why the tip is 17c30c1 and the reviewed e976a29 is left frozen. Finding 3 (my test block was inserted mid-section-5 and numbered 9, splitting the section) is fixed: it now sits after section 5 as section 6 and the file reads 1-6 contiguously. Pass 2 is running on 03b9277..17c30c1.

TEST (tests/credential-redaction.mjs section 6, driven through BOTH exported redactors): host preserved, host:port preserved, bracketed IPv6 preserved, fragment preserved, userinfo preserved, leading space and tab, rooted relative path unchanged by the fix, absolute branch unchanged, no-credential control, unparseable string left alone. Mutation: reverting the whole fallback fails the first assertion, byte-identically restored by md5.

STATED BOUNDARIES, not left implied: '//?token=..' (empty authority) makes the URL parser throw and takes the documented "leave an unparseable string alone" path, so a credential there survives; a credential in the FRAGMENT is out of scope; and userinfo is out of scope for this redactor. The first two are in the test comments, the third is web-uplift-73y3.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: redactUrlCredentialValues now re-emits the authority (host:port, plus userinfo) when it rewrites a protocol-relative URL instead of emitting only its path, allows leading whitespace before the '//', and re-appends whitespace the URL parser stripped. Its comment now states the real relationship to the absolute branch. tests/credential-redaction.mjs gains section 6 covering the shapes through both exported redactors.
WHY: a protocol-relative redirect Location or console URL lost its host in the artifact while looking plausible, because the relative-path fallback rebuilt the URL without it.
EFFECT: an artifact or HAR entry now shows the URL that was actually requested, with only the credential-named query parameter values replaced.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REVIEW PASS 2 (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash, independent family): VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK. Tip unchanged at 17c30c1, so the branch that carries the HOLDS is the branch in the queue.

It confirmed the four parts of the fix, the test coverage through both exported redactors, and the file parity between evidence/ and .web-uplift/evidence/. It also explicitly AGREED with the two boundaries I asked it to challenge: '//?token=..' (empty authority) taking the documented unparseable path is right, because that function is also applied to prose and heuristically mutating unparseable text would corrupt it; and fragment credentials belong to a dedicated token sanitizer rather than this query-parameter redactor.

Its one P3 note, which I have filed rather than fixed here: a protocol-relative URL with a password but NO username ('//:s3cr3t@x.test/a?token=..') loses its '@', so the password runs into the host. One-condition fix ((u.username || u.password) ? '@' : ''), only reachable when a credential parameter is also present, not a leak. Filed separately so this verified tip is not moved for an exotic shape; see the review-finding bead.

Both review rounds are now on the record: pass 1 REQUEST CHANGES with 4 findings (2 of which I had already fixed locally from my own sweep), pass 2 HOLDS + merge OK. This bead is ready to land, stacked on the lsn3 follow-up branch as explained above.

title: [4rv follow-up] adopt --remote-debugging-pipe so no local process can attach to the audit browser
description: Offered by mwg-drift while fixing web-uplift-4rv. 4rv pins and verifies the CDP endpoint to loopback and refuses to launch on exposure, but any LOCAL process can still attach to the loopback devtools port for the life of the audit. The real fix is Chrome's --remote-debugging-pipe, which requires switching the CDP transport from websocket to the fd pipe. That is a different transport, so it is tracked here rather than smuggled into 4rv. Owner: coord to route. Referenced in the README residual note from 4rv.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
REPRODUCED (before), and the claim in the bead is stronger than stated: it is not just "can attach", a separate process can drive the audit browser.

Evidence, /tmp/j3re-repro.mjs, run against the current launcher:
- a SEPARATE node process (spawned child, not the launcher) fetched http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version and got HTTP 200 with the full browser identity ("Chrome/154.0.8037.92", Protocol-Version 1.3);
- a separate CDP session then attached to the same port and evaluated in a target ("document.title + location.origin" returned " (null)" on about:blank, i.e. the evaluate ran). That is the whole risk: a local process can read every page the audit holds open, run script in them, and drive the browser as the operator for the life of the run.
The prober is a separate process deliberately: the claim is about other processes, not about the launcher's own connection. Chrome was closed in a finally and none of mine was left running.

SCOPE, and why this is not a small change (flagged to coord as a transport swap):
- Launch: `--remote-debugging-port=0` becomes `--remote-debugging-pipe`, with fds 3 and 4 as Chrome's command/response channels, NUL-terminated JSON frames. Port discovery disappears, including the stderr "DevTools listening on ws://" parse.
- Client: the browser-level pipe gives no webSocketDebuggerUrl, so a small CDP client over the pipe is needed (send with an optional sessionId, flat session routing). No new npm dependency: chrome-remote-interface cannot take a pipe, and the repo's rule is no new dependency, so this is a ~100-line transport with the same surface the call sites use (`session.client.<Domain>.<method>`, `session.close()`).
- Call sites to update: evidence/cdp.mjs (the launcher/attach), runner/flow.mjs (2), runner/run-batch.mjs (1), and the tests that launch browsers: tests/launch-loop.mjs, tests/no-orphan-browser.mjs, tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs, tests/regression.mjs, tests/cdp-endpoint-exposure.mjs (which is 4rv's, on its own branch - see below).
- The 4rv guard: with a pipe there is no listening socket at all, so the endpoint-exposure guard becomes about the RETAINED port path. Plan: pipe is the default, the port path stays behind an explicit opt-in so 4rv's guard keeps protecting it, and the pipe path gains a test that asserts NO listening socket exists for the browser pid (read the pid's socket inodes and look for LISTEN rows, the same kernel-read approach 4rv already uses).
- Stacking: 4rv's work (fleet/cdp-endpoint-guard @ a4cd289) is still in the queue and also touches evidence/cdp.mjs, so this should land after it and stack on whatever tip it lands as, rather than racing it in the same file. I will confirm the base with coord before starting the branch.

Status: IN PROGRESS. Repro done and recorded; implementation is next, and it is a real transport change rather than a one-liner, so it gets its own review and its own verification (the repro above has to FAIL afterwards: no port to probe, no attach).

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
SURFACE MAPPED and branch started (nothing pushed yet - this is the design step, not the implementation).

Branch fleet/cdp-pipe in a dedicated worktree, based on 4rv's PASSed tip a4cd289 as planned, so it stacks on 4rv rather than racing it in evidence/cdp.mjs.

What a pipe client has to provide, counted from the callers rather than guessed: session.client (12), session.close (10), chrome.port (10), chrome.close (10), chrome.proc (7), chrome.userDataDir (2), and on the client: Page.navigate/captureScreenshot, Network.emulateNetworkConditions/responseReceived/requestWillBeSent, Runtime.evaluate, Page.loadEventFired, Input.dispatchKeyEvent, Emulation.setScriptExecutionDisabled/setDeviceMetricsOverride, Tracing.start/end/tracingComplete/dataCollected, ServiceWorker.enable/workerVersionUpdated/workerRegistrationUpdated/workerErrorReported. That is a generic Domain.method surface plus events, which a Proxy can serve without hand-coding the protocol - the reason a small own client is viable rather than a dependency.

Three decisions that make it small:
1. newSession takes the LAUNCH HANDLE, not a number: a number keeps the websocket port path (and 4rv's exposure guard with it), an object uses the pipe. That keeps the port path testable instead of deleting it, and makes the 10 chrome.port call sites a mechanical `newSession(chrome)`.
2. Events vs commands by argument shape - a function argument registers a listener for the domain event, anything else is sent as a command. No caller passes a function as a command parameter, and this avoids hand-maintaining an event-name registry, which would be a new drift surface of exactly the kind this repo keeps getting bitten by.
3. Close semantics: chrome.close() must end the pipe, kill the process group, and not leave the fd reader hanging, because the no-orphan-browser test and the reaper both depend on it.

Next: implement the transport, then make the recorded reproduction FAIL as the acceptance test - the separate process must find no listening port and must not be able to attach - with the port path still passing 4rv's exposure tests when explicitly selected.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
PROTOCOL MEASURED, not assumed - the whole transport rests on these three facts, so I checked them before writing any client code (script: /tmp/j3re-pipe-probe.mjs).

Result against this VM's Chrome (154.0.8037.92), launching with --headless=new --remote-debugging-pipe:
- fd 3 is the COMMAND channel (our writes) and fd 4 is the RESPONSE channel (Chrome's writes), with a NUL terminator after each JSON frame. I sent Target.getTargets and got a well-formed result back with real targetInfos (including the extension service worker Chrome always has attached), so framing, direction and terminator are all confirmed rather than copied from a blog post.
- A second command in the same session (Browser.getVersion) arrived in the same data chunk: responses are not one-per-read, so the client must buffer and split on NUL rather than assume a 1:1 read-to-message mapping. That is exactly the kind of assumption that makes a transport flaky under load.
- Chrome was killed in the probe and nothing was left running.

Also noted so the implementation does not have to rediscover it: the launch needs stdio fd 3 AND 4, i.e. ['ignore','ignore','pipe','pipe','pipe'] - the first two entries are 0/1, so the pipe fds only exist if three pipes are requested.

Next step in the implementation: no listening socket at all in pipe mode, so the acceptance test is the recorded reproduction FAILING (a separate process finds no DevTools endpoint and cannot attach), plus an explicit check that the browser pid holds no LISTEN row in /proc/net/tcp* at any point during a session. The port path stays behind an explicit opt-in so 4rv's exposure guard keeps protecting it.

NOTE ON THE BEAD RECORD: my bd dolt push is currently refused by GitHub push protection for a FABRICATED Stripe-shaped string I put in a bead comment on web-uplift-73y3 (see the comment there). So this note and any further bead writes from me are local until that is cleared; coord has the detail and the work itself is unaffected.

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
web-uplift-mwg-drift

title: Exclude .web-uplift/ from version control and generate it on install
description:
**Context:**
The `.web-uplift/` directory contains duplicated copies of the `evidence/`, `aggregate/`, and `runner/` source trees (used as the install surface). Because it is committed to git, developers frequently forget to run `install-surface.mjs` after editing the main source files. This leads to drift and the risk of shipping vulnerable code (as reported in web-uplift-6ha1).

**Decision:**
Add `.web-uplift/` to `.gitignore` and run `install-surface.mjs` automatically via an npm `postinstall` hook (or `prepack`). The directory will no longer be tracked in git, but will always be present and up-to-date in the developer's working environment and for end users.

**Consequences:**
We eliminate a major source of git merge conflicts (41 touches to `.web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs` in 30 days) and guarantee that the installed surface never drifts from the source tree. This resolves the duplication risk in web-uplift-6ha1.

**Alternatives considered:**
Using symlinks instead of copying. Rejected because `install-surface.mjs` deliberately copies files to create an isolated surface that can be vendored cleanly, and symlinks can break on some Windows environments or when packaging for npm.
close_reason: Closed

title: Adopt node:test to enable filterable fast test gates
description:
**Context:**
The test suite (`tests/regression.mjs`) is 8,177 lines and was touched 125 times in the last 30 days. Tests are executed via bare function calls in a single monolithic `try` block. There is no built-in test runner, meaning we cannot run specific tests or configure a fast gate (`CHECK_FAST_CMD`) for changed files. This forces the fleet to run the full 4-minute suite on every change (see web-uplift-n93i).

**Decision:**
Adopt the native `node:test` runner. Migrate all tests to use `test('name', async () => { ... })`. This provides test discovery (`node --test tests/`), built-in filtering (`--test-name-pattern`), and allows us to easily run a subset of tests.

**Consequences:**
We can implement a tiered test architecture. `CHECK_FAST_CMD` can be configured to run only the specific test files covering the changed source code. This eliminates the need to build a custom CLI argument parser for `regression.mjs`, and unblocks splitting the monolith.

**Alternatives considered:**
Adding a custom CLI argument parser (e.g. `--only`) to the current `regression.mjs` monolith as suggested in web-uplift-n93i. This was rejected because it requires maintaining custom test harness logic, whereas `node:test` is standard, zero-dependency, and built into Node v24.
close_reason: Closed

title: ADR: Split monolithic tests/regression.mjs and evidence/cli.mjs to reduce collision and enable targeted fast gates
description:
**Context:**
The project uses `tests/regression.mjs` (8177 lines) as the single entry point for all tests, touched 119 times in the last 30 days. `evidence/cli.mjs` (4205 lines) contains every evidence primitive, touched 38 times. This monolithic structure causes merge conflicts across agents and forces the entire test suite (~4-18 mins) to run on every change because there is no mapping from changed module to specific tests.

**Decision:**
Split `tests/regression.mjs` and `evidence/cli.mjs` into smaller, independently testable modules organized by primitive or subsystem. Move towards a test architecture that supports a `CHECK_FAST_CMD` to run only tests affected by a changed module.

**Consequences:**
Agent collisions on landings will drop significantly. By mapping tests to specific modules, we can implement a fast gate tier, saving the scarce fleet heavy slot.

**Alternatives considered:**
Running `node tests/regression.mjs --grep <pattern>` could run tests faster but does not solve the git merge collision problem in the file itself.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-mwg-drift
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW + merge-queue on fleet/flow-record-classifier @ c69a281 (2 commits, merge-base origin/master = e3520f8; 5 files). Focused tests run and green; `fleet-check --fast` (npm run test:fast) was started on this tip and its verdict is recorded below when it lands.

WHAT THE BEAD FOUND, restated because it is what makes this worth a branch: the recorder's sensitive-field classifier existed TWICE - at module scope, which the unit tests read, and again as hand-maintained source inside the page script makeCaptureJs() injects, which is the copy that actually RUNS at record time. Only the second copy decides what gets redacted, so adding a word or a token to the first and forgetting the second kept the suite green while the live recorder wrote that field's value into flow.json verbatim - the file this tool tells operators to treat as a secret. There was no assertion that the two agreed. The bead notes the set was edited six times across two lanes in the week that filed it, each time by hand in both places.

FIX: the page receives the classifiers as SOURCE, not as a copy, so there is exactly one implementation of each:
- evidence/credential-terms.mjs exports SENSITIVE_CLASSIFIER_SOURCE, built from its own member/isCredentialWord/isPiiWord/isSensitiveWord/splitName/isSensitiveName functions (web-uplift-fejl).
- runner/flow-record.mjs builds PAGE_SIDE_CLASSIFIER_SOURCE the same way from hasSensitiveWord/isSensitiveAutocomplete/isSensitiveField, and makeCaptureJs() injects both plus the word data (NAME_WORD_DATA, already shared since so2).
- The page's hand-written isSensitiveName - a THIRD copy, of credential-terms' function - its word-set plumbing (member/credentialWord/piiWord/sensitiveWord/splitName) and its two duplicated classifiers are deleted. The module's isSensitiveField takes the capture flags as options, so the page wraps it once passing its closure's CAPTURE_HIDDEN/CAPTURE_SENSITIVE; the change listener still skips hidden inputs before calling it, unchanged.

GUARD (tests/flow.mjs): asserts the whole SENSITIVE_CLASSIFIER_SOURCE and each of this module's three functions appear VERBATIM in the injected script, that all NINE functions are defined exactly once (the six shared names are derived from that source by regex, so adding a function there extends the guard automatically), and then compares the page's verdict against the module's over a 15-field matrix observed through what the recorder actually persists - redacted:true with an empty value, or the typed value.

REVIEW: independent family (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol; implementer deepseek-flash). Pass 1: HOLDS, merge verdict OK with notes - 1 P2 + 1 P3. P2: the identity guard covered only this module's three functions, so a hand-written page copy of isSensitiveName or isSensitiveWord could drift on a word the matrix does not happen to cover with nothing failing. Fixed by covering the whole shared source and all nine names. P3: the matrix asserted that a redacted step carries no value but said nothing about a retained one; it now asserts the persisted value on every case. Pass 2 on c69a281: VERDICT HOLDS, merge verdict OK, no issues found.

MUTATION CHECKS, and the second one is the point of the whole bead:
1. A hand-written page copy that returns false for everything fails the EXISTING behavioural assertions immediately.
2. A hand-written copy that is BEHAVIOURALLY IDENTICAL but textually drifted (renamed internals in isSensitiveAutocomplete) passes every behavioural assertion and fails exactly the source-identity guard - that is the drift that used to be invisible.
3. The reviewer's scenario: hand-copying isSensitiveName - one of the six shared functions - with renamed internals passed the ENTIRE suite before the P2 fix and fails only the new extended assertion after it.
Each time the mutated files were restored byte-identically, verified by md5 against the committed content (never `git checkout --` on an uncommitted fix).

STATED LIMITATION, not left implicit: the generation depends on the module's functions keeping the identifiers they reference (the injected names must exist in page scope, and renaming them, e.g. by a bundler, would break the injection). This repo has no bundler or minifier - `npm test` runs `node tests/regression.mjs` and `npm run test:fast` runs `scripts/test-fast.mjs` directly, and the installer copies the modules rather than transforming them - so the property holds today, and the guard fails loudly if a page copy drifts.

Verified: tests/flow.mjs tests OK (including the new section), tests/flow-shadow-browser.mjs tests OK (real browser: the injected script still records, in its isolated world, with the generated classifier), tests/credential-redaction.mjs tests OK, tests/secrets-coverage.mjs tests OK, tests/cdp-copy-sync.mjs all 23 vendored copies identical.

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] Default-on update check makes unsolicited network egress and trusts an unauthenticated registry response
description:
Severity: LOW (vuln-triage; threat-model rated info; the summary's 'routed critical' is a routing label, not severity). Rule tm-update-check-default-egress.
Location: bin/web-uplift.mjs:494 (verified present at origin/master dba6c2c).
Every ordinary CLI subcommand (except --help/--version and when CI/NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER/WEB_UPLIFT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK is set) makes an HTTPS request to registry.npmjs.org, persists the result under XDG_CACHE_HOME/web-uplift/update-check.json, and prints a warning. The response is only used to compare a version string and is never executed, and the fetch is bounded by an AbortController, so impact is limited. The gap: the check is on by default (unsolicited egress) and acts on an unauthenticated registry response.
Evidence: const response = await fetch(`https://registry.npmjs.org/${encodeURIComponent(packageName)}/latest`, { signal: controller.signal, ... });
Remediation (factory proposal): make the check opt-in (or first-run consent explicit), document the egress, and avoid acting on an unverified version string beyond printing it.

title: [test-infra] Regression suite accumulates a ~42M npx cache tree per run (packed tarball uses a fresh /tmp path)
description: Found during the 2026-10-08 disk reclaim (fleet-6r0s): ~/.npm/_npx had grown to 12G across ~287 cached trees, and ~273 of them are created by OUR OWN regression suite. Mechanism: the install/pack test packs web-uplift to a FRESH path each run (/tmp/web-uplift-regression-<rand>/pack/web-uplift-0.5.0.tgz) and then installs it via npx/npm exec; because the file: spec path changes every run, npx cannot reuse its cache and lays down a NEW ~42M tree (web-uplift's dependency closure incl. web-features/zod/axe-core) every time. One tree per test run, forever. Evidence: sampled tree's root package.json has dependencies {web-uplift: file:../../../../../tmp/web-uplift-regression-s5kQIS/pack/web-uplift-0.5.0.tgz} and _npx.packages pointing at that temp path; 271 trees carry web-features@3.40.0. The modern-web-guidance npx trees are only 8 and correctly pinned - not the problem. FIX (pick one): (a) pack to a STABLE path (e.g. a fixed /tmp or repo-local cache dir) cleared at the start of the test, so npx reuses one tree; or (b) after the install-test, remove the specific npx tree it created; or (c) run the packed-CLI check via a direct node invocation instead of npx. ACCEPTANCE: repeated full-suite runs no longer grow ~/.npm/_npx by ~42M per run; a test/assert can observe this. NOT urgent (reclaim buys headroom); this is the durable half.

title: Headless audit runner vs reaper: a detached audit job is forfeited by the orphaned-browser rule, and an in-flight primitive that never lands stderr is unattributable
description:
Filed per coord 13:52Z from web-uplift-ies run-2 evidence. TWO halves:
(1) RUNNER-VS-REAPER TENSION (fleet infra side already reported to hub by coord — do NOT fix reaper.mjs here): a headless batch audit launched through fleet-gate's setsid path is classified orphan:true by the reaper; the lane-alive hatch (reaper.mjs ~line 85) is dead on this VM because lanePane (~line 48) is built only from state files with host !== 'sdk' and every lane here is an sdk-host lane sharing one host_pid, so lanesAlive is always empty; line 86 then kills any orphan tree containing a browser at >=10 min. CONSEQUENCE: one chrome held past ~5-10 min — during an agent model pause, an npx cold start, or one hung primitive — FORFEITS THE WHOLE AUDIT JOB. Evidence: run 2 (reports/paul_kinlan_me/2026-10-06T12-47-41-014Z) killed at 11 min (23 procs, 187% CPU, 2173MB, kill msg 'orphaned browser (11 min, nobody will close it)'), after producing 101 healthy artifacts in 10.5 min, lighthouse just starting. Worked-around for run 4 via pi-subagents async runner (owner alive -> orphan:false -> 45-min browser window); note that path needs env -u PI_PACKAGE_DIR (async runner leaks it and breaks nested standalone-pi startup — separate hub infra item).
(2) UNATTRUTABLE-PRIMITIVE OBSERVABILITY GAP (ours to fix): the browser open at the kill was an evidence-CLI chrome (profile /tmp/web-uplift-cdp-skYnpy, launchChrome cmdline signature) but NO stderr file in the run tree names skYnpy — every COMPLETED primitive logs its own profile in its stderr, but a primitive still in flight (or one whose stderr redirect never landed) leaves no artifact tying a live browser to an invocation, so the kill could not be attributed to a primitive. PROPOSAL: have the evidence CLI append a launch marker (timestamp, primitive, target, profile dir, pid) to a run-level launches.jsonl AT LAUNCH time, not at teardown, so any surviving/orphaned chrome is attributable post-mortem. Acceptance: a deliberately hung stub primitive killed externally is attributable from launches.jsonl alone.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: web-uplift-net-bodies
comments.text: MECHANISM CORRECTION (coord 14:00Z, code-verified): reaper.mjs j.ageMin = ROOT process age (line 70), not browser age. So: line 86 (orphan && browser && ageMin>=10) kills any orphaned tree CONTAINING a browser at root age >=10 min — the browser itself can be seconds old; and line 87 (browser && ageMin>=BROWSER_MIN 45) kills even OWNED job trees at root age >=45 min if any chrome is in the tree at sample time. IMPLICATIONS for this bead: (a) the runner-vs-reaper tension is sharper than filed: an owned headless-audit job has an effective ~43-min ceiling (45 minus sample interval) whenever any primitive chrome is alive — pi-subagents ownership fixes the 10-min orphan rule but NOT the 45-min browser rule; timeoutMs above ~40 min is not protection, the reaper decides. Splitting long audits into stages under ~40 min each is the only safe shape. (b) run-2 forensics: the 'orphaned browser (11 min)' message reported ROOT age; skYnpy need not have been open 11 min (likely a fresh primitive launch — evidence was landing until 12:58). The observability gap (no artifact tied the live browser to an invocation) and the launches.jsonl proposal are unchanged and if anything better motivated: even the reaper's own message cannot tell you WHICH browser or how old it was.

comments.author: web-uplift-mw-invoker
comments.text:
SECOND-SOURCE of half 2 (the observability gap), read-only on master 5c0ab59 (mw-invoker, kimi/k3, 14:25Z): CONFIRMED, with one nuance that makes the fix smaller.

(a) THE LAUNCH-TIME FACT EXISTS BUT ONLY AS A STREAM. evidence/cdp.mjs:403-404: launchChromeOnce creates the profile (mkdtempSync(tmpdir()+'/web-uplift-cdp-')) and immediately logs '[browser] launching ... profile <dir>'. But every caller's log is console.error: evidence/cli.mjs:3861, runner/run-batch.mjs:454, runner/flow.mjs (both). A stderr line persists only if whatever spawned the process saves it; in a headless claude run that is the agent's Bash capture, not the run tree. So the gap is not that the fact is never produced - it is that it never reaches a FILE at launch time.

(b) NOTHING WRITES A LAUNCH RECORD TO DISK. grep for launches/launch-marker across master: clean (no launches.jsonl anywhere). Every writeFileSync in evidence/cli.mjs (lines 230, 267, 294, 398, 680, 868, 878, 1133, 1140, ...) is a RESULT artifact written at or after primitive completion; gather() (cli.mjs:3857) launches chrome, runs the primitive, then writes opts.out. A primitive killed mid-flight leaves no run-tree artifact naming its profile or pid. CONFIRMED: an in-flight primitive is unattributable from the run tree alone.

(c) FIX-SHAPE NOTES for whoever implements (the acceptance is 'hung stub primitive killed externally is attributable from launches.jsonl alone'):
- The common choke point for ALL browser launches is launchChromeOnce in cdp.mjs (cli.mjs primitives, run-batch.mjs:455 flow replay, flow.mjs record/replay all go through it) - but cdp.mjs knows neither the primitive name nor the out dir, so the marker write belongs one level up: cli.mjs gather() right after launchChrome succeeds (it has primitive, url, opts.out, and the browser handle carries userDataDir + proc.pid). The runner's own flow-replay chrome can record the same way with primitive:'flow-replay'.
- The marker must carry pid AS WELL AS profile dir: the reaper kills by process tree, so post-mortem attribution needs pid -> primitive, not just profile -> primitive.
- Concurrency: batch runs and the flow replay can hold several chromes at once appending to one launches.jsonl - single-write O_APPEND lines are atomic enough at this size, but the file location must be decided: <out dir of the run>/launches.jsonl (agent primitives share the run's evidence dir) rather than per-primitive --out files.
- The test the acceptance describes is cheap: a stub HTTP server that never responds, launch the CLI against it, kill -9 the process tree externally, assert launches.jsonl has the line with primitive+pid+profile.

title: Docs drift after fourteen lands: the new fetch-deadline flag is undocumented, and the changed behaviour must match what the docs claim
description: GROUNDED, NOT SPECULATIVE: a grep on current master shows --fetch-deadline occurs ONLY in evidence/cli.mjs and its vendored mirror — it appears in NO README, NO skill file and NO docs page. It is a real user-facing surface: a flag with an environment variable and a per-call default that changes how long the raw-HTML fetch is allowed to take, added in revision five of the widening bead. An operator cannot discover it, and a documented zero-config default of thirty seconds now disagrees with nothing because nothing states it. WHAT TO DO: (1) document the fetch deadline where the other CLI options live, including its environment variable, its default, and the ONE behaviour an operator needs to know — that when the raw fetch fails or times out the comparison is reported as UNKNOWN rather than as a finding about the page, so a short budget produces absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence. (2) Then check the broader drift the same grep implies: the lands since the release changed real behaviour — the discovery comparison now distinguishes a timeout from genuinely empty content, a completed empty 200 is deliberately treated as observed evidence, the usability gate requires a 2xx response, credential redaction descends into containers and splices rather than re-serialises, batch runs gained write-scope accounting, and a planted latest pointer is contained — and any doc or skill copy that describes the OLD behaviour is now wrong. Check EACH doc surface that describes these behaviours rather than assuming the three skill copies are in sync; SKILL copies have drifted before on this project. (3) Report drift as a bead comment with file and line, and fix only what is genuinely wrong — do not restructure docs. Do NOT touch the changelog: the owed entries are drafted on web-uplift-kk5 and the changelog stays heading-free until Paul cuts the next version. Evidence standard: for each claim of drift, quote the doc line and the code that contradicts it; a doc that merely omits something is a lesser finding than a doc that states the opposite, and the two should be labelled differently.

All twelve lands are accounted for: NINE drafted entries below, THREE explicitly classified not-user-visible at the end.

=== Security ===

- **A published scorecard can no longer be steered into embedding a file from outside the audited run.** The scorecard renders before/after screenshots from the comparison record, which is untrusted input - it is written by an agent whose context includes page content - and the record's run identifiers decided the BASE directory the screenshot paths were contained against, so a crafted identifier could point that base anywhere on disk and inline any image file into the published report. Comparison run identifiers now go through the same containment rule as every other artifact path (one path segment, resolving to a direct child of the run directory); a refused side is left out of the comparison instead of crashing the render. (9li)

- **A planted `latest` pointer can no longer choose which directory the scorecard reads.** `resolveLatest()` joined the `latest` symlink target and the `latest.txt` content - files inside the tree the audited agent can write - straight onto the host's run root, so a planted pointer could name any directory on disk as the run to publish from. The target is now contained inside the host run root; a pointer that fails containment is treated as no pointer at all and the scorecard falls back to the newest run inside the tree. Containment bounds WHERE a pointer can point; it cannot authenticate WHICH run is current - a planted name of a legitimate earlier run inside the tree is still read as current - and that residual is now stated once in the code, bounded by operator isolation. (9t8)

- **Batch audits get fix mode's write-scope accounting.** Every agent spawn in a batch (the baseline audit included) is now snapshotted around, the default output tree is walked too, and a run whose changes land outside `--target`/`--out` is refused with a per-run diff written for review; concurrent runs no longer refuse each other's clean work. As in fix mode this is DETECTION, not confinement, with the same documented gaps (`runner/write-scope.mjs`). Batch completion counting was corrected with it: a URL counts as complete only after its publication actually succeeded, a publication failure is recorded as its own named reason, and a duplicate URL later in a resumed batch is attempted instead of silently skipped. (wy6)

- **Credential redaction in recorded evidence now reaches the shapes it missed.** Audit artifacts (HAR and evidence JSON) previously kept credentials in camel-case names (`accessToken`, `apiKey`, `clientSecret`), in URL-valued headers such as `Referer` (which carries the audited page URL verbatim), in the initiator fields, and inside nested JSON containers (`{"wrapper":{"token":...}}` was returned unchanged). All are redacted now: names match on separator AND camelCase boundaries against a curated set, deliberately fail-closed on ambiguity (`code`, `key` are redacted); every header value passes the URL redaction; the JSON walker descends into containers. Structured inputs are redacted by DECODED KEY, and the parse is used only to LOCATE spans - the redaction splices the original text and never re-serialises, so non-credential bytes are recorded exactly as received (a `__proto__` key no longer vanishes; integers beyond the safe range are no longer rounded). The artifact's note no longer claims the unstructured-text scan is complete; it is a capped best-effort pass and now says so. (dsj)

=== Fixed ===

- **The published report no longer shifts under the reader as screenshots decode.** The scorecard inlines before/after screenshots as data URIs, so the browser has no network hop to learn their size from and the image elements carried no dimensions: every image's height was 0 until its bitmap decoded and the content below moved then, worst on first render over a slow connection. The report now reads each image's intrinsic size from its own bytes (PNG IHDR, GIF logical screen descriptor, JPEG start-of-frame, WebP VP8X/VP8/VP8L) and emits `width`/`height`, with the stylesheet letting that ratio drive the box so the reservation survives responsive layout. Measured in a real browser with both bitmaps genuinely in flight: the sized image reserves 250.75px pending and moves the content below 0.0px; the unsized twin reserves 2px and moves it 97.6px on decode. A file whose size cannot be read keeps the old behaviour rather than getting a guessed box. (xq5)

- **The report image reader refuses sizes declared beyond the file's own container.** A WebP whose declared RIFF size ended before the chunk header previously had the chunk code and size read from outside the range the format declares; the container must now cover the chunk header before either field is read. This completes the rule the reserved-box entry states: every field the size reader uses must lie inside both the buffer and the range the format declares for it, so a malformed file gets no `width`/`height` attributes rather than an invented box. (93s)

- **The resilience primitive no longer misses a service worker that registers late - and an empty list no longer reads as absence.** ServiceWorker registrations arrive asynchronously, and the primitive extended its wait only when a page-origin registration had ALREADY been observed, so a registration landing after the settle window produced an artifact whose empty list claimed, by silence, that the site had no service worker. The wait now extends for a registration that arrives after the settle window, within a budget; a page that registers after the budget still yields an empty list, but the artifact now records the observation window (`serviceWorker.observation`: `budgetMs`, `waitedMs`, `registrationObserved`, `budgetExhausted`) and carries a note in that case, so a reader who never sees the documentation still cannot mistake the empty list for absence. (5jd)

- **The evidence CLI fails loudly on a host that stops answering, instead of hanging indefinitely - and discoverability never derives page claims from a raw document it failed to retrieve.** Every CDP wait on the attach, navigation, console-collector and tracing paths is now bounded (default 30s; `--cdp-deadline <ms>` or `WEB_UPLIFT_CDP_DEADLINE_MS`), and every raw-fetch exchange is bounded including its body stream (default 30s; `--fetch-deadline <ms>` or `WEB_UPLIFT_FETCH_DEADLINE_MS`). An expiry rejects with an error naming what was awaited, the bound, the target URL, and how to raise the bound. On the discoverability side, the raw-document comparison now passes a single gate with enumerated routes - usable means the document the URL names was retrieved, with no fetch error, a recorded status and a 2xx final response - and when the raw document was not retrieved (timeout, network error, non-2xx, body-read failure) the WHOLE derived block is null: `coveragePct`, `isJsShell`, the presence comparisons and the raw stats are absent rather than computed from an empty string, so a network condition can no longer masquerade as a JS-shell finding and a non-2xx body is never read as the document. Fields describing the RENDERED page are still reported. (17o)

=== Changed ===

- **The vendored install surface is declared once and checked against a real install.** `install-surface.mjs` now declares every vendored directory, vendored file and tracked copy (and records what is deliberately NOT part of the surface, with reasons); the installer builds its copy plan from that declaration and the byte-identity guard builds its comparison pairs from it, so the two hand-maintained lists that could silently diverge are one derived list. A test drives a REAL install into a temp target and compares what actually appears under `.web-uplift/` against the declaration in both directions: an undeclared vendored file fails, and a declaration the install no longer produces fails. The declaration module itself ships in the package `files` allowlist, which the packed-tarball test enforces - an omission there would install a CLI that dies with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. (7mr)

=== Classified NOT user-visible (no entry drafted, with the reason) ===

- x4d (bd12d22): TESTS ONLY - one file, tests/regression.mjs +129. Measures the reserved image box in a real browser with and without the size attributes, proving the measurement apparatus can see the difference (the 0.0px/97.6px numbers the xq5 entry cites come from it). No product code changed.
- uz9 (9f996af): TESTS ONLY - one file, tests/regression.mjs +95/-14. Gives the pointer-containment positive controls teeth (they now name the OLDER of two runs, which the newest-run fallback cannot satisfy) and asserts every relative import in the installed vendored tree resolves. No product code changed.
- zje (f444d9a): DOCS AND WORDING ONLY - narrows the runner's completion-guarantee comments to the accurate precedence rule and states the residual once; rewords one NOT QUARANTINED stderr diagnostic to point at it (message text, no behaviour); fixes a stale path in the published 0.5.0 changelog text (`fixer/write-scope.mjs` -> `runner/write-scope.mjs`) and tightens one 0.5.0 sentence. Verified from the diff: no code-behaviour lines change. No product behaviour changed.

=== Notes for the release owner ===
- Sections follow the existing 0.5.0 shape (Security / Added / Fixed / Changed); no land in this set adds a new command or flag surface that is not already named inside its Fixed entry, so there is no Added section.
- The 93s entry is deliberately separable: its rule sentence also appears (broader) in the xq5 entry, so the owner may fold 93s into xq5 or keep both, as house style prefers.
- 17o is one land carrying two user-visible clusters (bounded waits; discoverability gating). The entry covers both because both landed in 0e68e99; split into two entries if the cut prefers one topic per entry.

title: A starved host can make the evidence CLI wait indefinitely: no deadline on the CDP attach/navigation path
description:
Filed from the investigation of web-uplift-dl6, which DISPROVED its own premise (the reported subprocess hang does not reproduce on a quiet host; every observation was a contention artifact at load 16.8 with three concurrent suites). This is the real, smaller gap that investigation surfaced.

WHAT: the evidence CLI puts a bounded deadline on exactly ONE interaction primitive, but the CDP attach and navigation path has NO deadline. On a heavily contended host — which this VM was for much of tonight — that means the CLI can wait indefinitely rather than failing, so a user or a CI job sees an apparent hang with no diagnosis. That is why a starvation episode was indistinguishable from a real hang, and why it took a dedicated investigation with a controlled table to tell them apart.

ALSO IN THE SAME AREA, from the same investigation: --out takes a FILE path, not a directory (the primitive writes one artifact to that path). Passing an existing directory fails with a bare EISDIR and an unhelpful message; one run misread the resulting output as a hang. Small ergonomics fix: detect the directory case and say plainly that --out expects a file path, rather than surfacing a raw filesystem errno.

ACCEPTANCE: a bounded deadline on the attach/navigation path that fails LOUDLY with a diagnosable message and a non-zero exit instead of waiting forever; the bound configurable (flag and/or environment) with a sane default and documented; a test that a slow or starved attach fails rather than hanging — via a seam that can simulate slowness if a real starved host cannot be arranged deterministically; and the clearer --out-is-a-file error with its own assertion. Do NOT change the successful path's behaviour or timing on a healthy host.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: an indefinite wait is the worst failure mode for an automation surface — it burns a CI slot, it is indistinguishable from a real defect (as this bead line just demonstrated), and it hides the actual cause. A bounded wait converts tonight's confusing episode into a one-line error.

SEQUENCING: edits evidence/cli.mjs, so it is bd-blocked on web-uplift-dsj (the higher-priority credential-redaction bead) to keep one writer on that file.
