title: A published scorecard can be steered into embedding a file from outside the audited run
description:
WHAT: the scorecard reads the comparison record an earlier run wrote and uses the run identifiers in that record to locate the before/after screenshots. Those identifiers are not validated, and the containment check that guards screenshot paths is resolved against a base directory the record itself supplies, so the record's own contents can move the check out of the way.

IMPACT: a scorecard generated on a machine can embed bytes from a file elsewhere on that machine into the published scorecard. Because scorecards are produced to be published or archived, that is a local file disclosure.

WHAT A BAD ACTOR COULD ACHIEVE: a page that steers the agent while it writes a run record, or a run directory obtained from elsewhere, can make a later scorecard publish the contents of a chosen local file. Reachability is conditional on influencing that record, and only files whose names end in an image extension can be read out this way.

FIX DIRECTION: treat the run identifiers in the comparison record as untrusted path-like fields: require each to be a single run-directory name (reject empty, NUL, absolute, and anything containing a separator or a '..' segment), resolve the run directory through the run-history helper instead of joining the raw value, apply the same guard to the vendored copy, and add a regression test that a traversal run identifier drops the image instead of inlining it.

title: A security-header audit can report headers as missing on sites that send them
description: IMPACT: when the tool inspects a site's security response headers, a response whose header names arrive capitalised - which is what a plain HTTP/1.1 response does - has every header read as absent. A page that really does send a content-security-policy, strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, referrer-policy or permissions-policy is reported as sending none of them. WHAT A BAD ACTOR COULD ACHIEVE: an operator is told their site lacks protections it actually has, so the security reading recorded in the evidence is wrong in the safe direction and a real gap is indistinguishable from this false one - the header evidence cannot be trusted either way, and remediation effort goes to the wrong place. FIX DIRECTION: match response header names case-insensitively, and cover the primitive with a test (it has none).
close_reason: MERGED 90c41b289ddc3dccd0c54007aeb7130be936af98 (tree 6aeb37b6); gate land-0w6 exit 0/268s; not a trivial merge so the author gate legitimately stood per the load-lever rule. Independent review PASS: three-state header reporting (a present-but-empty header reads neither absent nor satisfied), both remaining case-sensitive lookups fixed through the existing helper with a complete sweep, the one deliberate leave is the platform fetch accessor which is case-insensitive by spec, and the tests prove their own casing and fail on the old revision. Impact: a site could be reported as not sending a protective header purely because of header-name casing, or because the header was present but empty.

Fix: verify the run directory is a real directory before destructive cleanup and never delete through an agent-mutable parent — the rename approach removes most of this risk.
P2, POSITIVE CONTROL STILL SYNTHETIC: ACCEPTED AS A DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL by coord, because a real-agent audit smoke run needs an external agent CLI and token spend and belongs to a deliberate acceptance step rather than the unit gate. comments.text:
REVIEW RESULT rev3: FAIL on a26ff3c (same independent cross-family reviewer) — TWO P1s and a P2, all in the guard's own bookkeeping; mechanism in the lane brief. Regressions required for both planted paths.
P1b, THE REAL-DIRECTORY CHECK COMES TOO LATE: the scope record is written THROUGH the run directory before the quarantine validates it, so an agent can replace that directory with a symlink to another run and have that run scope record overwritten, or point it outside the output tree so the post-snapshot write escapes accounting. P2: the deleted-directory fix has no regression; add a batch-level case where the agent deletes its run directory and a LATER URL still completes.
RESIDUAL recorded by the reviewer as PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: the preparation of the next URL sits outside the per-URL catch and can still abort the batch; mw-invoker will fold it in if cheap or document it with its reason. - THE COMMENT AT :232 WAS STALE and asserted the old fallback as the reason for quarantining, next to code that removed the dependency on it - exactly the claim-versus-reality gap we have been closing all night. It now describes the quarantine as defence in depth and evidence, and names resolveLatest's remaining fallback and who still uses it.
So the honest statement of the guarantee is: 'the batch's completion decision comes from our own pointer and cannot be influenced by planted files; the quarantine is advisory evidence; other consumers still resolve the newest run with a report for reporting purposes.'

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text:
REV4 REVIEW RESULT: FAIL on 8b22cc4 (same independent cross-family reviewer) — and the verdict triggers the cap: the fix is SIMPLIFICATION, not a fifth patch. Mechanism in the lane brief. WHAT THE REVIEWER CONFIRMED RIGHT: the author call-graph answer holds — the batch does not import or call the latest-resolution fallback, and leaving that fallback in place for reporting consumers is acceptable because neither internal use controls refusal or completion; the comment-only tip changed nothing behavioural; the swap test meaningfully protects the innocent scope record; and the runner and its mirror have no behavioural difference.
WHAT MAKES THE CLAIM FALSE: PROVENANCE. The batch reads its pointer from agent-writable disk, so it cannot tell whether the tool or the agent wrote it; planting a pointer that names a refused run whose valid report could not be quarantined makes a later resume skip that URL. So the recorded guarantee that planted files cannot influence completion is false as written, and two comments repeat it (the new division-of-consumers comment and an older one still calling the rename load-bearing).
REMAINING P1s: a scope-record failure can fall through to report publication; and the real-directory check validates the leaf but not symlinked ANCESTORS, so a check-to-write race remains. P2s: readFileSync is MISSING from the import, which silently disables the pointer-file resume path altogether — a genuine defect and one that means the resume behaviour believed to exist may never have run; an impossible quarantine is logged on stderr but not recorded as a separately named failure reason; and the destroyed-directory test's destructive-URL failure assertion can pass on the ordinary URL text.
REV5 ROUTED AS SIMPLIFICATION PLUS CONCRETE FIXES, applying the cap coord recorded earlier: rewrite the claim to what the mechanism actually delivers (on-disk completion state is agent-writable and therefore ADVISORY; in-memory state decides within a batch; across a resume a tampered pointer is a documented residual whose real boundary is operator-supplied isolation, the same conclusion as fix mode); fix the concrete defects above, including a resume test that would fail today because of the missing import; and keep the tripwire, quarantine and loud reporting as DETECTION once nothing depends on them for correctness. That is the same pivot shape as the confinement work one level down: do not let a decision depend on state the adversary controls, and do not claim a guarantee the mechanism cannot deliver. Status IN_REVIEW; merge-queue label stays off.

title: [factory-audit/vuln] Fix mode gives a prompt-injectable agent unconfined write access to the whole working tree
description:
## What
Fix mode spawns a shell/file-capable agent whose prompt context contains untrusted page-derived content, with no enforcement that model-authored edits stay inside `--source`/`--target`. The child process is not even rooted at the source directory, so a successful prompt injection can write anywhere the installing user can.

## Evidence (verified in code at origin/master 2649765)
- `fixer/fix.mjs:345-347`:
  ```js
  function runAgent(prompt, iteration) {
    const cliArgs = agent.args(prompt, { maxTurns: 120 });
    ...
    const child = spawn(agent.bin, cliArgs, { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
  ```
  There is no `cwd` in the spawn options, so the agent inherits the caller's working directory — not `--source`, not `--target`. There is no snapshot of the target tree, no diff gate, and no post-iteration check that edits stayed inside the declared directory.
- The same file's own comments establish the trust model for its inputs: "A report file is untrusted input: fix mode reads reports written by other runs, other tools, and older versions." The audit URL and page-derived evidence also flow into `agent.prompt(auditUrl, outDir, `--source ${target}`)` (`baselineAudit`, line 338).
- The agent's write approval comes from `runner/agents.mjs` (`Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(npx:*)`, `Write`, `Edit`), which is the separate root cause tracked by `web-uplift-tia`.

## Why it is real
Distinct from the allowlist root cause: even with a tightened allowlist, `Write`/`Edit` remain, and nothing confines them to the declared source tree. The threat model's I4 ("Untrusted page content must not steer the agent beyond the skill's intended actions") is a path-level requirement, not only a tool-list requirement, and section 5 HS6 asks that each relaxation be "scoped, restored, and documented".
The vuln-triage station kept this separate from the prompt-injection rule for exactly this reason: it "requires its own confinement patch (sandbox or per-iteration diff review) rather than prompt sanitisation".

## Calibrated severity
Station severity: medium. Conditional (needs a successful injection and a fix-mode run), but the impact is unbounded writes as the invoking user. P3.

## Station citation
Factory audit run 2026-10-06T00:22Z, target `/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-factory` @4cccc60, vuln-triage finding `vuln-triage/fix-mode-unconfined-writes` (report `/home/exedev/agents/runs/vuln-triage-web-uplift-factory-20261006-003424/report.json`). Hand-calibrated because the findings store records every finding as CRITICAL (fleet-eqv).

## Bounded next step
Root the fix agent at the declared source tree (`cwd: resolve(target)` in the spawn), snapshot the tree before each iteration, refuse to keep any iteration whose diff escapes the declared directory, and emit a per-iteration diff so a human can review what the model changed.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text: DESIGN DECISION (coord, 2026-10-06T01:36Z) — recorded as policy, no mechanism. The P1 boundary question is settled: fix mode will FAIL CLOSED by default, refusing to drive the write-capable agent unless it can establish an isolation boundary (a supported sandbox runtime or a detected container), with a diagnosable refusal that names what it needs. An operator may still run without a boundary, but only as an EXPLICIT, AUDITABLE risk acceptance — an explicit flag plus a recorded marker in the run result/artifact, plus a loud warning — never silent and never the default; that mirrors the project own section 7 precedent for accepted risk and is what turns an implicit violation into a recorded one. The interactive in-session workflow is unaffected and remains the documented default. Rationale: the invariant mandates the boundary and the headless path is already the container-gated automation path, but removing headless fix entirely on sandbox-less hosts is a user-facing capability removal this lane will not make unilaterally; a section 7-style recorded acceptance keeps it available and auditable. The oracle is returning the concrete design (runtime detection order, where the override is recorded, refusal message content, and what the positive end-to-end test asserts on a host with no sandbox runtime — skip with recorded reason or a mockable provider seam); that goes straight to mw-invoker as the P1 brief. Product-direction change noted for the hub in the next batch, since it alters an automation capability.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text: DECISION REVISED — REAL BOUNDARY NOW THE PRIMARY (coord, 2026-10-06T01:37Z), recorded as policy, no mechanism. mw-invoker measured the host read-only and it changes the answer: bwrap IS installed here and unprivileged user namespaces WORK, so the "smallest real boundary" the reviewer demanded is actually available rather than hypothetical. Therefore fix mode will wrap the agent child in a real OS sandbox by default (bwrap with a fallback ordering, refusing if no primitive is available), with only the declared source/output roots mounted read-write and the tool/dependency trees and other host paths read-only or unmounted; the explicit recorded override remains only as a section-7-style exception for hosts without any primitive, never the design and never silent. The existing snapshot/diff/refuse tripwire stays as defence in depth. Second measured input from mw-invoker: agent-side write control is uneven across agent entries (cheap to remove only for two of them; the rest pass blanket flags), which is precisely why an OS-level boundary is the uniform answer. Open design points the oracle is resolving: the network question (fix mode legitimately needs the network, so it must be reconciled with the SSRF and supply-chain posture just hardened), the exact bind set, the fallback ordering and refusal message, where the unsandboxed marker is recorded, and the test strategy for hosts WITH and WITHOUT the primitive, including a positive end-to-end proof that a legitimate fix still succeeds inside the sandbox. Unconditional fixes are already pushed on this branch (publication-pointer bug, withdrawn false claim, uncovered-list corrections, refusal asserts nothing published including latest, new success case). Status stays IN_REVIEW; merge-queue label should come off.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text: P1 DESIGN DECIDED AND HANDED TO mw-invoker (coord, 2026-10-06T01:40Z) — policy-level record, mechanism in the lane brief only per the public-repo rule. The oracle returned a concrete design: headless fix mode will launch the agent (baseline and every iteration) inside a real OS sandbox built as an empty mount namespace, with ONLY the declared source and output roots writable, the tool and dependency trees, the agent runtime closure and the system minimum read-only, protected subtrees kept read-only even when nested beneath the target, private non-host-backed scratch, and other checkouts, the real home, credentials and the container socket not mounted at all. The provider probe must validate the complete profile before use; a fallback qualifies only if it builds and tests the same layout, and otherwise the run refuses BEFORE any agent spawn with a message naming what was found and required. The explicit override survives only as a loud, recorded, section-7-style accepted risk that writes a marker before spawn and is propagated into the result; a refused run records refused, a sandboxed run records the provider and validated profile. The existing snapshot/diff/refuse tripwire stays as defence in depth, and the publication pointer must only move after a successful completed result (already fixed on this branch). HONEST RESIDUAL, stated in both code and docs: the filesystem sandbox does NOT address network egress, SSRF/metadata access or exfiltration of the provider credential handed to the child, so the hardened evidence-fetch checks and pinned guidance invocation stay, and restricted-network deployments need separate host/VM egress controls; the intended source remains writable by the untrusted agent, and the override permits unconfined writes by deliberate operator acceptance. ACCEPTANCE BAR: on a host with the primitive, a browser-driven positive end-to-end fix must succeed INSIDE the sandbox, and a negative agent attempting writes to the protected tool/dependency tree, an unrelated host path and the previous latest pointer must fail at the WRITE SYSCALL, not merely be noticed by the tripwire; on a host without the primitive, mockable provider-seam tests must prove default refusal before the baseline spawn, latest unchanged and a refusal marker, and must NOT be skippable. Status stays IN_REVIEW with the merge-queue label removed until the revision passes.

comments.text: REVISION 2 RE-REVIEW: FAIL (same independent adversarial reviewer, tip 1c85d20) — four P1s and two P2s, all inside the new sandbox itself; mechanism in the lane brief only per the disclosure rule. ACCEPTED: the syscall-level substitution satisfies the write-failure bar the reviewer originally set, the publication fix works for detected refusals, and the override marker is written by rename before the spawn on the ordinary path. Impact-level list of what still leaks: (1) host environment secrets can reach the sandboxed agent because the child does not get a cleared/allowlisted environment; (2) certain chosen target or output layouts can leave protected areas writable, and the probe does not traverse every writable descendant so such a profile can look safe; (3) when the target IS the project root, canonical tooling trees remain writable, so a later iteration can run altered tooling; (4) the recorded security marker can be replaced or deleted by the agent before publication because the authoritative copy lives in a directory the agent can write. ACTION: revision 3 scoped to net those six decisively with adversarial tests (environment canary, nested protected-tree overlaps, canonical-tool writes, marker tampering), gate once, then re-review. COORD CAP RECORDED: this is the last design round on the sandbox approach — if it does not converge, coord will re-scope to the minimal design (require operator-supplied isolation and keep the tripwire) rather than continue to hand-roll isolation, because two rounds of real holes in a hand-rolled sandbox is a signal about the approach, not just the code. comments.text:
REVISION 3: all six review findings fixed in 3af1230, gate 'arp-r3' running (tip sha in its log). Each fix ships with the test that would have caught it, verified standalone first (21 adversarial checks green on top of the mount-contract, provider-seam, publish and tripwire suites).
- inherited secrets: the launcher now starts from an empty environment on both paths and passes only its allowlisted variables; the probe and a test both plant a canary variable in the parent environment and assert it is ABSENT in the child.
- protected-tree overlap: the resolved target, out and every operator-allowed writable root are validated BEFORE any mount is built and refused when they equal or sit inside a protected tree, with one permitted shape (a genuine run leaf under reports/). Previously a nested target could leave hooks or dependencies writable.
- project-root target: the canonical tooling trees are now re-bound read-only AFTER the writable target bind, so the executable a later iteration runs cannot be swapped; asserted at the syscall level.
- forgeable marker: the authoritative isolation record now lives beside --out, outside anything the agent can write; a copy inside --out is compared to it after the run, restored from it, and any divergence recorded; a missing authority refuses publication.
- --allow-write under isolation: operator-declared roots are now real writable mounts (created if absent) and validated like any other, instead of an option the sandbox silently denied.
- hard links: the limit is stated in the module documentation and the target is scanned with a bounded warning; the write-scope note no longer implies a rooted child cwd is an enforcement boundary (it scopes relative writes only - the OS sandbox is the boundary).

comments.text:
REVISION 3 RE-REVIEW: FAIL — and COORD DECISION TO PIVOT (2026-10-06T02:45Z). Impact-level record; mechanism in the lane brief per the disclosure rule. THREE MORE P1s, all PATH-TOPOLOGY holes rather than missing assertions: (1) for a supported layout the authoritative security record's sibling path can land inside a writable mount, so the isolation attestation is forgeable and publication would republish the forged authority; (2) protected trees are protected only immediately beneath the target, so a nested dependency directory or a nested git directory below the target stays writable and is absent from the probe, which is the same later-execution/persistence vector the profile claims to close; (3) when the target is an ancestor of the project, the code warns rather than refuses, so the project's own git hardening can be defeated by a profile that still passes the probe. Plus two P2s (marker verification runs after publication, and the fallback provider's environment canary cannot pass as written). Correctness fixes from the previous round ARE confirmed: the environment is cleared with a canary, the documented default output location is accepted while a pointer-holding one is refused, bind order places tooling read-only after the writable target, the extra-write option is a real mount, and the cwd-is-not-a-boundary statement is corrected.
DECISION: PIVOT TO THE MINIMAL DESIGN, which the author had already committed to and the reviewer recommended in those words. Three rounds found NINE genuine holes, and the last five are holes in the model itself, so another localized bind or marker patch would be treating the symptom. The minimal design: DELETE the hand-rolled sandbox entirely; REQUIRE an explicit operator assertion naming the isolation the operator supplies, failing closed before any agent spawn when it is absent; PROCEED with the assertion but print a loud warning and record an explicit unverified marker plus the named mechanism; DOCUMENT a copy-pasteable example of running the fixer inside the operator's own sandbox rather than shipping enforcement; KEEP the write-scope tripwire as defence in depth with its documented gaps and the publication-pointer fix; and STATE the residual plainly (operator-asserted, unverified, with a tripwire) instead of implying enforcement. Tests keep the refusal-before-spawn, the recorded declaration, the tripwire suite and a positive end-to-end fix, and the mount-contract/syscall tests that only exercised the deleted profile are removed rather than left asserting a mechanism that no longer exists. Expected effect: the change gets substantially SMALLER than the current revision. Product-direction note going to the hub because fix mode's precondition changes. Status IN_REVIEW; merge-queue label stays off.

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] Headless agent allowlist grants arbitrary node/npx execution while ingesting untrusted page content
description:
## What
The Claude entry in the headless agent runner allowlists `Bash(node:*)` and `Bash(npx:*)`. Both patterns match arbitrary trailing arguments, so they permit `node -e '<code>'` and `npx -y <any-package>` on the host — not just the evidence primitive and the guidance feed the comment says they are for.

## Evidence (verified in code at origin/master 21a3a53)
- `runner/agents.mjs:35-39`:
  ```js
  // Scoped permissions instead of a blanket bypass. Bash(node:*) lets the
  // agent run the evidence primitives (node evidence/cli.mjs ...); npx lets
  // it query the Modern Web Guidance feed and run Lighthouse if it chooses.
  '--allowedTools',
  'Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Bash(node:*),Bash(npx:*),Bash(mkdir:*),Bash(ffmpeg:*)',
  ```
- The runner's purpose is to audit untrusted pages (`runner/run-batch.mjs` spawns the CLI and feeds the model the URL plus page-derived evidence), so page text is an untrusted input to the same process that holds these permissions.

## Why it is real
The threat model treats this as an open invariant, not a design decision:
- section 6, I4: "Untrusted page content must not steer the agent beyond the skill's intended actions; the headless path must treat all evidence text as data, never as instructions, and must run under a sandbox/container (F-001)."
- section 5, HS6 asks that each relaxation be "scoped, restored, and documented as requiring a disposable container".
- section 7 excludes blanket auto-approval flags (`--yolo`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-all-tools`) as by design *when gated on container isolation*. This finding is narrower and independent of that: even with container isolation, the allowlist is broader than the documented intent, and nothing in the runner enforces the container.

## Calibrated severity
P3. Station input, stated accurately: `high` from threat-model, vuln-verify and vuln-triage; `medium` from vuln-discovery. I hold P3 rather than P1 because it is conditional twice over (a successful prompt injection *and* a non-container run), while the fix is a one-line allowlist tightening with no behavioural loss for the intended workflow, so the cheap fix dominates. A reviewer is free to argue it up to P1 on the raw station severity. (An earlier revision of this bead said "station severity: medium", which misstated the input; corrected.)

## Station citation
Factory audit run 2026-10-06T00:22Z (target `/home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-factory` @4cccc60), rules `TM-001-prompt-injection-agent-rce` / `headless-prompt-injection-surface` / `vuln-triage/prompt-injection-auto-approved-shell`; reports under `/home/exedev/agents/runs/*-web-uplift-factory-20261006-00*/report.json`.

## Bounded next step
Tighten the allowlist to the exact needed forms, e.g. `Bash(node evidence/cli.mjs:*)` and a pinned `Bash(npx -y modern-web-guidance@0.0.172:*)`; drop blanket `Bash(npx:*)` and `Bash(node:*)`. Keep the container requirement documented, and make the skill text treat page evidence as data. The separate write-confinement gap for fix mode is `web-uplift-arp`.

title: [flake] CDP browser launch/endpoint is unreliable under host CPU starvation (DevTools endpoint timeout, socket hang up)
description: SEPARATE ROOT CAUSE FROM web-uplift-7kl (console --interact capture yielding 0 entries). This is the LAYER BELOW it: obtaining a Chrome DevTools session at all. Four observations on web-uplift (2 vCPU) tonight, all at ~84% host CPU STEAL (84.9% measured /proc/stat window; hub swept 75-87% on eight of nine VMs): (1) ~04:2xZ net-bodies isolation attempt: 'Error: Timed out waiting for Chrome DevTools endpoint' at evidence/cdp.mjs:254; (2) 05:26Z mw-invoker npm test gate run 2: 'Error: create CDP target (5 attempts): socket hang up' ECONNRESET from evidence/cdp.mjs:299 via newSession, at tests/regression.mjs:1638 testThrottlingConditions — AFTER the existing 5-attempt retry budget, so that budget is insufficient under starvation; (3) 05:30Z net-bodies gate2 launch-loop with CHROME_BIN and CHROME_PATH unset: same DevTools endpoint timeout at evidence/cdp.mjs:301, while the SAME run discovery proof PASSED rc=0 resolving the CfT binary, so resolution was fine and the handshake is what timed out; (4) the same launch-loop then passed 3/3 on a quieter slot with both env vars unset. NOT A CONTENT FAILURE: the failing call sites differ (testThrottlingConditions, isolation check, launch-loop) and the failure is always at launch/endpoint handshake, never at a page-behaviour assertion — different tests failing at the same LAYER under the same load is the environment signature, whereas a repo bug would be one test failing at one point regardless of load. WHY IT MATTERS: every land is gated by npm test, whose browser tests must launch Chrome; a launch-layer flake fails a whole gate after it has queued for the single heavy slot (20-40 min under steal) and looks identical at a glance to a content failure — which is how a real regression could be waved through as 'the flake', or vice versa. SUGGESTED FIX (launch layer only, never weakening a page assertion): treat browser startup as a first-class retryable step — longer/backed-off DevTools endpoint wait, retry with jitter on ECONNRESET/socket hang up, and make the error state the measured load/steal so a lane can distinguish environment from content at a glance. FLEET CONTEXT: filed because the coordinator was asked to escalate when this became a pattern rather than a single occurrence; four observations across two lanes and three call sites is that pattern, and the fleet-level statement is the harness load-sensitivity on a starved 2-vCPU host, not a defect in the changed content. Observed 2026-10-05 ~04:20-05:55Z.

comments.author: web-uplift-coord
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT: THE 20 s ENDPOINT WAIT IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT — the failures are LAUNCH failures, not slow launches. This corrects the hypothesis the bead was filed under, so it changes the fix.

METHOD (conservative by construction): 8 launches using the EXACT flags cdp.mjs uses (--headless=new, --remote-debugging-port=0, --no-sandbox, private --user-data-dir, --no-first-run, --no-default-browser-check, --disable-gpu, --disable-dev-shm-usage, --hide-scrollbars=false), waiting for the same stderr line cdp.mjs matches ("DevTools listening on ws://<host>:<port>/"), with a 40 s outer cap so any case the 20 s constant would have killed is visible. Run on a QUIET heavy slot (queued behind net-bodies' gate4 through fleet-heavy, acquired after 1205 s) so the number is the BEST CASE for the starved box rather than the worst.

RESULT: 8/8 READY. min 979 ms, median 1397 ms, p90 2003 ms, max 2003 ms. ZERO of 8 would have exceeded the 20000 ms constant. Host CPU steal at the time was ~83.6% (since-boot /proc/stat), i.e. the box was just as starved as during the failures.

IMPLICATION, and it is the important part: a normal Chrome launch on this box takes one to two seconds, so 20 s is roughly 10-20x the observed launch time. When the constant fires, Chrome has therefore NOT been slow — it never printed the DevTools line at all, which is a startup failure or wedge (crashed/hung browser, unusable profile dir, a stale resource, or a lost race), not a timeout that a bigger number would have survived. Raising 20000 to 45000-60000 would very likely turn a fast failure into a slower one rather than fixing anything.

REVISED FIX FOR THIS BEAD (and it is cheaper than the original): (1) make the LAUNCH retryable as a unit — a fresh attempt with a FRESH --user-data-dir and a bounded backoff — which the measurement shows is cheap (1-2 s per attempt) and which addresses a wedge or a lost race rather than a slow start; (2) keep the per-attempt wait near 20 s, since it is not the binding constraint, and state in the code comment that the number comes from a measured median of ~1.4 s and a max of ~2.0 s; (3) make the failure DIAGNOSTIC: on timeout, say whether the browser process is still alive, whether it exited and with what code, whether its stderr carried any error line, and whether the profile dir was fresh — because "still alive but silent" (wedge) and "exited early" (crash) are different faults with different fixes; (4) the second defect recorded above still stands independently: the timeout path leaks the profile dir, and it matters MORE now that retries are the fix, because a wedged launch leaves residue that the next attempt may inherit.
CAVEAT, stated so nobody over-reads this: the measurement did NOT reproduce a failure (8/8 ready), so the failure mode itself is still uncharacterised at the level of "which of wedge/crash/stale-state it is" — which is exactly why (3) is on the list. What it does establish is the NEGATIVE: slowness is not the explanation, so a longer timeout is not the fix.

title: [factory-audit/perf-review] network --bodies fetches response bodies serially; parallelise with Promise.all
description:
## What

When the `network` evidence primitive is run with `--bodies`, response bodies are fetched with one serial await per recorded request, turning N independent CDP round trips into a sequential waterfall that adds wall-clock latency (counted against the capture window) for no ordering benefit.

## Evidence (verified in code)

evidence/cli.mjs lines 1003-1014: `if (opts.bodies) { for (const rec of records) { if (!rec.response || rec.failed || rec.redirectedTo) continue; try { const body = await client.Network.getResponseBody({ requestId: rec.requestId }); rec.body = body; } catch { ... } } }`. Each call is independent (keyed by requestId) and chrome-remote-interface multiplexes concurrent requests over the single CDP socket, so the serial await is the only thing forcing sequence. The same loop exists in the generated vendored copy at .web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs:1009.

## Why it is real

Verified at target sha 0c0c7e8 in /home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-factory. On a request-heavy page with --bodies, elapsed time scales linearly with the retrievable-body count instead of with the slowest single round trip. Redirects, failed, and data responses are already skipped, so the work set is purely retrievable bodies.

## Priority mapping

Station severity medium mapped to P3 per critical-P0, high-P1, medium-P3, low-P4.

## Station citation

perf-review station report: /home/exedev/agents/runs/perf-review-web-uplift-factory-20261005-031317/report.json, rule sequential-await-waterfall. Factory audit run 2026-10-05T03:07Z-03:15Z, target sha 0c0c7e86fe56477dee07fefbc4d64bee1c70a623.

## Bounded next step

Replace the for loop with a filter plus a single `await Promise.all(records.filter(...).map(async (rec) => {...}))`, keeping the per-record try/catch and the in-place `rec.body` assignment so HAR assembly is unchanged; apply the same fix to the canonical file, then refresh the vendored .web-uplift copy via install --agent all and run npm test.

title: [factory-audit/modern-web] Scorecard finding dialogs opened imperatively via JS showModal(); use Invoker Commands (commandfor/command=show-modal)
description:
## What

The generated HTML scorecard opens its finding dialogs imperatively with a JS helper and hand-rolled button semantics instead of Invoker Commands.

## Evidence (verified in code)

- aggregate/scorecard.mjs line 728: `function openFor(el){var id=el.getAttribute('data-open');if(!id)return;var d=document.getElementById(id);if(d&&d.showModal){d.showModal();}}`
- Lines 729-732: the same helper is wired to click plus a manual keydown Enter/Space handler (`if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '){e.preventDefault();openFor(el);}`) because the openers are not real buttons.
- Line 368: openers are emitted as `<li class="fitem ..." data-open="fd-..." role="button" tabindex="0">`, i.e. non-semantic elements faking buttons.

## Why it is real

The dialog is already a native `<dialog>`; only the open path is imperative JS plus a fake-button li with a hand-rolled keyboard handler. Invoker Commands (`commandfor` / `command="show-modal"`, Baseline Newly available 2025) handle click, Enter/Space, and focus semantics natively, letting openFor() and both listeners be deleted. Verified at target sha 0c0c7e8 in /home/exedev/worktrees/web-uplift-factory.

## Priority mapping

Station severity medium mapped to P3 per critical-P0, high-P1, medium-P3, low-P4.

## Station citation

modern-web station report: /home/exedev/agents/runs/modern-web-web-uplift-factory-20261005-031201/report.json, rule declarative-dialog-popover-control, guide ids declarative-dialog-popover-control / custom-button-actions. Factory audit run 2026-10-05T03:07Z-03:15Z, target sha 0c0c7e86fe56477dee07fefbc4d64bee1c70a623.

## Bounded next step

Emit each opener as a real `<button type="button" commandfor="fd-<id>" command="show-modal">`, delete openFor() and its click/keydown listeners, keep a showModal() fallback behind a feature check (HTMLButtonElement.prototype.commandForElement), then regenerate the vendored .web-uplift copy via install --agent all and run npm test.

title: No guard enforces that evidence/ and .web-uplift/evidence/ stay byte-identical (vendored-copy drift risk)
description:
Answering coord's prep question on aoo.2.1: is there any mechanism enforcing the two cdp.mjs copies stay in sync? NO.

EVIDENCE
- master 89b746b: `cmp evidence/cdp.mjs .web-uplift/evidence/cdp.mjs` -> IDENTICAL (no drift today).
- aoo.2.1 branch da48f61: both copies are also identical (sha256 b7690b3c102d51ec678b43a47635f943204d4a2b0d73f0985a8c6d78945fded8 for both), so that branch does NOT introduce drift.
- Sync exists only as a manual command: bin/web-uplift.mjs:233 copies the whole evidence/ dir into .web-uplift/evidence/ on `install --agent all`. Coord has ruled that regen OUT of scope for landing (needs Paul's npm credentials question), so nothing re-syncs the vendored tree automatically.
- tests/regression.mjs testInstalledEvidenceCli installs into a tmp target from PKG_ROOT and runs `.web-uplift/evidence/cli.mjs --help`; it asserts the INSTALLED copy loads, never that the repo's vendored copy matches its source. Nothing in tests/ compares any two repo paths byte-wise.
- .web-uplift/manifest.json stores no file hashes (package, version, installedAt, agents, updateCommand only).
- .github/workflows/audit-playground.yml triggers on evidence/** but has no install + `git diff --exit-code` step.

CONSEQUENCE
A change to evidence/*.mjs that forgets the vendored copy (or vice versa) passes npm test and CI. Anything consuming the vendored CLI keeps the old behaviour silently. The only current defence is a reviewer eyeballing the diff, which is exactly what coord asked me to do for aoo.2.1.

SUGGESTED GUARD (not prescriptive)
A regression assertion that hashes the vendored tree (evidence/, aggregate/, runner/, knowledge/, schema/ and the skill copies) and compares it to its source, so drift fails npm test. Do not fix inline.

FOUND BY: web-uplift-merger during aoo.2.1 landing prep, 2026-10-04.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — branch uplift/1as-unaccounted-coverage @ 96864fe (1 commit, off origin/master 2afb1e5, 0 behind, pushed).

What it does: compareReports now carries each side's coverage verdict and reasons (before.coverage / after.coverage, so compare.json has them too), and renderCompareMd prints a Coverage line whenever a side is incomplete without a blocked/not-run row to count. Before, web-uplift-cpm made such a report complete: false but its displayed unconcluded count was still 0, so compare.md said:

  - **Unconcluded checks (blocked/not-run):** 0 -> 0 (0)

for a report that concluded nothing. Now the same comparison renders:

  - **Unconcluded checks (blocked/not-run):** 0 -> 0 (0)
  - **Coverage:** before incomplete: coverage.complete is true but the report records no checks; after incomplete: ...

The general form covers every incompleteness that has no row to count (unaccounted, or coverage.complete simply not true), not just the cpm case. A genuinely complete pair renders no Coverage line, a partial run whose incompleteness is already visible in the unconcluded count is unchanged, and the added fields are additive so compare.json consumers keep working (the only readers of the touched fields are compare.mjs itself and its test).

Evidence:
- red first: a scratch scenario printed the misleading 0 -> 0 line with no Coverage line, and the extended compare test failed on the same scenario.
- green: npm test passes; the Coverage line renders with the named reason; the clean pair stays silent.
- .web-uplift/aggregate/compare.mjs re-synced so the tracked installed copy is byte-identical.

title: i18n checks cannot be judged: no locale or timezone emulation
description:
The three be-internationalised checks (lang-dir-and-logical-properties,
locale-aware-data, time-zone-correctness) can only be judged by reading
source today. Emulation.setLocaleOverride and
Emulation.setTimezoneOverride are never used, so the audit cannot observe
what the page actually renders for a different locale or time zone.

Source reading cannot answer the question the checks ask. A page can call
Intl.DateTimeFormat correctly and still hard-code a calendar assumption, or
pass a naive Date through a formatter and produce the wrong day either side
of a DST boundary. Only rendering under a second locale and a second time
zone shows it.

Fix: accept --locale and --timezone options in applyConditions, and have the
screenshot and evaluate primitives record the conditions they ran under. The
model can then diff the rendered dates and numbers across two conditions.

These checks are contextual, so this is legitimately lower priority than the
default-expectation gaps, but without it the honest outcome is not-run
rather than not-applicable, and a not-run makes the whole run partial.

title: add a11ytree primitive: computed accessibility tree and focus-order walk
description:
be-inclusive/names-roles-labels and structure-and-focus are judged from DOM
attributes and, when it can be loaded, axe. Accessibility.getFullAXTree is
never called (grep count 0), so the audit never sees what assistive
technology actually receives: computed accessible names, roles, the ignored
subtree, and the real reading order after aria and CSS have had their say.

DOM attribute inspection and the computed a11y tree disagree in exactly the
cases that matter: an aria-label overridden by aria-labelledby, a control
whose name comes from a title attribute, a landmark hidden by
aria-hidden on an ancestor, a heading removed from the tree by display
contents.

Fix: add an `a11ytree` primitive returning the computed tree with
name/role/ignored per node, plus a focus-order walk that tabs through the
page and records activeElement with its computed outline at each stop.

Lower priority than the axe primitive: axe covers more ground per unit of
work, and this is the deeper follow-up for the cases axe reports as
"incomplete".
close_reason: Landed to master at 3017511 after independent review PASS by uplift-gemini

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — branch uplift/5lp-a11ytree-primitive @ 20ef0b0 (rebased onto origin/master 121bc4b, which carries the features primitive; pushed after resolving the rebase against it).

What landed: `a11ytree` primitive in evidence/cli.mjs (+ README row, vendored copy re-synced).
- tree: Accessibility.getFullAXTree projected to role, computed name, description, ignored (+ ignoredReasons), the flag properties the checks turn on (focusable/focused/level/checked/expanded/...), childCount and depth, nested in reading order; capped at 400 projected nodes with totalNodes/nodesProjected/truncated reported, plus maxDepth, ignoredCount and a role histogram over non-ignored nodes.
- focusOrder: the REAL tab order. Tab is dispatched with CDP key events (Input.dispatchKeyEvent) and each stop records tag/id/class/name/role/tabindex, rect and on-screen state, computed outline and box-shadow with a mechanical hasVisibleIndicator reading, and whether it sits inside an aria-hidden subtree. The walk stops when the tab cycle wraps or at 60 stops, and reports cycleDetected/truncated/maxStops, stopsWithoutVisibleIndicator and stopsInsideAriaHidden.

Two findings from building it, both now encoded:
1. aria-hidden removes an element from the accessibility tree but NOT from the keyboard tab order. My fixture's button inside aria-hidden="true" is absent from the AX tree as an accessible button yet IS reached by Tab - so the primitive records insideAriaHidden per stop and counts it (stopsInsideAriaHidden). That mismatch is exactly the class of thing a DOM-attribute probe cannot see.
2. A name only comes from title when the element has no content-derived name: <button title="X">icon</button> computes as "icon", while an EMPTY <button title="X"></button> computes as "X". The test fixture uses the empty form to prove the title path, and the content form to prove that content wins.

Verified: npm test green (~51s). The new test drives a real fixture: the tree answers role/name questions DOM attributes cannot (aria-labelledby overriding aria-label, name from title, the aria-hidden button missing from the accessible tree), and the walk reproduces real tab semantics (DOM order, tabindex=-1 skipped, the aria-hidden button reached but flagged, outline:none read as no indicator against a 3px outline read as visible, cycle wrap detected).

Reviewer: different model family from deepseek-flash please; re-run npm test. Worth checking: the caps, and whether the projected property whitelist misses anything the checks need.

title: [factory-audit/threat-model] safeFetch DNS rebinding TOCTOU window
description: safeFetch validates the resolved address but global fetch re-resolves at connect, leaving a DNS rebinding window. Remediation: Pin the validated address or disable target-origin exemption for private addresses.
notes:
Fixed DNS rebinding TOCTOU window by introducing `pinnedFetch`, a wrapper around `http.request` and `https.request` that respects the validated IP address obtained in `assertPageDerivedFetchAllowed`.

- Branch: fleet/16e
- Tip SHA: `29dce99f69d40a126f2ab46227e9b80aab1e4ab6`
- Merge-base: `49fdb4848d44dda6dee9b2dbd681a999abb5352b`

- Falsifiable test evidence: Added `testSafeFetchDnsRebindingGuard` in `tests/regression.mjs` which mocks `dns.lookup` to return a public IP for `assertPageDerivedFetchAllowed` but then resolves to `127.0.0.1` at fetch time. Before the fix, the mocked fetch correctly hit the private address and failed the test. With the fix, the mocked fetch uses the explicitly pinned '8.8.8.8' address, resulting in a timeout rather than hitting `127.0.0.1`.
- Residual risks: `pinnedFetch` uses standard `http/https` node agents rather than Undici, avoiding automatic proxy logic and keeping streams basic, mirroring exactly what `safeFetch` requires. The HTTPS TLS SNI connects perfectly using the underlying custom `lookup`.

title: [test] Reap the 4wx attribution-test browser on the RED path so a mutation run cannot leak an orphaned chrome
description:

title: Demonstrate the tracing-complete bound firing with a stub client, and state the narrowed residual
description:
Filed by coord from the widening bead's own artifact rather than invented: that bead's sweep answered the question "is any raw unbounded await left on the attach/navigation path?" with ONE ENUMERATED EXCEPTION, stated honestly next to the deadline helper — a POST-NAVIGATION tracing-complete await that the sweep places out of scope. The claim is therefore not false, because the exception is written down; this bead exists so that the exception is RESOLVED rather than left as a permanent footnote.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, before deciding what to do: CAN A STARVED HOST HANG THIS AWAIT? If it can, the residual is the same defect class as the bead that enumerated it — an unbounded wait that makes the tool depend on a host that is not answering — and it should either be bounded or explicitly accepted with a reason tied to reachability. If it CANNOT, say why (its own abort path, a bounded wait inside the tracing stop, unreachability in the primitives that use it), because "out of scope" without a reason is the shape of a footnote that later becomes wrong.

ACCEPTANCE, one of two, and say which: (a) the await is bounded through the SAME shared deadline helper the widening bead introduced, with the CLI flag applying where it should and a reproduction that a never-responding server makes it fire rather than hang, plus a healthy control; or (b) it is not boundable or not reachable, and the artifact states WHICH with the evidence, so the exception becomes an explained boundary instead of an open item. Option (b) is a real outcome, not a failure — a documented unreachable residual is a better artifact than an unnecessary guard — but it needs the reason written where the next reader meets the exception.
SEQUENCING: the widening bead is IN_REVIEW on this same file, so investigate read-only now and make no edit to the evidence CLI until that bead has LANDED; coord will confirm the landing. Then branch from the landed master, not from the earlier branch.

Mechanism, verified in chrome-remote-interface source (lib/api.js addEvent, lib/chrome.js _handleConnectionClose):
1. evidence/cli.mjs trace(): 'const done = new Promise((resolve) => client.Tracing.tracingComplete(resolve)); await client.Tracing.end(); await done;'. The 'done' promise fulfils ONLY when Chrome fires the Tracing.tracingComplete event. CRI's event registration is 'chrome.once(rawEventName, fulfill)' — there is NO reject path at all.
2. CRI's _handleConnectionClose rejects pending COMMAND callbacks ('WebSocket connection closed') but does NOT settle event waiters. So on a starved-but-alive Chrome the event never arrives and 'await done' hangs unbounded; even on a hard disconnect the event waiter is never released — it does not become an actionable error.
3. The adjacent 'await client.Tracing.end()' command is also unbounded under live-connection starvation (it would reject only on disconnect).
4. Reachability: trace is a first-class primitive (CLI help line 31, PRIMITIVES map); the await runs on every trace invocation after load + --wait.

Repro nuance for acceptance (a): tracingComplete is fired by the BROWSER, not the page, so a never-responding server does not stall it (that stalls the load wait, which 17o already bounds). The faithful starvation repro is a never-responding BROWSER: SIGSTOP the Chrome process during a trace run, show the bounded path fires with the actionable deadline error instead of hanging, plus a healthy control where a normal trace completes inside the bound.

PLAN once 17o lands (coord to confirm): branch fleet/net-bodies from landed master, wrap the Tracing.end command + tracing-complete event wait in the SAME withDeadline helper (nav/call deadline so --cdp-deadline / WEB_UPLIFT_CDP_DEADLINE_MS applies), add the SIGSTOP repro + healthy control to tests/regression.mjs, update the ENUMERATED EXCEPTION comment in cdp.mjs to record the resolution. description: Filed by web-uplift-merger after a RED gate attempt on an unrelated branch, so the timing sensitivity is tracked instead of being silently re-run. Suggested direction, not a prescription: the assertion depends on a live registration in Chrome with no bounded wait for it, so under contention it can observe the pre-registration state. Owner suggestion: the lane that owns the resilience primitive. Do not treat a single red of this assertion on an untouched region as evidence against the change under review.
close_reason: MERGED 7a1e144 (Merge fleet/5jd), tree 32b38e4a holds; fleet-check PASS exit 0/243s whose verdict tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the landing commit tree; independent cross-family review PASS with merge verdict OK on 4a0df1f, all nine checks clean. The fixture no longer writes into the checkout, and the report emits an explicit note when the budget exhausts so the tool distinguishes observing nothing from knowing nothing exists — the residual 2s budget is stated rather than the report implying absence. DECISION 2 — FOLD THE "NOT OBSERVED WITHIN THE BUDGET" DISTINCTION INTO THIS BEAD NOW, BEFORE GATING. title: Pointer containment: add the symlink positive control and assert a fresh-install execution
description:
Filed by coord from the two findings in the final review of the pointer-containment bead, both of which the reviewer classified as TEST-COVERAGE gaps rather than code defects, so the bead landed and these are tracked rather than fixed in place.

(1) THE SYMLINK FORM HAS NO POSITIVE CONTROL. The text-file pointer form has one — a legitimate pointer is asserted to resolve — but the symlink form is only exercised for the negative escape and fallback case. The behaviour is real in production, so this is coverage rather than correctness, but a negative-only test cannot distinguish "the containment works" from "the symlink branch never resolves anything". Add a legitimate symlink pointer and assert it resolves.

(2) THE FRESH-INSTALL CLAIM IS VERIFIED BUT NOT ASSERTED. The change introduced a CROSS-DIRECTORY import from the runner directory into the containment module, which is exactly the packaging shape that caused a real defect earlier: the repository works while an installed copy does not. The author checked it in the repository, in the vendored tree and in a fresh install, and the packaged file list includes both directories — so the claim is true. But NO TEST natively executes those modules from a fresh install; the existing install test asserts the VENDORED tree, which is a different artifact. Add an assertion that runs the affected module from a freshly installed package, so the claim cannot rot the next time a file moves between directories.

WHY THESE ARE WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE: both are the same class the fleet fixed repeatedly tonight — a claim that is true today but has nothing keeping it true tomorrow. The symlink control protects a branch from silently becoming a no-op, and the fresh-install assertion protects a packaging claim from decaying the next time modules move, which this repo has now done twice.

title: A planted run pointer can steer a published scorecard at a directory outside the run tree
description: IMPACT: the tool keeps a pointer to a host's newest run, and a consumer reads that pointer as a directory to load the run's report from. A pointer planted inside the reports tree - a tree the audited agent can write, which is the documented reason operator isolation is the boundary - can name a directory outside that tree, so the report a scorecard reads and renders is chosen by whatever wrote the pointer rather than by the tool. WHAT A BAD ACTOR COULD ACHIEVE: steer a published or retained scorecard at JSON outside the run tree, so the numbers a reader sees come from a file the tool never produced, and a run the tool did publish can be hidden from the summary. FIX DIRECTION: validate the pointer target as a direct child of the host's run root before use - the same shape as the containment already applied to the scorecard's comparison identifiers - and state the residual where the pointer is read, since the batch consumer documents it and this consumer does not.

The two findings were TEST-COVERAGE rather than code and are tracked as web-uplift-uz9 (the symlink form lacked a positive control, and the fresh-install claim was verified but not asserted) — authority-only public text throughout. title: Batch-audit guard: two cosmetic follow-ups from the wy6 final review
description:
Filed by coord from the FINAL review of web-uplift-wy6 (verdict PASS-WITH-NITS, and the reviewer stated it found NO material crash or data-loss defect). These are the two remaining cosmetic findings, accepted under the cap and tracked here so they survive as work rather than as a note in a comment stream. Fold both in the next time the batch runner or its tests are touched; neither is worth a revision of its own.

(1) COMPLETION COMMENTS REMAIN TOO BROAD. Two comments say completion WITHIN A BATCH is decided by the in-memory set. That is true for a URL already in the set, but for a URL not yet in it, the resume lookup for that same process reads the DISK POINTER, so the accurate wording is narrower: URLs this process successfully published take precedence from the set; other resume lookups use the disk pointer. Also the disk-pointer residual is currently repeated in the refusal comment, the quarantine comment and the completion comment — the reviewer notes it should be stated ONCE, in the completion check, so it reads as a deliberate residual rather than three separate hedges.

(2) THE NEW DUPLICATE-URL REGRESSION DOES NOT PROVE A SECOND ATTEMPT. The assertion counts appearances of the URL and requires two, but ONE attempted URL already appears both in the auditing output and in the failure summary, so the assertion passes even if the duplicate is never attempted. Under that fixture the test should assert the SECOND URL's own failure reason (the could-not-prepare-a-run-directory one) or otherwise distinguish an attempt from a summary line. NOTE the implementation ordering itself is CORRECT — the set is only updated after publication succeeds — so this is a test-strength issue, not a behaviour one.

SEQUENCING: low priority, no dependency, after the current queue (dsj, then 17o). If either is folded in while touching those files, remove it from this bead's scope and say so in a comment.

title: Image-size comment claims a universal containment rule the implementation does not fully apply
description: IMPACT: the comment above the report's image-size reader states that every field read must lie inside the buffer AND inside the range the format declares, while two places read a field slightly before the declared segment is proven complete (a JPEG component count, and a PNG dimension read on a 24-byte buffer whose IHDR is not fully present). Neither can produce a size for a well-formed image and neither can crash, so the effect is that a malformed, non-decodable file could still be given a box on a cosmetic layout fix. WHAT MATTERS HERE: the comment is a claim stronger than the mechanism, which is the same shape as every evidence-fidelity finding closed tonight, so either the two reads should be tightened or the comment should say the parser is best-effort for well-formed images. FIX DIRECTION: soften the comment to describe best-effort parsing, or validate the two reads - one line either way. Recorded by coord from the xq5 rev4 review, deliberately NOT fixed in that revision because its gate was measuring those exact bytes.

THE FIX: the WebP branch read the chunk code and chunk size before verifying that the range the RIFF header declares reaches them, so a container declaring four bytes had both fields read from outside its own declared range — the same defect as an unguarded dimension read, one line earlier; the container end must now be at least 20 bytes before either field is read.
THE ENUMERATION COORD ASKED FOR, and it is the part that settles the rule: every field read in the function listed with the guard that covers it and checked against BOTH bounds — the buffer and the range the format declares. PNG signature, chunk length, chunk type and dimensions under the whole-declared-chunk requirement plus the chunk length asserted to be 13; GIF version and descriptor under the fixed descriptor length; JPEG scan and marker bytes under the index bounds; the segment length field under a bound that also requires the segment to end inside the buffer; the component count under the segment length AND the buffer; the frame dimensions under a length derived from the component count; WebP magic and container size under the buffer; the WEBP magic and chunk header under the buffer AND the new container bound; the chunk size and code under those same two; the chunk extent including its pad byte under both the container end and the buffer; and each variant field under its own minimum plus a containment check against both the chunk end and the buffer. No read is left outside a guard, and the enumeration is in the commit message as well as the report.
COORD ERROR CORRECTED BY THE AUTHOR, recorded because it is instructive: coord asked for a fixture that FAILS on the previous tip. The author ran the committed test against the previous revision AND this one and found BOTH PASS, because the chunk-extent check that follows already rejects such an input — so no input outcome changes and NO fixture can discriminate for this guard. It kept the fixture as a BEHAVIOUR PIN, labelled as a pin rather than as coverage of the guard. That is the same shape as the JPEG half, which the reviewer had already accepted as a correct omission rather than an oversight. THE GENERAL RULE, recorded on the board: when a change makes a mechanism COMPLY with an invariant rather than altering a result, the honest artifact is a labelled pin that states the invariant, not a regression test that cannot fail — and the report must say which one it is. THE ENUMERATION SWEEP, every field read with the guard that covers it, checked against BOTH bounds - the buffer and the range the format declares: PNG signature, chunk length, chunk type and dimensions (buffer >= 33, the whole declared IHDR chunk, plus the declared chunk length asserted to be 13); GIF signature, version and logical screen descriptor (buffer >= 13, the whole fixed descriptor, with no further declared range for these fields); JPEG scan byte and marker byte (i and j within the buffer); JPEG segment length field (j + 4 within the buffer, and the segment must end inside the buffer before any field of it is used); JPEG component count (len >= 8 and j + 8 within the buffer, so it is inside the SEGMENT as well); JPEG frame dimensions (len >= 8 + 3 * components, so the entries the length claims exist); WebP RIFF magic and the container size field itself (buffer >= 30, the size field being the declaration itself); WebP WEBP magic and the chunk header (buffer >= 30 and, new, containerEnd >= 20); WebP chunk size and four-character code (those same two guards); WebP chunk extent with its pad byte (<= containerEnd AND <= the buffer); and each variant's fields (chunkSize >= the shape's minimum, and inside(offset, length) against BOTH chunkEnd and the buffer). No read is left outside a guard, which is what makes the rule in the comment true. The enumeration is in the commit message as well as here.

FIXTURE, and the limit I could not talk myself out of: the malformed container is a fixture now, but it is a BEHAVIOUR PIN and not a regression test for this guard, and that was verified rather than assumed - the committed test passes against 98256e7 (without the guard) AND against this revision, because the chunk-extent check that follows already rejects such an input. No input's outcome changes, so no fixture can discriminate for this fix: the guard makes the read comply with the rule without altering a result. That is the same shape as the JPEG ordering change the reviewer accepted as a correct omission, and the pin is labelled as a pin in the test so nobody later reads it as coverage of the guard. The invariant is worth pinning independently of which guard enforces it.

title: Measure the reserved image box in a real browser (xq5 shipped the structural guarantee only)
description:
Filed by coord from the honest reporting on web-uplift-xq5. That bead fixed a layout shift by emitting intrinsic width/height on the scorecard images and letting the stylesheet derive the height so the ratio drives the box, and it verified that STRUCTURALLY (the attributes carry the sizes parsed from real image headers, and the stylesheet lets the ratio decide). What it could NOT do is MEASURE the reserved box in a browser, and the reason is worth recording because three separate apparatus attempts failed rather than the fix: (1) cloning an image with its source removed gives no aspect ratio in Chrome, so it measured zero; (2) serving the image from a delayed endpoint did not work because the harness waits for the load event and the panel then read as zero geometry; (3) holding the request at the protocol layer and activating the tab as a reader does failed because the before/after section is a tab panel hidden until opened, and a hidden lazy image is never requested at all. So the shipped guarantee is structural and the commit says so rather than implying a measurement.

WHY THIS IS WORTH ONE SMALL BEAD: the repo's standard for a UI change is browser-driven evidence, and a layout-shift fix is precisely the kind of thing where the arithmetic looks right and the frame still moves. The missing piece is a dedicated fixture with a VISIBLE, UNFETCHED image (a local endpoint that holds the response, in a panel that is already open), so the pre-decode state can be measured and the content below asserted not to move when the bitmap arrives.

ACCEPTANCE: a fixture that renders the scorecard with an image whose bytes are deliberately delayed and whose panel is already visible; measure the position of content below the image while the bitmap is genuinely in flight; assert it does not move when the image arrives; and report the numbers both sides (with the fix and with the size attributes removed) so the evidence distinguishes the fix from the apparatus. If the apparatus fails for a new reason, report the reason rather than substituting a structural check.

SEQUENCING: low priority, no dependency; do it after the current queue. If a cheaper faithful apparatus turns out to be impossible in this harness, say so and the residual can be accepted with that reason recorded instead.

This is the BEHAVIOURAL measurement xq5 deliberately did not make, and it measures both shapes in the same run so the apparatus is proven able to see the difference rather than merely agreeing with the fix.

MEASURED, and printed into the gate log by the test itself: an image carrying width and height reserved 250.75px while its bitmap was pending and 250.75px once decoded, with the content below it moving 0.0px. The same image without them reserved 2px while pending - its 1px border, the one part of the box that does not depend on the bitmap - and occupied 112.625px once decoded, moving the content below it by 97.6px. The second half is the point: it shows the measurement can see the difference, which three earlier attempts could not establish. Those were a source-less clone (Chrome gives such an image no aspect ratio), a deliberately slow response (the page's load event waits for it, and the reading came back at zero geometry) and the scorecard's own imagery (a hidden tab panel never requests a lazy image, and a closed dialog never lays one out).

Distinct URLs, because one URL is served from cache for the second image - the first run of this test held only one request - and eager loading, so the pending state comes from the hold rather than from a lazy-loading threshold. The unsized control's pending-height assertion is a tenth of its decoded height rather than zero, because the border is real: a strict zero would have been asserting something false about the box model, and the movement bound is tied to the measured height rather than to a font-dependent constant.

The numbers are logged by the test, so the verdict and the evidence arrive together in the gate log.

title: Verify the vendored-mirror guard's coverage set is complete and cannot drift from what the installer vendors
description:
REFRAMED BY COORD (2026-10-06T04:03Z) — THE ORIGINAL GAP CLAIM WAS FALSE, and this bead is being kept only for the forward-looking hardening. Recorded here so nobody re-derives a non-problem from the old text.

WHAT WAS CLAIMED AND WHY IT WAS WRONG: this bead was filed on a report that the vendored-mirror guard does not cover the aggregate directory, so a stale vendored copy of it could ship unnoticed. The independent review of web-uplift-9li checked the guard directly and found that its directory list DOES include the aggregate pair, and coord reproduced that check independently. So there was NO coverage gap, the guard's green already covered that directory, and the specific claim was mistaken. A SECOND CLAIM FROM THE SAME MESSAGE was also wrong: the author said they had added an assertion to the gate verifying the two aggregate mirrors byte-identical, and that assertion is absent from the submitted diff (verified by coord). The mirrors themselves are identical, so nothing was shipped wrong — the problems were in the REPORTING, not the code.

WHY THE BEAD SURVIVES IN REDUCED FORM: the underlying question is still worth one bounded check, because the value of a guard is that its green means something. The guard compares a FIXED list; the installer vendors a set determined by its own code. Those two are maintained separately, so a FUTURE vended directory could be added without the guard covering it, and the green would then be a false assurance for that part. That is a real (if currently unrealised) drift risk, not a present defect.

ACCEPTANCE, deliberately small: derive the set the installer actually vendors FROM THE INSTALL PATH (not from the guard's list, so the comparison is not circular), diff it against what the guard covers, and either extend the guard or state a reason per gap. Then make the two sets unable to drift silently — ideally by deriving one from the other, or by a check that fails when a vendored directory has no guard entry. Report the two lists explicitly even if they match, because "they match today" is the useful finding.

PRIORITY P4 and no urgency: the current shipped set IS fully covered. Do this when the guard is next touched.

DRAFT ENTRIES (DRAFT - written against the tree at 8d3bcd4, whose file has been deleted; re-verify every claim before reuse):

### Fixed
- **Report images reserve their box before the bitmap arrives.** The report inlines screenshots as data URIs, so the browser has no network hop to learn their size, and the image elements carried no width or height: the stylesheet reserved width only while the placeholder carried an aspect ratio that real images did not, so an image's height was zero until its bitmap decoded and everything below it moved when it did. The size is now read from the image's own bytes - PNG, JPEG, GIF and the three WebP chunk shapes - the markup carries it, and the stylesheet lets that ratio drive the height. A file whose size cannot be read gets no attributes rather than a made-up box, a pair with nothing readable on either side is still dropped, and the placeholder is unchanged. Two residuals are stated in the code: a JPEG whose EXIF orientation rotates it can display with a different ratio from its start-of-frame dimensions, and an image in a format this does not handle is left unreserved - the fail-safe direction, since nothing is invented.
- **A published scorecard cannot be steered into reading outside the reports tree.** The comparison record is untrusted input - it is written by an agent whose context includes the audited page - and its run identifiers were joined into the directory the before/after screenshots are read from, so a crafted identifier chose the BASE that the containment check then validated the screenshot path against. Identifiers are now validated as single-segment directory names resolving to a direct child of the runs root, and a rejected identifier leaves that side of the pair out instead of reading it. A comparison record with no identifiers at all no longer takes the whole scorecard down.
- **The packed package starts.** install-surface.mjs is imported by the CLI, and without it in the package's files list a tarball install died at startup with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. It is now shipped, and the release-step prose names it.

### Changed
- **The installer's vendored surface is declared once.** The set of files and directories install copies was maintained separately from the set the byte-identity guard compares, so a directory could be vended and never compared, or compared while no longer being vended, with nothing able to notice - and the guard's green implied the whole vendored surface was consistent. Both now read one declaration, a test drives a real install and compares what actually appeared against it in both directions, and the declaration records what is deliberately not part of the surface with the reason.

PART 1: DRAFTED CHANGELOG SECTION (for Paul's next release cut)
================================================================================

### Security

- **Strict environment allowlist for agent subprocesses.** Subprocesses spawned by the runner no longer inherit the host process environment. An explicit allowlist passes only essential execution variables (such as PATH, locale, and HOME) along with provider credentials scoped to the targeted model CLI. Sensitive variables withheld from the child process are warned on stderr, and operators can pass specific overrides using the `--agent-env KEY=VALUE` flag. (l6d: a625fee, b293cf6)
- **Provider credential scoping for mapped agents.** By default, mapped agent CLIs receive only their corresponding provider credential family (Claude receives Anthropic keys, Codex receives OpenAI keys, and Gemini receives Google keys); unmapped CLIs receive the broad provider set and operators can pass specific overrides using `--agent-env`. (5ta: 32aab14, c91a3b6)
- **Executable tree integrity verification.** The write-scope tripwire covers key execution roots (`evidence`, `runner`, `fixer`, `aggregate`, `schema`, `knowledge`, `bin`, `install-surface.mjs`, and vendored dependencies in `.web-uplift`). title: Generated scorecard images have no reserved box, so the report shifts while it loads
description:
WHAT: the scorecard emits evidence and before/after images with a percentage width and lazy loading but no intrinsic size, and its stylesheet reserves no aspect ratio for them, so each image box has no height until the bitmap is decoded.

IMPACT: the published scorecard visibly reflows as the images resolve, a layout-shift defect in a report meant to be read and archived. The window is short because the images are inline data URIs, but the shift happens on every render.

IMPACT, plain terms: the report inlines its screenshots, so the browser has no way to know their size before it decodes them, and the image elements did not state it either. The stylesheet reserved width only, while the no-image placeholder carried an aspect ratio that real images did not, so an image's height was zero until its bitmap decoded and everything below it moved when it did - the report shifting under the reader, worst on a first render. WHAT A READER LOSES: the evidence they were reading moves under them, and a screenshot's place in the page cannot be relied on until every bitmap has arrived. Fixed: the size is read from the image's own bytes and the markup reserves the box before the bitmap is there.

VERIFICATION: fleet-gate xq5, bound 2700s, EXIT=0 after 439s. copy-sync rc=0 with 21/21 identical; the vendored aggregate mirrors asserted identical; changelog guard rc=0; npm test exit 0, "tests OK"; CHROME_BIN and CHROME_PATH unset. The test was run as the committed function against both revisions: it fails on the old code and passes here. It checks the sizes through the renderer for a real PNG, JPEG and WebP produced by Chrome's own encoder plus a GIF header; asserts every image whose size can be read carries it and that only the unreadable case does not; that a side with nothing to show still renders the placeholder; that a pair with nothing readable is still dropped; and that the stylesheet lets the ratio drive the height rather than a fixed one.

MEASUREMENT, reported honestly because coord asked for it and it is NOT in the suite: three apparatus attempts to measure the reserved box in a real browser each failed for a reason in the apparatus rather than in the fix. (1) Cloning an image with the src removed: Chrome gives a source-less image no aspect ratio, so it measured 0px, which would have read as a failing fix. (2) Serving the report with one image pointed at a delayed endpoint: the harness's navigate() waits for the load event, and the reading showed the before/after panel at zero geometry. (3) Holding the request at the CDP layer with Fetch and activating the tab the way a reader does: the before/after section is a tab panel hidden until opened, and a hidden lazy image is never requested, so the held request never fired. What remains in the test is the structural guarantee - the size attributes plus a stylesheet that lets the ratio drive the height - and that is what this change can be held to until a fixture exists whose image is visible and not yet fetched. That fixture is small, separate work; I did not fold an unmakeable measurement into the test and call it verification.

comments.text:
REVIEW RESULT: FAIL on 2418d52 (independent review, retry run after an empty-response failure) — ONE P1, ONE P2 and two test gaps; mechanism in the lane brief. PASSED: PNG and GIF offsets and endianness correct; JPEG covers the start-of-frame marker range and advances over ordinary length-prefixed segments; WebP covers all three variants with the right offsets and increment rules; BOTH screenshot emission sites add dimensions when parsed; the stylesheet sets height auto with no competing image-height override; the delta touches exactly the two scorecard mirrors and the test file, with identical mirror hunks; and the renderer test uses real image bytes and would fail on pre-fix markup.

Fix: skip fill bytes before reading the marker; regression with a fixture that actually contains them.
P2, INVENTED DIMENSIONS FOR UNREADABLE DATA: the null-on-unreadable claim is not implemented — PNG is accepted on its signature alone, GIF on a three-letter prefix plus ten bytes, and WebP without validating chunk headers, so a truncated or malformed buffer gets a made-up box (the author's own non-decodable GIF fixture demonstrates it). IN_REVIEW rev2 (web-uplift-net-bodies, 2026-10-06). Branch fleet/xq5, tip 83debe1, pushed. Tip == gated tip: the gate log's base line names 83debe1 and origin/fleet/xq5 is 83debe1. This revision answers the adversarial review of 2418d52 (one P1, one P2, plus test-coverage notes).

P1, JPEG MARKER FILL: any number of 0xFF bytes may pad the space before a marker, and the walk read the byte after the first 0xFF as the marker. It then took a segment length from the following bytes and could step straight over the start-of-frame, so a VALID JPEG returned no size and lost its reserved box - the very case the size reader exists for. The walk now consumes the fill bytes before reading the marker, and skips the stand-alone markers and a stuffed 0xFF00 byte, which carry no length field.
P2, INVENTED DIMENSIONS: the PNG branch accepted a signature with no IHDR, the GIF branch a three-letter prefix above ten bytes, and the WebP branch checked neither the container size nor the chunk's identifying bytes - so a malformed file was given a box computed from bytes that are not dimensions. Every branch now validates the header it depends on and the bounds it reads within, requires a non-zero size, and returns null otherwise, so an unreadable file gets no attributes rather than a made-up box. That is what the commit claimed and now what the code does.

RESIDUALS, stated in the code rather than fixed, both from the review: a JPEG whose EXIF orientation rotates it can display with a different ratio from its start-of-frame dimensions and this reads the start-of-frame only; and an image in a format this does not handle gets no attributes at all, leaving that box unreserved - the fail-safe direction, since nothing is invented and only the movement below it is unbounded.

VERIFICATION: fleet-gate xq5rev2, bound 2700s, EXIT=0 after 318s. copy-sync rc=0 with all 21 vendored copies identical; changelog guard rc=0; npm test exit 0 "tests OK"; CHROME_BIN and CHROME_PATH unset.
